# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask commands` from the command registry. Don't edit it by hand: `cargo xtask check` fails if it differs from what the registry generates. -->

Every action a person or an agent can take in Beatlayer is a command in the registry (`crates/commands`). Menus, shortcuts, key and MIDI mapping, the agent API, and tests all run commands by the IDs below, so an action has one implementation however it's reached (decisions D16 and D17 in [the architecture](02-architecture.md#decisions-log)).

Each command has:

- an **ID** that never changes, which key maps, MIDI maps, agents, and logs use;
- a **label**: what a person sees in menus and key-mapping lists;
- a **description** written for a model: what it does, when to use it, and what it changes;
- a **permission class**, which decides whether an agent asks first;
- **contexts**: the parts of the interface where a person reaches it, as [the UI parity reference](ui-parity/README.md) names them;
- **default keys**: shortcuts from [the UI parity reference](ui-parity/shortcuts.md), by ID, with any arguments they fix. The UI supplies the other arguments from the selection in the shortcut's context, a text field, or a gesture. A command Live has no shortcut for has no default keys;
- **arguments** and a **result** as JSON Schemas generated from the Rust types. An agent sends the arguments as a JSON object. The types they use are under [Types](#types);
- a **readback** for every command that isn't `read`: the read command or query that shows its effect, so an agent can check what it did ([Readback](#readback)).

486 commands in 37 areas.

## Permission classes

| Class | What a command in it may do | An agent |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | Changes nothing in the project or on disk: queries, and moving the keyboard focus or the view. | Runs it |
| `edit` | An undoable change to the project, or a preference that's trivially changed back. | Runs it |
| `destructive` | Removes project content (deleting tracks, clips, or devices), or loses work that undo can't restore: discards unsaved changes, overwrites a file, or quits. An agent asks first even when undo could restore the content. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |
| `external` | Reaches outside the project: files outside the project folder, the network, audio and MIDI devices, or other applications. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |

## Commands

### Area `agent`

#### `agent.approve_client`

**Allow Agent**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Allows the agent called `client` to connect to the agent server, as answering Allow when it first connects does, and makes it its own token. Its approval and its autonomous mode belong to that token, not to its name: a client that connects with the agent's token isn't asked about again, and one that connects with the server's token is asked each time and is never autonomous, whatever name it gives. The approval is kept for the next start. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.forget_client`

**Forget Agent**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Withdraws the approval of the agent called `client`, so the person is asked again the next time it connects. Its sessions end. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.new_client_token`

**New Agent Token**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Replaces the own token of the allowed agent called `client` with a new random one, so a client configured with the old one can no longer speak for that agent until it's given the new one: requests carrying the old one are refused. Use it if the agent's token may have leaked. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.new_token`

**New Token**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Replaces the agent server's token with a new random one, so agents configured with the old token can no longer connect until they're given the new one, which the Settings window shows. Use it if the token may have leaked. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.set_autonomous`

**Autonomous**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches autonomous mode for the allowed agent called `client`. With it on, the agent runs destructive commands (deleting, discarding, overwriting, or placing clips over others) and external ones (files outside the project, devices, other applications) without asking the person first; with it off, as it starts, each one waits for the person's confirmation. It applies only to requests that carry the agent's own token. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether it runs destructive and external commands without asking. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.set_server`

**Agent Server**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches the agent server on or off, or moves it to another port. While it's on, agent clients on this computer reach the agent API over Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`, each request carrying a token as a bearer token: an allowed agent's own token, or the server's token, with which a client is asked about each time it connects. Requests from web pages are refused. Switching it on the first time makes the server's token. The setting is kept for the next start. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Whether the server runs. |
| `port` | integer or null | no | The port to listen on, from 1024 to 65535. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

### Area `arrangement`

#### `arrangement.automation_arm`

**Automation Arm**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches Automation Arm, the Control Bar's button beside Arrangement Record: while it's on and the transport records, moving a control (a track's volume, pan, mute, or send, or a device's parameter) writes its values into that parameter's envelope at the playback position, replacing what was there over the range written, and the envelope resumes where the control is released. The whole recording is one undo step, made when recording stops. Changes only the view until then.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.automation_mode`

**Automation Mode**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches Automation Mode: while it's on, every track shows an automation lane under its lane, with the device and parameter choosers that pick the parameter it shows, and its envelope is drawn and edited there. A (the View menu item and the button above the track headers) does the same. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ENV-001 | `A` | `A` | `arrangement` | Show or hide automation lanes (Automation Mode) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.copy`

**Copy**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Copies clips (`clips`, or the selected clips), or the material in a span of time on tracks, to the Arrangement's clipboard with the tracks they're on, for `arrangement.paste`. Cmd-C (Ctrl-C) runs this on the selection. The clipboard isn't part of the set, and copying changes nothing in it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-002 | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` | `global` | Copy | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ClipboardState`](#clipboardstate).

#### `arrangement.cut`

**Cut**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Copies clips or the material in a span of time to the clipboard, as `arrangement.copy` does, then deletes it, as `arrangement.delete` does. Cmd-X (Ctrl-X) runs this on the selection. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-001 | `Cmd+X` | `Ctrl+X` | `global` | Cut | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.delete`

**Delete**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes clips (`clips`, or the selected clips), or the material in a span of time on tracks (`tracks`, `start`, `end`, or the time selection on the selected tracks): clips inside the span are deleted and clips that cross its edges are shortened or split, leaving the time empty. Nothing after the span moves. Delete runs this on the Arrangement's selection. Undo restores what it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-005 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `global` | Delete | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.duplicate`

**Duplicate**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Places a copy of clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) right after the span they cover, on the same tracks, or a copy of the material in a span of time on tracks right after the span, and selects the copy, so running it again repeats the material. The copy replaces whatever it covers; when that's part of another clip, it's destructive, so an agent asks first. Cmd-D (Ctrl-D) runs this on the Arrangement's selection.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-004 | `Cmd+D` | `Ctrl+D` | `global` | Duplicate | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.fixed_grid`

**Fixed Grid**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches the Arrangement's editing grid between fixed, which keeps its spacing (such as 1/16) at any zoom, and zoom-adaptive, which keeps its lines a set distance apart on screen as the view zooms. Each keeps its own setting. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-GRID-006 | `Cmd+5` | `Ctrl+5` | `global` | Switch between a fixed and a zoom-adaptive grid | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.focus_title_bar`

**Go to Track Title Bar**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects the title bar of the highlighted track (the first selected track, or the top track), as Esc does from a track's controls, so the track-header keys apply. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-034 | `Esc` | `Esc` | `arrangement` | Jump to the highlighted track's title bar | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.fold_groups`

**Show Grouped Tracks**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Shows (`fold` false) or hides (`fold` true) the tracks inside the selected group tracks, as + and - do with a group's title bar selected. Can't run unless a group track is selected. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-008 | `Plus` | `Plus` | `track-headers` | Show the tracks inside a group | fixes `fold` = `false` |
| S-TRACK-009 | `Minus` | `Minus` | `track-headers` | Hide the tracks inside a group | fixes `fold` = `true` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fold` | boolean | yes | Hide the grouped tracks (true) or show them (false). |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.fold_tracks`

**Fold Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `track-headers`.

Folds tracks, so each shows only its title row, or unfolds them to their own height; a folded group track also hides the tracks inside it. Acts on `tracks` or the selected tracks; left without `fold`, it toggles. The fold button beside a track's name does the same, and U toggles the selected tracks. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-010 | `U` | `U` | `track-headers` | Collapse or expand a group track | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fold` | boolean or null | no | Fold (true) or unfold (false). Left out, each track toggles, taking the first track's new state. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.follow`

**Follow**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `sample-editor`.

Switches Follow, the Control Bar's switch: while it's on and the song plays, the Arrangement View turns the page whenever the playhead leaves the view, so the playhead stays in sight. Scrolling sideways by hand, or clicking the beat-time ruler, pauses it until playback starts or stops, or a click lands in the track lanes or the scrub area; `paused` does the same directly. The Sample Editor follows playback on the same switch (Option-Shift-F there too). With no arguments it toggles Follow, which also resumes it. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ZOOM-005 | `Option+Shift+F` | `Alt+Shift+F` | `global` | Scroll the display to follow playback | runs it |
| S-ARR-023 | `Option+Shift+F` | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `arrangement` | Scroll the display to follow playback | runs it |
| S-SAMPLE-005 | `Option+Shift+F` | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `sample-editor` | Scroll the display to follow playback | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch Follow on or off. |
| `paused` | boolean or null | no | Pause following (true), as clicking the beat-time ruler does while the song plays, or resume it (false), as clicking the scrub area does, without switching Follow. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.loop_selection`

**Loop Selection**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the Arrangement's loop brace to span from `start` to `end`, or the time selection (or the selected clips) when they're left out, and switches the loop on, as one undo step, as Cmd-L (Ctrl-L) does. With nothing selected and no span given, it switches the loop on or off instead. Playback that reaches the brace's end then goes on from its start.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-011 | `Cmd+L` | `Ctrl+L` | `arrangement` | Loop the selection, or toggle the Arrangement loop | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where it ends, after `start`. Left out with `start`, the selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the loop brace starts. Left out with `end`, the selection's start. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.move_clips`

**Move Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) in time by `by` ticks, or so that `anchor` starts at `to`, and to other tracks: `anchor` goes to `track` and each other clip keeps its distance from it in the track list. With `copy`, copies go there and the originals stay. A clip placed over another clip on its new track replaces the part it covers: a clip covered entirely is deleted, one covered at an end is shortened, and one covered in the middle is split around it. Audio clips go only to audio tracks and MIDI clips to MIDI tracks, and no clip can start before 1.1.1; if any would, nothing moves. The moved clips (or the copies) are selected afterwards. Dragging a clip's title bar runs this, with Option (Ctrl on Windows) held to copy; the whole drag is one undo step. A move or copy that would replace part of another clip is destructive, so an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip that `to` and `track` place. Left out, the earliest clip (the topmost of those that start together). |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far to move them in time, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `to`, or neither to move them only between tracks. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips. Left out, the selected clips. |
| `copy` | boolean | no | Copy the clips instead, leaving the originals where they are. |
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where `anchor` starts after the move; the other clips keep their distance from it. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track `anchor` moves to; the other clips keep their distance from it in the track list. Left out, every clip stays on its track. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.narrow_grid`

**Narrow Grid**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Makes the Arrangement's editing grid twice as dense: the next narrower adaptive setting, or the next finer fixed spacing. Can't run at the narrowest. The grid decides where the insert marker and selections snap. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-GRID-002 | `Cmd+1` | `Ctrl+1` | `global` | Narrow the grid | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.nudge`

**Nudge**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) one step of the editing grid earlier (`left`) or later (`right`), as Left and Right do in the Arrangement; with no clips selected it moves the insert marker one grid step instead, which changes nothing in the set. A clip can't move before 1.1.1. A clip nudged over part of another replaces it, which is destructive, so an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`Direction`](#direction) | yes | Which way. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips. Left out, the selected clips; with none selected, the insert marker moves instead. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.optimize_height`

**Optimize Height**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches Optimize Height: while it's on, every track shares the lanes' height so all of them are in view, and they keep fitting as tracks come and go. Turning it off gives the tracks back their own heights. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-025 | `H` | `H` | `arrangement` | Fit all tracks to the Arrangement's height | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.optimize_width`

**Optimize Width**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches Optimize Width: while it's on, the whole arrangement, from 1.1.1 to the end of its last clip, fits across the lanes. Turning it off returns to the view before; zooming or scrolling sideways turns it off where the view is. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-026 | `W` | `W` | `arrangement` | Fit the Arrangement to the window's width | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.overview`

**Overview**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Shows or hides the Arrangement View's Overview, the strip above the rulers that shows the whole arrangement with the part in view outlined. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-011 | `Cmd+Option+O` | `Ctrl+Alt+O` | `global` | Show or hide the Arrangement Overview | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

#### `arrangement.paste`

**Paste**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Places the clipboard's material starting at `at` (left out, the time selection's start or the insert marker), its first track's clips on `track` (left out, the first selected track) and its other tracks' clips on the tracks after it, keeping their spacing. The material replaces what it covers (destructive, so an agent asks first, when that's part of another clip) and is selected afterwards. It fails, changing nothing, if a clip would land on a track of another kind or there's nothing on the clipboard. Cmd-V (Ctrl-V) runs this.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-003 | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` | `global` | Paste | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the material starts. Left out, the time selection's start, or the insert marker. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track the clipboard's first track goes to; its other tracks go to the tracks after it, keeping their spacing. Left out, the first selected track, or the track the material was copied from. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.resize_clips`

**Resize Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves the `start` or `end` edge of clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) by `by` ticks, or so that `anchor`'s edge lands at `to`, every clip's edge moving as far. Moving the start edge keeps the clip's contents where they play, so the clip shows more or less of them; it can't go before where the contents begin or before 1.1.1, and a clip can't become shorter than a tick. Lengthening a clip over its neighbour replaces the part it covers. Dragging a clip's edge runs this, and so does Enter, then Left or Right, then Enter, from the keyboard; each is one undo step. Lengthening a clip over another is destructive, so an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-004 | `Enter then Left`, `Right` | `Enter then Left`, `Right` | `arrangement` | Resize a clip from its edge: Enter, then arrows, then Enter (Esc cancels) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edge` | [`Edge`](#edge) | yes | Which edge moves. |
| `anchor` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip whose edge `to` places. Left out, the earliest clip. |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far each clip's edge moves, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `to`. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips. Left out, the selected clips. |
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where `anchor`'s edge goes; the other clips' edges move as far. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.scroll`

**Scroll Arrangement**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Scrolls the Arrangement View by `x` points sideways (positive goes later in the song) and `y` points down the track list, as the scroll wheel, Shift with the wheel, and dragging with Cmd-Option (Ctrl-Alt) held do. It can't scroll before 1.1.1 or past the last track. Scrolling sideways while the song plays pauses Follow. Changes only the view; turns Optimize Width off when it scrolls sideways.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ZOOM-006 | `Shift+scroll` | `Shift+scroll` | `global` | Scroll left or right | runs it |
| S-ZOOM-007 | `Cmd+Option+drag` | `Ctrl+Alt+drag` | `global` | Pan the display around the selection | runs it |
| S-ARR-024 | `Cmd+Option+drag` | `Ctrl+Alt+drag` | `arrangement` | Pan the display around the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | no | How far to scroll sideways, in points: positive moves later in the song. |
| `y` | number | no | How far to scroll the tracks, in points: positive moves down the track list. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.select_clips`

**Select Clips**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects clips in the Arrangement, as clicking a clip's title bar does: `replace` selects only these, `toggle` adds or removes each (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), `add` adds them, and `extend` adds them and every clip between them and the first selected clip (Shift-click). Their tracks become the selected tracks and the time they span the time selection, which Z zooms to. Selecting is never an undo step and changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-010 | `Cmd+click` | `Ctrl+click` | `global` | Add or remove one item from the selection | fixes `mode` = `"toggle"` |
| S-ZOOM-010 | `Cmd+click` | `Ctrl+click` | `global` | Add non-adjacent clips, tracks or scenes to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"toggle"` |
| S-EDIT-011 | `Shift+click` | `Shift+click` | `global` | Select a range from the first to the last clicked item | fixes `mode` = `"extend"` |
| S-ZOOM-009 | `Shift+click` | `Shift+click` | `global` | Add adjacent clips, tracks or scenes to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"extend"` |
| S-ZOOM-008 | `Shift+click`, `Shift+drag` | `Shift+click`, `Shift+drag` | `global` | Add items to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"add"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clips. Empty with `replace` clears the clip selection. |
| `mode` | [`SelectMode`](#selectmode) | no | How to change the selection; `replace` if left out. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

**Set Insert Marker**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Places the Arrangement's insert marker at `at` and, with `track`, selects that track, as clicking in a track's lane does; a click also snaps to the grid when Snap to Grid is on, and resumes Follow. Clears the time selection. Not an undo step; changes only the view.

Sets the height of unfolded tracks (`tracks`, or the selected ones) to `height` points, or changes it by `delta`, from 18 to 800, as dragging a track's lower edge and Option with + or - (Alt on Windows) do. Turns Optimize Height off. Changes only the view.

Picks the parameter `track`'s automation lane shows, as its device chooser (the track mixer, one of its devices, or `null` for None) and parameter chooser do. A track's lane shows its volume until the choosers pick another parameter; with `target` `null` it draws no envelope, while the lane and its choosers stay. Changes only the view.

### Area `assistant`

#### `assistant.forget_key`

**Forget Assistant API Key**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Removes the built-in assistant's API key for its current provider from the OS keychain, so turns are refused until a key is stored again. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.send`

**Send to Assistant**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Sends the person's message to the built-in assistant: it joins the conversation in the panel, and the assistant answers it as one turn, whose changes to the set are one undo step. Refused while a turn is running or when the message is empty. It belongs to the person using the app, so the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The message. |

Result: [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate).

#### `assistant.set_base_url`

**Assistant Base URL**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Sets the base URL the assistant's OpenAI-compatible provider is reached at, such as `http://localhost:11434/v1` for a local Ollama server, or `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` for OpenRouter. Empty uses the provider's own address. The setting is kept for the next start. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | string | yes | The base URL, or empty for the provider's own. |

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.set_key`

**Assistant API Key**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Stores the built-in assistant's API key for its current provider in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service on Linux), replacing any key already there. The key is never written to the preferences or a set, never returned in a result, and never shown again: the Settings window only reports whether one is stored. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The API key. |

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.set_model`

**Assistant Model**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Sets the model the assistant asks its provider for, such as `gpt-4o-mini` for an OpenAI-compatible API or `claude-sonnet-4-5` for Anthropic. The setting is kept for the next start. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | string | yes | The model. |

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.set_panel_width`

**Assistant Panel Width**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the width in points of the assistant's panel while it is docked, as dragging its left edge does. A width outside 240 to 640 points is brought within them. The width is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. It belongs to the person using the app, so the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | number | yes | The width in points. A width outside the limits is brought within them. |

Result: [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate).

#### `assistant.set_provider`

**Assistant Provider**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the model provider the built-in assistant talks to: an OpenAI-compatible API (OpenAI itself, OpenRouter, or a local server such as Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or vLLM), Anthropic's Messages API, or Google's Gemini API. The setting is kept for the next start. Its API key is stored separately, in the OS keychain. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | [`AssistantProvider`](#assistantprovider) | yes | The provider. |

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.stop`

**Stop Assistant**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops the assistant's turn that is running, between two of its commands. What it already did stays done, and is the turn's one undo step. Does nothing while no turn is running. It belongs to the person using the app, so the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate).

#### `assistant.toggle_activity_log`

**Assistant Activity Log**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Opens or closes the built-in assistant's activity log, which lists every command the assistant ran with the time and the result. It changes how the assistant works, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window's Agents page: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate).

#### `assistant.toggle_floating`

**Float Assistant**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Floats the assistant's panel into a window of its own, or docks it back at the main window's right edge. The choice is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. It belongs to the person using the app, so the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate).

### Area `audio`

#### `audio.configure`

**Configure Audio Device**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Changes any of the audio driver type, input and output devices, sample rate, buffer size, and output channels, and applies them straight away without a restart. Fields left out keep their values. If the device refuses the new settings, the previous ones are restored and the error is returned. Changing the sample rate can change the device's own setting for other apps too. The settings are kept for the next start.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buffer_size` | integer or null | no | The buffer size in frames, or 0 for the device's default. |
| `driver` | string or null | no | The driver type: an ID from `audio.devices`, such as `coreaudio`, `wasapi`, `asio`, `jack`, `alsa`, or `null`. Changing it resets the devices to the driver's defaults unless they're given too. |
| `driver_error_compensation_ms` | number or null | no | Driver Error Compensation in milliseconds: kept to two decimals and within -1000 to 1000. A positive value moves new recordings earlier. Changing it doesn't restart the audio stream. |
| `input_device` | string or null | no | The input device: an ID from `audio.devices`, or `none` for no input. |
| `output_channels` | integer or null | no | Output channels to open, or 0 for all the device has. |
| `output_device` | string or null | no | The output device: an ID from `audio.devices`, or `default` for the system's default output device. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | no | The sample rate in hertz, or 0 for the device's current rate. |

Result: [`AudioStatus`](#audiostatus).

#### `audio.devices`

**List Audio Devices**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Lists the driver types this computer offers and, for the chosen one, its input and output devices with the sample rates, buffer sizes, and channels each accepts. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AudioDevices`](#audiodevices).

#### `audio.set_test_tone`

**Test Tone**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Plays or stops the Audio settings' test tone, a sine wave on every output channel for checking that the device works, and sets its level (Tone Volume, -60 to 0 dBFS; -36 on a new install) and frequency (Tone Frequency, 20 Hz to 20 kHz; 440 Hz on a new install). Fields left out keep their values; the level and frequency are kept for the next start. The tone stops when the Settings window closes. Set a low level before switching it on: a loud tone can hurt ears and speakers.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frequency_hz` | number or null | no | The tone's frequency in hertz, from 20 to 20,000 (Tone Frequency). Values outside the range are brought within it. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Whether the test tone plays. |
| `volume_db` | number or null | no | The tone's level in dBFS, from -60 to 0 (Tone Volume). Values outside the range are brought within it. |

Result: [`TestToneState`](#testtonestate).

#### `audio.status`

**Audio Status**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports whether the audio engine is on, the driver and devices in use, the sample rate and buffer size the device actually runs at, the CPU load of audio processing, and any device error. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AudioStatus`](#audiostatus).

#### `audio.toggle_engine`

**Audio Engine On**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the audio engine off, closing the audio device, or on again, reopening it with the current settings. While it's off, nothing plays and the CPU meter reads OFF.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

### Area `automation`

#### `automation.delete`

**Delete Automation**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Deletes all of one of a track's parameters' automation: its envelope and every breakpoint on it, as Delete Automation in the control's context menu does. The control's value stays where it is and the parameter follows it again. Nothing changes if the parameter has no automation.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.delete_breakpoint`

**Delete Automation Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Deletes one of a track's automation breakpoints, so the segments either side of it become the one starting at the breakpoint before it, as clicking a breakpoint on an automation lane does. Deleting the last one takes the parameter's envelope with it, so the parameter follows its control again. A position with no breakpoint is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.move_breakpoint`

**Move Automation Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves one of a track's automation breakpoints from `at` to `to` and, with `value`, to that value, as dragging it on an automation lane does. `to` is 0 (1.1.1) or later and mustn't land on another breakpoint of the same envelope, and `value` is in the parameter's own units. Without `value` the breakpoint keeps its value. A position with no breakpoint is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another breakpoint of the same envelope already is. |
| `value` | number or null | no | The value it takes there, in the parameter's own units, or `null` (or nothing) to keep the value it has. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.re_enable`

**Re-Enable Automation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Turns every overridden envelope in the song back on, as the Control Bar's Re-Enable Automation button does: every automated control that a hand move turned off follows its envelope again. It's one undo step, and nothing changes when no envelope is overridden. Use `automation.re_enable_for` for one parameter.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.re_enable_for`

**Re-Enable Automation for a Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Turns one parameter's overridden envelope back on, as Re-Enable Automation in that control's context menu does. `track` and `target` name the parameter the same way `automation.set_breakpoint` does. Nothing changes if the parameter's envelope isn't overridden.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.set_breakpoint`

**Set Automation Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets one of a track's automatable parameters at `at` on its envelope, adding a breakpoint there or replacing the value of the one that's there, as clicking or dragging a breakpoint on an automation lane does. `target` names the parameter: `{"type": "mixer", "param": "volume"}`, `{"type": "send", "to": <return track>}`, or `{"type": "device", "device": <device>, "param": <parameter>}`. A parameter with no envelope yet gets its first breakpoint and its envelope drives it from then on. Values are in the parameter's own units: volume as linear gain, pan from -1 to 1, the Track Activator 1 for muted, and a device parameter as the device's own value. `at` is 0 (1.1.1) or later. The value between two breakpoints follows the segment's shape: the straight line unless `automation.set_curve` bent it; before the first and after the last the nearest one's value holds.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter: a mixer control, a send, or a device parameter. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint sits: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value there, in the parameter's own units. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `automation.set_curve`

**Curve Automation Segment**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Curves one of a track's automation segments, as holding Alt (Windows) or Option (macOS) while dragging a line segment on an automation lane does. `track` and `target` name the parameter as `automation.set_breakpoint` does, and `at` is the position of the breakpoint the segment starts at. `bend` is a signed number from -1 to 1: 0 is the straight line, the sign chooses which side the segment bows to, and its size how far. Between the two breakpoints the value is `from + (to - from) * t^(2^bend)`, `t` running from 0 at the segment's start to 1 at its end, so the value stays between the two breakpoints' values. A bend of 0 straightens the segment again, as the same drag with a double-click does. Refused when no breakpoint is at `at`, or when `at` is the last breakpoint, with no segment after it. Beatlayer's own law: Live's curved shape isn't measured yet.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track the parameter belongs to. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the segment starts: the breakpoint there. |
| `bend` | number | yes | The bend, from −1 to 1: 0 is the straight line, and the sign chooses which side the segment bows to. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `browser`

#### `browser.add_folder`

**Add Folder to Browser...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `browser-sidebar`.

Adds the folder at `path` to the browser's Places, after Current Project, without moving or changing it, and indexes its files in the background so search finds them. Added folders are kept between launches; adding one twice changes nothing. A person choosing the menu item or the sidebar's Add Folder... picks the folder in a dialog.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The folder's path. |

Result: [`BrowserState`](#browserstate).

#### `browser.add_to_arrangement`

**Add Files to Arrangement**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `browser`.

Puts audio files into the Arrangement as clips, as dragging them from the browser does: onto the audio track `track` starting at `at` (or the insert marker), one after another; or, with no `track`, onto a new audio track below the last track (the drop area), named after the first file. With `spread`, each file goes on a track of its own, new tracks below the target. Each clip is named after its file and lasts as long as the file plays at the song's tempo. A clip placed over part of another replaces that part: the other is shortened, split around it, or removed, so a track never plays two clips at once; when a clip on `track` ends after `at`, it's destructive as well as external. One undo step. Reads the files, outside the project, and registers them so the set keeps them.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | array of string | yes | The audio files, in the order they go down. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where the first clip starts. Left out, the insert marker. It isn't snapped: snap first if you want the grid. |
| `spread` | boolean | no | Put each file on a track of its own (as dropping with Cmd or Ctrl held does), new tracks going below the target, instead of one after another on one track. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The audio track to put them on. Left out (or `null`), a new audio track below the last track, as dropping in the drop area does. |

Result: [`AddResult`](#addresult).

#### `browser.focus_search`

**Search in Browser**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows the browser, chooses the All label, and puts the keyboard focus in the search field, as Cmd-F (Ctrl-F) does, so typing searches. Changes nothing.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-BRW-006 | `Cmd+F` | `Ctrl+F` | `global` | Search the browser | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `browser.load_selected`

**Load Selected Item**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `browser`.

Loads the browser's selected audio files into the Arrangement, as Enter or a double-click does: onto the selected track at the insert marker if it's an audio track, otherwise onto a new audio track below the last one, one after another, as one undo step. A clip placed over part of another replaces that part, so when a clip on that track ends after the insert marker it's destructive as well as external. A selected preset file, or a device or rack listed under a label (Drums, Instruments, Audio Effects, MIDI Effects or Modulators), is added to the shown track as `device.add_preset` and `device.add` add it, and a chain preset to the chain list's rack (`chain.load_preset`). While a device is being hot-swapped (`device.hot_swap`), a selected preset or device replaces it instead (`device.replace`), as does a chain preset the chain armed by its Hot-Swap button (`chain.load_preset`); a selected audio file loads into it if the device plays samples (the sampler, or the eight-slot drum sampler, into its selected slot: `device.load_sample`). With one plug-in selected it loads that plug-in instead, as `plugin.load` does: onto the selected track (a new track when none is), an instrument onto a new MIDI track when the selected track holds audio, or in place of the device being hot-swapped. Reads the files, outside the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-BRW-004 | `Enter` | `Enter` | `browser` | Load the selected item | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AddResult`](#addresult).

#### `browser.open_folder`

**Open Folder**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `browser`.

Opens or closes a folder in the browser's content pane, listing its folders and audio files indented under it (in the Plug-Ins label, a vendor's folder and its plug-ins). Opening a folder closes the other open folders it isn't inside, unless `keep_others` (Cmd or Ctrl held). Right and Left do this on the selected folder. Changes nothing, but reads folders outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The folder, as a row of the content pane gives it. |
| `keep_others` | boolean | no | Keep the other open folders open, as holding Cmd (Ctrl) does. Otherwise opening a folder closes every open folder it isn't inside. |
| `open` | boolean or null | no | Open (true) or close (false). Left out, it toggles. |

Result: [`BrowserState`](#browserstate).

#### `browser.open_place`

**Open Browser Label**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `browser`, `browser-sidebar`.

Chooses a label in the browser's sidebar and shows its contents: a place's folders and audio files, the places themselves under `all`, every audio file under `samples`. Ends any search. Up and Down in the sidebar do this. Changes nothing, but reads folders outside the project.

**Preview**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `browser`.

Previews an audio file (`path`, or the selected file): plays it once from its start through the main output, at the preview volume, on a voice of its own, replacing any preview, whether or not the Preview switch is on, as Shift-Enter and Right do. The file is decoded in the background, so it starts a moment later; `browser.state` reports it loading, then playing. Never changes the set. Plays through the audio device.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

**Remove from Sidebar**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `browser-sidebar`.

Takes a folder the person added out of the browser's Places, as its context menu's Remove from Sidebar does. The folder and its files stay on disk. The User Library and Current Project can't be removed.

| `path` | string | yes | The folder's path. |

**Browser Search**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `browser`, `browser-search`.

Searches the browser by file name, as typing in its search field does: an item matches when every word in `query` appears in its name, ignoring case. Under `all` and `samples` it searches every place (User Library, Current Project, added folders; `samples` only audio files), under a place that place. Returns the browser's state with the results as its rows, in name order; an empty query ends the search. Changes nothing, but lists files outside the project.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

**Select in Browser**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `browser`.

Selects items in the browser's content pane by path (or, in the Plug-Ins label, by the row's key), replacing the selection or, with `add`, adding to it, as clicking, Shift-clicking, and Up and Down do. While the Preview switch is on, selecting one audio file previews it through the audio device; selecting anything else stops the preview. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | array of string | yes | The items to select, by path, as rows of the content pane give them. Empty clears the selection. |
| `add` | boolean | no | Add them to the selection instead of replacing it. |

#### `browser.set_preview`

**Browser File Preview**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `browser`.

Sets the browser's Preview switch (`on`): while it's on, selecting an audio file previews it. Also sets the preview volume (`volume`, a linear gain from 0, silence, to 2, about +6 dB; 1 is unity), which is the Main track's Preview/Cue volume. With no arguments it toggles the switch. Switching it off stops a preview. Both are kept for the next start.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

Shows an audio file in the browser, as Show in Browser does in the Sample Editor: shows the browser, chooses the place the file lies in, opens the folders down to it and selects it. #### `browser.state`

**Browser State**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `browser`, `browser-sidebar`.

Reports what the browser shows: the sidebar's labels and places, the chosen label, the search text, the content pane's rows (folders and audio files, with open folders' contents under them, or the search results; `offset` and `limit` page through them, 100 at a time by default), the selection, the preview, and how far indexing has got. **Stop Preview**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `browser`.

### Area `chain`

#### `chain.add`

**Add Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds a chain to a rack at `index` in the rack's list of chains, where 0 is first. The chain has a new ID from the project, a `name` (left empty, a chain made with a device in it is named after the device's title and an empty one `Chain`), an optional `colour` (0 to 69), `info` text, a `mixer` (leave it out for a new chain's: `volume` 1, `pan` 0, `enabled` true, `solo` false) and its `devices`, each with a new ID, in the order for the kind of rack. A drum rack's chain also takes `receive`, `play`, `choke` and `sends`, and `is_return` makes it one of the rack's return chains (up to six, after the drum chains, audio effects only; a new one has `audio_to` null, which is the rack's own output); any other rack's chain keeps none of these. An empty chain passes its input straight to its mixer, which makes a dry path. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where the chain goes in the rack's list, from 0 to its length. |
| `chain` | [`Chain`](#chain) | yes | The chain, with a new ID, and new IDs for its devices. An empty `name` becomes its first device's title, or `Chain` with none. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.copy`

**Copy Chain**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `rack-chains`.

Copies a rack's chain, or the chains selected in the chain list if `chain` is left out, with their devices, names, colours, info texts and mixers, to the chain clipboard for `chain.paste`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-002 | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` | `global` | Copy | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The chain; the selected chains if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `chain.create`

**Create Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Makes a chain in a rack at `index` (the end if left out), as the chain list's drop area does, named after what it holds, and selects it: holding a new `device`, a device made from a `preset` file, or the existing device `move_device` moved out of where it is; with none of them it is empty. A `preset` that holds a rack makes a chain holding the rack, and one that holds a chain is loaded as `chain.load_preset` loads it. The chain must fit the rack's kind. In a drum rack a chain made without `index` receives the first pad from the view's first that holds no chain, and with `returns` it is a return chain, after the others. One undo step (Insert Chain).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) or null | no | A new device to put in it, as `device.add` describes one. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where the chain goes in the rack's list; the end if left out. |
| `move_device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | A device to move into it from where it is. |
| `preset` | string or null | no | A preset file: the chain holds a new device with its values. |
| `returns` | boolean | no | Make a return chain of a drum rack (the drop area of its return section): it goes after the drum chains and the rack's other return chains, holds audio effects only, and sends to the rack's own output. A drum rack holds six at most. |

Result: [`ChainAdded`](#chainadded).

Copies a rack's chain, or the selected chains if `chain` is left out, to the chain clipboard and deletes them: one undo step (Delete Chain). Because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

#### `chain.extract`

**Extract Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Pulls a drum chain out of its rack onto a new MIDI track, as dragging it from the Session mixer onto the drop area right of the tracks does: the track holds the chain's devices, and the notes the chain received leave the clips of the rack's track (Arrangement and Session) for clips on the new track at the same places and in the same slots, moved to the chain's Play note so its devices hear what they heard in the rack. The chain leaves the rack. One undo step (Move Chain). Dragged from the chain list onto another track or rack it takes only its devices: `chain.drop_on_track`.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

Result: [`Extracted`](#extracted).

#### `chain.extract_return`

**Extract Return Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Pulls a return chain out of its drum rack onto a new return track after the last one, as dragging it onto the Session mixer's returns does: the track holds the chain's audio effects, and the drum chains' sends to it leave the rack with it. One undo step (Move Chain).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |

Result: [`Extracted`](#extracted).

#### `chain.hot_swap`

**Hot-Swap Chain**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Arms a chain for hot-swap, as its Hot-Swap button does, or disarms it; arming it ends the hot-swap of a device, and the other way round. It shows on the chain's row in `device_view.state`. While it is armed, loading a chain preset from the browser replaces the chain (`chain.load_preset`), and loading a device or a preset gives the chain that device as its only one (`device.replace`). It changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Arm (true) or disarm (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `chain.load_preset`

**Load Chain Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Loads a chain preset file (.blpreset) into a rack as a new chain at `index` (the end if left out), as dropping it on the rack's chain list does, with new IDs for it and its devices, and selects it. With `chain` (or, with no `rack`, the chain armed by its Hot-Swap button) it replaces that chain in its place instead, and the new chain stays armed. The chain must fit the rack's kind. One undo step, named Insert Chain, or Load Preset when it replaces a chain. Reads a file outside the project; the samples the preset carries are written to the User Library's Samples/Preset Samples folder if the set's media store lacks them.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The chain preset file. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A chain to replace in its place, instead of adding one; the chain armed by its Hot-Swap button, if there is one and no `rack` is given. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where the new chain goes in the rack's list; the end if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack that takes it as a new chain; the chain list's rack, or the rack being hot-swapped, if left out. |

Result: [`ChainAdded`](#chainadded).

#### `chain.move`

**Move Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a chain to `index` in a rack's list of chains, within its rack or into another rack, on the same track or another, keeping its devices' settings and running state. The index counts positions after the chain is taken out of its current place. The chain must fit the other rack's kind, and a chain can't go into a rack it holds.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack it moves to. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in the rack's list of chains. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.paste`

**Paste Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `rack-chains`.

Pastes the chain clipboard's chains into a rack at `index` (the end if left out), as new chains with new IDs and everything else copied: one undo step (Insert Chain). A chain must fit the rack's kind.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-003 | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` | `global` | Paste | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the rack's list of chains; the end if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack to paste into; the rack in focus if left out. |

Result: [`ChainAdded`](#chainadded).

#### `chain.preview`

**Preview Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Holds a drum chain's Preview button, or lets it go: while it is held the chain plays its Receive note into itself alone, as `pad.preview` does for a pad. It changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `chain.remove`

**Delete Chain**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes a chain from its rack, with its devices and its automation. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.rename`

**Rename Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `rack-chains`.

Renames a rack's chain: the name the chain list shows. An empty name gives it the name a chain has without one: its first device's title, or `Chain` while it holds none.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-008 | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` | `global` | Rename the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

#### `chain.save_preset`

**Save Chain Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves a chain as a Beatlayer chain preset file (.blpreset), as dragging its row into the browser's User Library or a folder in Places does: to `path`, or to a new file named after the chain in `folder`, or, with neither, in the User Library, under Presets/<its rack's category>/<its rack's name>/, numbered if the name is taken. The preset holds the chain's name, colour, info text and mixer, every device in it with its state (nested racks whole, plug-ins' own state included) and the samples they play. The file is written whole or not at all. Writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The chain; the selected one if left out. |
| `folder` | string or null | no | Instead of `path`, a folder to put a new file named after the chain in, numbered if the name is taken: where dragging the row onto a folder in the browser drops it. |
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to write, ending `.blpreset`; a new file named after the chain in the User Library's folder for its rack's presets if left out. |

Result: [`ChainPresetResult`](#chainpresetresult).

#### `chain.select`

**Select Chain**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects chains in a rack's chain list, as clicking a row does, and gives the chain list the keyboard focus: `replace` selects only `chain`, `toggle` adds or removes it (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click), `range` selects every chain from the selected one to it (Shift-click), and `previous` and `next` step the selection up and down the list (Up and Down). The rack's devices view shows the selected chain's devices, or says how many chains are selected. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step and isn't saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The chain to click; left out for `previous` and `next`, which step from the chains selected now. |
| `mode` | [`ChainSelect`](#chainselect) | no | How the selection changes; a click if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `chain.set_audio_to`

**Change Audio To**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets where a drum rack's return chain sends its output: `track` is one of the set's return tracks, whose input it then adds to as a send does (that return runs after the drum rack's track), or null for the rack's own output, which is a new return chain's. Deleting the return track sends the chain back to the rack's output. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The return chain. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The return track, or `null`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_choke`

**Change Choke**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Puts a drum rack's chain in a choke group from 1 to 16, or in none with null: a note that reaches a chain in a group silences every other chain in that group by fading their output over 5 ms, and a chain doesn't choke itself. Unused while the chain's Receive is all notes. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |
| `choke` | integer or null | no | The group, or `null` for none. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_colour`

**Set Chain Colour**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Colours a chain with swatch `colour` of the palette of 5 rows of 14 (0 to 69), or clears its colour with null.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `colour` | integer or null | no | The swatch, or `null` for none. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_enabled`

**Chain Activator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a chain's Chain Activator: a chain that's off adds nothing to its rack's output, and its level glides down over 20 ms. Its devices keep running, and its latency still counts.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it's on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_gain`

**Set Chain Gain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets a chain's Volume as linear gain with the track fader's range: 1 is 0 dB (a new chain's), 2 about +6 dB, 0 silence. The chain's level glides to the new value over 20 ms with no new program. Chains of a MIDI effect rack have no volume. Moving it by hand turns off its automation envelope.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `volume` | number | yes | The gain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_info`

**Edit Chain Info Text**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the info text of a chain, Edit Info Text in its context menu. Empty clears it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `info` | string | yes | The text. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_pan`

**Set Chain Pan**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets a chain's Pan from -1 (left) to 1 (right), 0 centre (a new chain's), by the track mixer's constant-power law. Chains of a MIDI effect rack have no pan.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `pan` | number | yes | The position. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_play`

**Change Play**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the note a drum rack's chain passes on to its devices, from 0 to 127 (60 is C3, which plays a sampler's sample at its own pitch and is a new chain's), at the velocity it came with. Unused while the chain's Receive is all notes. Only a drum rack's drum chains have a Play. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |
| `play` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The note. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_receive`

**Change Receive**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the note a drum rack's chain answers: `receive` is `{"note": n}` for one MIDI note from 0 to 127 (Live's octave numbering: C3 is 60, and a pad's chain answers its pad's note, 36 for C1 on the first pad) or `"all_notes"`, which passes every note as it came and leaves the chain's Play and Choke unused. A note-on reaches every chain that answers it; a note no chain answers sounds nothing, and a note-off follows its note-on to the chains it reached whatever Receive says by then. The chain moves to its new note's pad at once. Only a drum rack's drum chains have a Receive. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |
| `receive` | [`Receive`](#receive) | yes | What it answers. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_send`

**Set Chain Send**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets a drum rack's drum chain's send to one of the rack's return chains (`to`) as linear gain: 0 is -inf dB and a new send's level, 1 is 0 dB. The send is taken after the chain's Volume, Pan and activator, and glides to a new value over 20 ms. Moving it by hand turns off its automation envelope. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The drum chain. |
| `to` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The return chain. |
| `level` | number | yes | The gain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_solo`

**Solo Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Solos or unsolos a chain: while any chain of a rack is soloed, the rack's unsoloed chains add nothing. It leaves every other rack and every track as it is.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `solo` | boolean | yes | Whether it's soloed. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.set_zone`

**Change Chain Zone**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets one of a chain's zones: `kind` key (notes 0 to 127), velocity (1 to 127) or select (the chain select zone, 0 to 127), with `low`, `high` and the values each fade spans (`fade_low`, `fade_high`). A zone holds at least one value of its scale and its fades stay inside it. A note in a key or velocity fade reaches the chain with its velocity scaled linearly, silent at the zone's edge and full at the fade's inner edge, as a multisampler's linear fades are; a chain select fade scales the chain's output the same way. A new chain's zones pass everything: every note, every velocity, and chain select 0 alone. An audio effect rack's chains have only a chain select zone, and a drum rack's none. One undo step, as one drag in the zone editor is. What it sets reads back in the `zones` of the query tool's `device` object.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `kind` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) | yes | Which zone. |
| `zone` | [`Zone`](#zone) | yes | The new zone. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `chain.solo`

**Solo Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `rack-chains`.

Solos the selected chains, or `chain`, as a chain's Solo button does: it is the rack's only soloed chain, and soloing it again unsolos it; with `add` it adds or removes the chain and leaves the others as they are (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click). Other racks and the tracks are not touched. One undo step. `chain.set_solo` sets one chain's solo by its ID.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-023 | `S` | `S` | `rack-chains` | Solo the selected rack chain | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | boolean | no | Add or remove the chain without touching the others' solo, as Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) does; otherwise it's the only one soloed. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The chain; the selected chains if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `clip`

#### `clip.create`

**Create Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Puts a new clip on an audio or MIDI track's arrangement lane, at `clip.start` for `clip.length` ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). An audio clip names its audio file by content hash and plays it unwarped, at the file's own speed, from the moment the song reaches the clip; its optional settings (Start and End markers, loop, gain, fades) default to playing the whole file once at 0 dB with no fades. A MIDI clip carries its notes, placed from the clip's start. Audio clips go only on audio tracks and MIDI clips only on MIDI tracks. `clip.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `clip` | [`Clip`](#clip) | yes | The clip, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.create_in_slot`

**Create Clip in Slot**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Puts a clip in a track's Session slot at `scene`, as Insert Empty MIDI Clip (Cmd+Shift+M) and dropping a clip in a slot do. Only audio and MIDI tracks hold slot clips, the slot must be empty, and the clip's data must match the track.
