A multisampler's `layer` (its first selected layer if left out) keeps its markers on the audio they marked: those after a cut move earlier by its length, those inside it to its start, and those outside a trim to its nearer end; Simpler's Start, Length and Loop are shares of the sample and stay. `revert: true` clears the list instead. One undo step named for the edit. The list reads back as `sample_edits` in the query tool's `device` result for Simpler and as `edits` in each layer of `layers` for the multisampler.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `kind` | [`SampleEditKind`](#sampleeditkind) or null | no | What the edit does. Leave it out with `revert`. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. Simpler has one sample and no layers. |
| `range` | [`SampleRange`](#samplerange) or null | no | The selection it acts on, in frames of the sample as the earlier edits left it, at its own rate. Left out it acts on the whole sample; Trim and Cut need one. |
| `revert` | boolean | no | Clears the sample's edit list instead of adding to it. |

Result: [`SampleEdited`](#sampleedited).

#### `device.expand`

**Expand Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides a device's expanded part, as the toggle in its title bar does: the extra controls (a modulation section, say) some devices keep out of sight until asked; switches unless `expanded` says which. Only devices with an expanded part (`expandable` in `device_view.state`) have one. Like folding, it changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set. The device's width in the chain follows it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `expanded` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false) the expanded part; switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.fold`

**Fold Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Folds a device to a narrow strip showing only its title bar on its side, or unfolds it, as double-clicking its title bar or the context menu's Fold does; switches unless `folded` says which. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-014 | `Minus` | `Minus` | `device-view` | Fold or unfold the selected device | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `folded` | boolean or null | no | Fold (true) or unfold (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.group`

**Group**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`, `rack-chains`.

Wraps the selected devices (or `devices`, all in one chain) in a new rack, as Group does: the rack takes the first device's place and holds one chain, named after the first device, that holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state; the rack is selected. The rack is the kind that can hold them: an audio effect rack for audio effects alone, a MIDI effect rack for MIDI effects alone, and an instrument rack for any other mix. A selection that grouping would put out of the chain's order is refused. With `chains` (several chains of one rack) they become the chains of a new rack of the same kind, inside a new chain in the first one's place. One undo step (Group).

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-001 | `Cmd+G` | `Ctrl+G` | `device-view` | Group the selected devices into a rack | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chains` | array or null | no | Several chains of one rack to group instead: they become the chains of a new rack of the same kind, in a new chain in the first one's place. |
| `devices` | array or null | no | The devices to wrap in a new rack, all in one chain; the selected device if both lists are left out. |

Result: [`Grouped`](#grouped).

#### `device.group_to_drum_rack`

**Group to Drum Rack**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Wraps the selected devices (or `devices`, all in one chain of a MIDI track) in a new drum rack, which takes the first device's place: the rack holds one chain, named after the first device, that receives note 36 (C1, the first pad a new drum rack shows) and plays C3, and holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state. They must fit one chain of an instrument rack: MIDI effects, then at most one instrument, then audio effects. One undo step (Group).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devices` | array or null | no | The devices, all in one chain of a track; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`Grouped`](#grouped).

#### `device.hot_swap`

**Hot-Swap Presets**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`, `browser`.

Starts or ends hot-swapping a device's presets, as the title bar's Hot-Swap Presets button does; switches unless `on` says which. While it lasts, the browser shows a bar (Swapping Audio Effect) and opens the User Library's folder of the device's presets, and loading a preset from the browser (Enter or a double-click) loads it into the device. Any device, preset or rack preset of the same role replaces it (`device.replace`), and hot-swap stays on after each load. With no `device` and none selected, it arms the first audio effect of the shown track, or its instrument on a MIDI track. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-008 | `Q` | `Q` | `device-view` | Hot-swap the selected device | runs it |
| S-VIEW-006 | `Q` | `Q` | `global` | Toggle hot-swap mode for the selected device or item | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping; switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.hot_swap_layer`

**Hot-Swap Sample**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Starts hot-swapping a layer's sample (`layer`, or the first selected layer), as the zone editor's Hot-Swap Sample button does: the sample the browser then loads (Enter or a double-click on a file) replaces the layer's, keeping its zones and settings, as one undo step. `on: false` ends it. It changes nothing in the set by itself.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer; the first selected layer if left out. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping; starts if left out. |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.import_sfz`

**Import SFZ**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Imports an SFZ multisample instrument, the open text format, as a multisampler: each region becomes a layer (its sample, key and velocity zones with their crossfades as fades, Root Key, tuning, Volume, Pan, start and end points, loop and loop mode), and the device-wide settings most regions agree on (the volume, filter, filter and pitch envelopes, Vel > Vol, Pitch Bend Range, reverse, the fade law) set the new device's controls. Sequences (`seq_length`) turn Round Robin on in Forward mode, random windows (`lorand`) in Random mode. With `device`, a multisampler, only the layers are added, at the end of its list; otherwise a multisampler is made on `track`, or on a new MIDI track below the last. The samples join the set's media where they lie. Regions whose sample is missing or isn't audio, or whose `trigger` isn't `attack`, are left out and named in `left_out`; opcodes the import doesn't read are listed in `unread`. A file with no region left changes nothing. One undo step. It reads files outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The `.sfz` file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | A multisampler to add the regions to as layers, at the end of its list. Left out, the import makes a multisampler: on `track`, or on a new MIDI track below the last track. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track to put a new multisampler on, after its other devices. Ignored with `device`. |

Result: [`SfzImported`](#sfzimported).

#### `device.insert`

**Insert Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`, `browser`.

Inserts a device into a track's device chain at `index`, where 0 is first in the signal flow. The device is a native Beatlayer device named by its type ID, or a plug-in named by its format and plug-in ID, with its `name` (the device's own, such as the title bar shows), its `role` (`midi_effect`, `instrument`, or `audio_effect`, the default), and any parameter values to set. A chain keeps Live's order: MIDI effects first, then at most one instrument, then audio effects, and only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments; an index that breaks the order is refused. `device.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it. To add a device as a person does, after the selected device and with its default preset, use `device.add`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in the chain, from 0 to the chain's length. |
| `device` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The device, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.insert_in_chain`

**Insert Device in Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Inserts a device into a rack's chain at `index`, where 0 is first in the chain's signal flow, as `device.insert` does for a track's chain. The chain may belong to a rack at any depth. The device is described as for `device.insert`, with a new ID. A chain keeps the order for its kind of rack: an audio effect rack's chains hold only audio effects, a MIDI effect rack's only MIDI effects, and an instrument or drum rack's chains hold MIDI effects, then at most one instrument, then audio effects; an index or device that breaks it is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in the chain, from 0 to the chain's length. |
| `device` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The device, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.insert_layers`

**Add Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds layers to a multisampler at `index` (`null` for the end), each a sample named by content hash with its zones (every zone whole and unfaded in a new layer), Root Key, loop points and levels. The multisampler gives each layer the next of its own layer IDs, in order, ignoring the `id` you send; read them back from the device's `layers` in the query tool's `device` result. A sample must be in the media store to play; to add files from disk as a person does, use `device.add_layers`. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`Layer`](#layer) | yes | The layers. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where in the layer list the first goes, or `null` for the end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.load_preset`

**Load Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Loads a Beatlayer preset file (.blpreset) into a device of the kind it was saved from, as choosing it while hot-swapping does: every parameter takes the preset's value (or its default, if the preset doesn't set it), and the device's title shows the preset's name. One undo step. A preset for another kind of device is refused. A rack preset loads into a rack of the kind it was saved from and replaces the rack with the preset's, as one undo step (the rack's ID changes; `device.replace` loads a preset into a device of another kind). A chain preset loads with `chain.load_preset`. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The preset file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.load_sample`

**Load Sample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Loads an audio file into a device that plays samples (the sampler, or the eight-slot drum sampler), as dropping the file on the device does: the file goes into the set's media store, named by its content hash, and the device keeps that reference, so the set reopens playing it. `slot` says which of a device's sample slots takes it (counted from 0); left out, it is the slot selected in the panel, or the only one. One undo step, named Load Sample. Reads a file outside the project. A device whose type doesn't play a sample, or a slot it doesn't have, is refused. `device.set_sample` with a null `media` clears a slot.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The audio file to load into the device. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `slot` | integer or null | no | The sample slot to load it into, counted from 0; the slot the panel has selected for a device with several, and 0 for one with one. |

Result: [`LoadSampleResult`](#loadsampleresult).

#### `device.move`

**Move Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a device to `index` in a track's chain, on the same track or another, with its settings. The index counts positions after the device is taken out of its current place. The chain must stay in Live's order (MIDI effects, the instrument, then audio effects), so an audio effect can't go before an instrument, and MIDI effects and instruments only go on MIDI tracks.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track it moves to. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that chain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.move_layers`

**Move Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves the listed layers, keeping their order, so the first sits at `index` among the layers that stay; the list's order decides Round Robin's turns and which layer a sort leaves first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layers to move. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where the first goes among the layers left. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.move_to_chain`

**Move Device to Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a device to `index` in a rack's chain, from a track's chain or another chain, on the same track or another, keeping its settings and running state. The index counts positions after the device is taken out of its current place. The chain must stay in order for its kind of rack. A rack can't be moved into one of its own chains. To move a device out of a rack, use `device.move`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain it moves to. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that chain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.normalize_layers`

**Normalize**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Normalize Volume sets each layer's Volume (`layers`, or the selected ones) so its sample's largest magnitude between Sample Start and Sample End reaches 0 dBFS; Normalize Pan sets each layer's Pan so its left and right channels play at equal RMS level after the pan. A silent layer, and a mono one for Normalize Pan, keep their value. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | [`Normalize`](#normalize) | yes | What to normalise. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.parameters`

**Device Parameters**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports a device's parameters, in the order its type lists them: each one's number (what `device.set_param` takes), name, what it does, its kind (a continuous value with its range, unit, and taper; a gain, whose value is a linear factor from 0, which is -inf dB, up to its top; a switch; a choice with its names; or a whole number), its default, whether it can be automated (every parameter can), its value now, and how that value reads. Empty for a device whose type doesn't describe its parameters, such as a plug-in that couldn't be loaded. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceParameters`](#deviceparameters).

#### `device.paste`

**Paste Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Pastes the clipboard's device, as a new device with its settings, before the selected device (or `before`), or at the end of the chain with none selected, on the selected track (or `track`), and selects it: one undo step, named Copy Device. The chain keeps Live's order, so an audio effect can't go before an instrument, and instruments and MIDI effects only go on MIDI tracks. With `chain` it pastes into that rack chain, or before a device that is in one.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-003 | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` | `global` | Paste | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | Paste before this device, which may be in a rack's chain; before the selected device, or at the end of the chain with none selected, if left out. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A rack's chain to paste into, at any depth, in place of the track's own chain (WP-5.1). |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.remove`

**Delete Device**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes a device from its track's chain, with its settings. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. To bypass a device but keep it, use `device.set_enabled`. From the keyboard it deletes the device selected in the Device View.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-005 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `global` | Delete | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.rename`

**Rename Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames a device: the name its title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on (`device.set_show_preset_name`). An empty name gives the device back its own name, such as `Auto Filter`. It changes nothing in the sound.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-008 | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` | `global` | Rename the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.rename_layer`

**Rename Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames a layer, as the layer list's Rename does. The name is what the title bar shows for the first layer while Show Preset Name is on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.replace`

**Replace Device**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a device or rack with another of the same role, in its place, as loading from the browser does while the device is hot-swapped (an audio effect or audio effect rack for an audio effect; an instrument, an instrument rack or a drum rack for an instrument; a MIDI effect or MIDI effect rack for a MIDI effect). Give a `preset` file, or a `new_device` as `device.add` describes one. `device` is the one being hot-swapped, else the selected one, if left out. A device preset of the device's own kind loads into it as `device.load_preset` does, keeping its ID and automation; anything else replaces it with a new device with new IDs, without the automation of a device of another kind, and a rack's chains go with it. With `chain`, the new device becomes the only one in that chain, which keeps its name and mixer. One undo step, named Load Preset for a preset and Insert Device for a device. Hot-swap stays on for the replacement. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A chain to give the new device to as its only one, instead of replacing a device: the chain keeps its mixer and name. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device or rack to replace; the device being hot-swapped, or else the selected one, if left out. |
| `new_device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) or null | no | A new device, as `device.add` describes one. |
| `preset` | string or null | no | A preset file: a device's or a rack's. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.reverse_sample`

**Reverse Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reverses the whole sample by writing a processed copy: a WAV with the sample's edits applied and then reversed, at its rate and channels, in the project's `Samples/Processed/Reverse/` folder. The device or layer then plays the copy with its edit list empty and its markers where they were, as one undo step; the original file stays as it was. A set that has never been saved is refused with a message in the Status Bar. The copy reads back as the device's or layer's `media`. `device.edit_sample` with `kind: reverse` reverses without a file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`SampleProcessed`](#sampleprocessed).

#### `device.save_default_preset`

**Save as Default Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves a device's state as the default preset for its type, as the context menu's Save as Default Preset does: to the User Library's Defaults/<Audio Effects, Instruments, or MIDI Effects>/<the device's own name>.blpreset, replacing any default saved before. Every device of that type added from then on (`device.add`) starts with it; for a rack, every new rack of its kind starts as the saved one is, chains and all. Writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.save_preset`

**Save Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves a device's state (its parameter values) as a Beatlayer preset file (.blpreset), as the title bar's Save Preset button does: to `path`, or to a new file named after the device's title in the User Library, under Presets/<Audio Effects, Instruments, or MIDI Effects>/<the device's own name>/, numbered if the name is taken. The device's title then shows the preset's name. A rack is saved whole, as a rack preset: its chains in order with their names, colours and mixers, every device in them (nested racks too) with its state, a plug-in's own state included, and the samples its devices play, so it loads in a set that lacks them. The file is written whole or not at all. Writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to write, ending `.blpreset`; a new file in the User Library's folder for the device's presets, named after its title, if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.select`

**Select Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a device, as clicking its title bar does, or none with `null`. The Device View's keys (Delete, Cmd-C, Cmd-D, Cmd-R) act on it. Selecting changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device, or `null` to select none. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.select_layers`

**Select Samples**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects layers in a multisampler's layer list, as clicking does: `replace` makes the listed layers the selection (every layer with none listed), `add` joins them to it, `toggle` flips each, and `same_range` selects every layer whose range in the editor in view equals the first listed layer's. The selection shows in the Sample tab and reads back in `device_view.state`. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | no | The layers; every layer if left out with `replace`. |
| `mode` | [`LayerSelectMode`](#layerselectmode) | no | How they change the selection. |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.select_slot`

**Select Sample Slot**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects one of a device's sample slots, as clicking its cell in the panel does: the panel then shows that slot's controls, and a sample loaded without naming a slot goes into it. Only a device with sample slots has any (the eight-slot drum sampler has eight, counted from 0). It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set. The selected slot is `selected_slot` in the device's panel (`device.state`).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The slot, counted from 0. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.set_display_view`

**Set Display View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Chooses the view a device's display shows, as its view buttons do: a compressor's Transfer Curve, Activity, or Collapsed. Only a device whose display has views takes one, and only one of them. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and `device_view.state` and `device.display` report the view chosen.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes | The view, one of the device's description's `views`. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.set_enabled`

**Activate/Deactivate Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device on or off, as its Device Activator in the title bar does. A device that's off passes its input through unchanged, so you can hear the track with and without it; it keeps its settings and its state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it's on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_enabled_all`

**Switch Device and Contents**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device and every device inside it, at any depth, on or off with `enabled`: Option-click (Alt-click) on a rack's Device Activator. On a device that isn't a rack it is `device.set_enabled`. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-003 | `Option+click a device activator` | `Alt+click a device activator` | `device-view` | Turn every device in a rack on or off | toggles `enabled` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device, usually a rack. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether they're on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_external`

**Set External Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the routing of a device that works with hardware outside the computer (the External Instrument), as the choosers in its title bar do; give only the settings to change. `midi_to` is `{ "type": "none" }` (No Output, a new device's) or `{ "type": "port", "name": ... }` with a MIDI output port's name as `midi.ports` lists it, with its Track switch on; `channel` is the MIDI channel to send on, 1 to 16 (1 on a new device); `audio_from` is the audio interface's inputs the hardware's sound comes back on, a channel or a pair (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 1 }`, the first pair on a new device); `hardware_latency` is the delay the hardware adds that the computer can't detect, in the unit the unit switch is on: `{ "unit": "milliseconds", "value": 12.5 }` (0 to 1000, kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ "unit": "samples", "value": 600 }` (0 to 192000, kept in samples); to switch the unit, send the converted value. Each change recompiles the song's audio, so these are settings, not parameters. Read them back in the query tool's `device` result, under `external`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `audio_from` | [`Channel`](#channel) or null | no | Audio From: the audio interface's inputs it comes back on. |
| `channel` | integer or null | no | The MIDI channel, 1 to 16. |
| `hardware_latency` | [`HardwareLatency`](#hardwarelatency) or null | no | Hardware Latency with its unit: the unit switch is the unit given, so switching the unit sends the converted value. |
| `midi_to` | [`ExternalPort`](#externalport) or null | no | MIDI To: `none` for No Output, or `port` with the MIDI output port's name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_floating`

**Float**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Floats a native device in a window of its own (`floating`: true), or docks it back in the Device View (false), as the device's context menu item Float, its window's Dock button, and closing its window do. While it floats, its place in the chain shows as a narrow strip, so the signal order stays readable, and its window can be made larger: only its displays grow, its controls keeping their size and place. Floating and docking are one undo step each (Float Device, Dock Device); whether a device floats is saved with the set. Moving or resizing the window is `device.set_window`, which isn't an undo step. Plug-ins open their own editor windows instead, so they can't float. It changes nothing in the sound. From the keyboard (Option-F on macOS, Ctrl-Alt-F on Windows and Linux, with the Device View or a floating device's window focused) and the menu it switches the selected device.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-015 | `Option+F` | `Ctrl+Alt+F` | `device-view` | Float the selected device in its own window, or dock it | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `floating` | boolean | yes | Float (true) or dock (false). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer`

**Change Sample Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Changes settings of layers (`layers`, or the selected ones) as the Sample tab does: Root Key, Detune, Volume (a linear gain), Pan, Sample Start and End, Link, the sustain and release modes, Loop Start and End, the Release Loop point, the loop's Crossfade and Detune. While the multisampler's Snap is on, every marker set lands on the nearest zero crossing of the layer's left channel. Markers are in frames of the sample at its own rate. The markers must stay ordered; one setting out of range refuses the whole change. One undo step. `device.update_layers` sets them exactly, without snapping.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | [`LayerSettings`](#layersettings) | yes | The settings to set; the ones left out stay as they were. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.set_layer_media`

**Replace Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces one layer's sample with another already in the media store, keeping the layer's zones and settings and its markers at the same share of the new length, as hot-swapping a sample does. `length`, `sample_rate` and `channels` describe the new sample. To pick a file from disk, use `device.set_layer_sample`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The new sample, by content hash. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its length in frames at its own rate. |
| `sample_rate` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its own rate in hertz. |
| `channels` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | Its channels. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer_options`

**Change Sample Options**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the multisampler options that aren't parameters: `ram_mode` (decode every layer whole into memory; off, long layers stream from disk), `snap` (markers set afterwards land on zero crossings of the left channel) and `linear_loop_fades` (the title bar's Use Constant Power Fade for Loops, off when true). Options left out stay as they were.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `linear_loop_fades` | boolean or null | no | Whether loop crossfades are linear rather than constant-power. |
| `ram_mode` | boolean or null | no | RAM Mode: decode every layer whole into memory. |
| `snap` | boolean or null | no | Snap: markers land on zero crossings. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer_sample`

**Replace Sample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a layer's sample (`layer`, or the first selected layer) with an audio file, keeping its zones and settings and its markers at the same share of the new length, as hot-swapping a sample does. The file is imported into the set's media. One undo step. It reads a file outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The audio file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer; the first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.set_layer_zone`

**Change Zones**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets one kind of zone (`key` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127, or `select` 0 to 127) of the listed layers, each with its own `low`, `high` and fades (`fade_low` and `fade_high`, how many values each fade spans). A zone holds at least one value and its fades stay inside it. In a fade the layer is silent at the zone's edge and reaches full level at the fade's inner edge, linearly or constant-power as the device's Fade Mode says. One undo step, as one drag in the zone editor is.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `kind` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) | yes | Which zone. |
| `zones` | array of [`LayerZone`](#layerzone) | yes | Each layer's new zone. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_midi_sidechain_source`

**Set MIDI Sidechain Source**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the MIDI track a device's MIDI sidechain listens to, as the MIDI source chooser in its sidechain parameters does: `track` is a MIDI track (the device's own track too), or left out for No Input, a new device's. The device hears the notes and channel messages that track's clips and input play, before its own devices change them; the track still plays as before. Only devices that declare a MIDI sidechain input have one. Deleting the track leaves No Input.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track whose notes and channel messages the device hears (its own track too), or `None` for No Input. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_multisampler_view`

**Set Multisampler View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets what a multisampler's views show, as its title bar's tabs and the zone editor's controls do: the `tab` in its body (`sample`, `pitch_osc`, `filter_global`, `modulation` or `midi`), whether the zone editor shows above the Device View (`zone_editor`, the Zone tab), which editor shows (`editor`: `key`, `velocity` or `select`), its row `size`, and Auto Select. The views are saved with the set but are no undo step, and change nothing in the sound. They read back in `device_view.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_select` | boolean or null | no | Auto Select: notes select the layers they play. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `editor` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) or null | no | Which zone editor shows: Key, Vel or Sel. |
| `size` | [`EditorSize`](#editorsize) or null | no | The zone editor's row size. |
| `tab` | [`SamplerTab`](#samplertab) or null | no | The tab shown in the body. |
| `zone_editor` | boolean or null | no | Whether the zone editor shows above the Device View (the Zone tab). |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.set_param`

**Set Device Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets one of a device's parameters to a value in the parameter's own units. The value must be finite. Parameters that haven't been set keep their defaults.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) | yes | The parameter. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value, in the parameter's own units. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_processed_layer_sample`

**Replace With Processed Copy**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a layer's sample with a processed copy of its edited sample that is already in the media store (`media`, `length` frames at its own rate): the copy holds the edits, so the layer's list empties. `crop` is the span of the edited sample the copy keeps, which moves the markers as a Trim does; with none the markers stay where they are. One undo step, named Crop with a `crop` and Reverse without. `device.crop_sample` and `device.reverse_sample` write the copy.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The copy, by content hash. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its length in frames at its own rate. |
| `crop` | [`SampleRange`](#samplerange) or null | no | The edited sample's span the copy keeps, or `null` for all of it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sample`

**Set Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the audio a device plays (`media`, a content hash, or null to play none), which the media store holds like a clip's audio, in sample slot `slot` (counted from 0, and 0 unless given: the sampler has the one, the eight-slot drum sampler eight). A device whose type plays samples plays that file; other devices ignore it. The set keeps the reference, so it reopens playing the same file. Null clears the slot, one undo step named Clear Sample. To load a file from disk as a person does, use `device.load_sample`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The media, by content hash, or `null` to play none. The media store is where the audio comes from; a device given media the store doesn't hold is silent. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | The sample slot to set: 0, the only one the sampler has, unless given; the eight-slot drum sampler's are 0 to 7 (WP-5.17). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_show_preset_name`

**Show Preset Name**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's Show Preset Name, the context menu item: on (as every new device is), the title bar shows the name of the preset last loaded or saved, or the name Rename gave it; off, the device's own name. It changes nothing in the sound.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `shown` | boolean | yes | Whether the preset's or given name shows. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_enabled`

**External Sidechain On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's sidechain on or off, as the External switch in its sidechain section does. On, the device's detector (a compressor's level detector, say) listens to its sidechain input instead of the track's own signal; its output is still the track's signal, processed. Off, as on a new device, it listens to its own input.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the sidechain is on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_gain`

**Set SC Gain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the gain a device's sidechain signal gets before its detector hears it, as linear gain: 1 is 0 dB (a new device's), 2 about +6 dB, 0 silence. Raise it when the sidechain source is too quiet to trigger the device.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `gain` | number | yes | The gain: 1 is 0 dB. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_input`

**Set Sidechain Input**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets where a device's sidechain listens, as the Source chooser in its sidechain section does: `none` (No Input, a new device's), or `track` with another audio, group, or return track, Main, or the device's own track, and a `tap`: `pre_fx`, `post_fx` (what choosing a track in the window picks), or `post_mixer`. Only devices that declare a sidechain input have one. The source track still plays as before; the device only listens to it. The detector hears it only while External is on (`device.set_sidechain_enabled`). To make a kick duck a bass, set the bass compressor's source to the kick's track and switch External on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | yes | `none` (No Input), or `track` with an audio, group, or return track or Main (the device's own track too) and a `tap`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_listen`

**Sidechain Listen**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's Sidechain Listen: on, the device's output is what its detector hears (the sidechain, after its gain and mix) instead of the processed track, so you can check what triggers it. Switch it off to hear the track again.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `listen` | boolean | yes | Whether to listen. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_mix`

**Set Sidechain Mix**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets how much of what a device's detector hears is its sidechain, from 0 (only the track's own signal) to 1 (only the sidechain, a new device's). Values between blend the two.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `mix` | number | yes | The mix, from 0 to 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_state`

**Set Device State**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a device's whole state at once, as loading a preset does: `params` lists every parameter value to set, as `[parameter, value]` pairs (any parameter not listed goes back to its default), and `name` is what its title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on (empty for the device's own name). One undo step. To load a preset file, use `device.load_preset`; to change one parameter, `device.set_param`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `params` | array of pair of [`ParamId`](#paramid) and number | yes | The parameter values, as `[parameter, value]` pairs, each finite and each parameter once. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on, such as the preset's; empty for the device's own name. |
| `shape` | array or null | no | A Shaper's breakpoint shape (the modulation spec, R23), which a preset of one holds; `null` for the default shape. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_window`

**Move Device Window**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves or resizes a floating device's window, as dragging it does: `frame` is its outer top-left corner and the size of its contents, in points. A size is kept within the window's smallest (the device's docked size) and, for a device that doesn't grow, held at it. The frame is saved with the set but isn't an undo step, so undo never moves a window instead of undoing an edit.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The floating device. |
| `frame` | [`WindowFrame`](#windowframe) | yes | Where its window sits and how big its contents are, in points. |

Result: [`FloatingWindows`](#floatingwindows).

#### `device.show_sidechain`

**Show Sidechain**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides a device's sidechain section, as the toggle at the top of the device's left strip does; switches unless `shown` says which. Only devices with a sidechain input or a MIDI sidechain input have one. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. The section's settings are the set's: `device.set_sidechain_input`, `device.set_sidechain_enabled`, `device.set_sidechain_mix`, `device.set_sidechain_gain`, and `device.set_sidechain_listen`; the MIDI sidechain's, `device.set_midi_sidechain_source`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.snap_layer_markers`

**Snap Markers**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Snaps a loop's two markers (the sustain loop's Loop Start and Loop End, or the release loop's point) to the nearest zero crossings of the layers' left channel once, whatever Snap says, as the loop brace's context menu does. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |
| `loop` | [`LoopKind`](#loopkind) | no | Which loop's markers; the sustain loop's if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.sort_layers`

**Sort Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sorts a multisampler's layers by name, key, velocity or selector (the lowest value of that zone), ascending or `descending`, as the layer list's sorting items do. Layers that tie keep their order.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `by` | [`LayerSort`](#layersort) | yes | What to sort by. |
| `descending` | boolean | yes | Whether the largest comes first. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.swap_to_snapshot`

**Swap to Simpler**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a Drum Sampler with Simpler in One-Shot mode, as Drum Sampler's context menu does: the new device takes the old one's place, sample, and on or off state, and keeps its sample's Start and Length; every other setting is Simpler's default. One undo step, named Swap to Simpler, and the new device is selected. A device that isn't a Drum Sampler is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.ungroup`

**Ungroup**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Takes the selected rack (or `device`) apart, as Ungroup does: the devices of its one chain take the rack's place in order and the first is selected; the rack, its chain's mixer and its Macro Controls go. A rack with no chains is just removed; a rack of several chains can't be taken apart. One undo step (Ungroup).

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-002 | `Cmd+Shift+G` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` | `device-view` | Ungroup the selected rack | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`Ungrouped`](#ungrouped).

#### `device.unwrap_rack`

**Take a Rack Apart**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Takes a rack with one chain, or none, apart: the chain's devices take the rack's place in order, keeping their settings and running state; the rack, its chain and its mixer are gone. A rack of several chains can't be taken apart. One undo step. To ungroup the selected rack as a person does, use `device.ungroup`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.update_layers`

**Change Sample Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Changes settings of the listed layers exactly as given, without snapping markers to zero crossings (`device.set_layer` does that while Snap is on): `root_key`, `detune`, `volume` (a linear gain, up to +24 dB), `pan`, `start`, `end`, `link`, `sustain` and `release` modes, `loop_start`, `loop_end`, `release_loop` (frames of the sample at its own rate), `crossfade_ms`, `loop_detune` and `one_shot` (the layer's voices play on to Sample End whatever the note does, as an SFZ `one_shot` region's do). Settings left out stay as they were. The markers must stay ordered: Start, Loop Start, Loop End, Release Loop and End, inside the sample. One setting out of range refuses the whole command.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layers to change. |
| `settings` | [`LayerSettings`](#layersettings) | yes | The settings to set. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.windows`

**Floating Device Windows**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports every floating device's window (IMP-14), on any track: the device and its track, the window's title, where it sits and how big it is (`frame`, in points, `null` until the app has placed it), its smallest size (the device's docked size under its title bar), whether it can grow (only a device with a display that grows can), and the device as its window draws it. `device.set_floating` floats and docks devices. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`FloatingWindows`](#floatingwindows).

#### `device.wrap_in_rack`

**Wrap Devices in a Rack**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Wraps devices of one chain in a new rack, which takes the first device's place: the rack holds one chain that holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state. `devices` are in one chain of a track or a rack; `rack` is a new rack device (its kind `rack` of `instrument`, `audio_effect`, `midi_effect` or `drum`, and the role of its kind) with new IDs and exactly one empty chain. The rack's kind must be one that can hold them: an audio effect rack for audio effects alone, a MIDI effect rack for MIDI effects alone, an instrument rack for any other mix. A grouping that would break the chain's order is refused. One undo step. To group the selection as a person does, use `device.group`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devices` | array of [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The devices, all in one chain of a track or a rack. Not empty. |
| `rack` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The new rack, with a new ID, of a kind that can hold the devices, with exactly one chain, with a new ID and no devices. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `device_view`

#### `device_view.state`

**Device View State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the Device View shows: the selected track and its devices in signal order, each with its title, its own name, its kind and role, whether it's on, folded, selected, or being hot-swapped, and whether it has an expanded part (`expandable`) and shows it (`expanded`); the selected device; hot-swapping; and whether there's a device to paste. A native device also lists its parameters' descriptors, its layout, and its values (`panel`); `device.parameters` reports any device's. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `edit`

#### `edit.redo`

**Redo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Redoes the step most recently undone. It fails if nothing has been undone since the last new change, because a new change discards the steps that could have been redone.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-007 | `Cmd+Shift+Z` | `Ctrl+Y` | `global` | Redo | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `edit.undo`

**Undo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Undoes the newest step in the undo history: the last command or gesture, however many changes it made. Use it to reverse a mistake; `edit.redo` puts the step back. It fails if there's nothing to undo.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-006 | `Cmd+Z` | `Ctrl+Z` | `global` | Undo | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `export`

#### `export.audio`

**Export Audio**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Renders the set's Main output (what you hear) or individual tracks to audio files, offline and faster than real time, as the File menu's Export Audio/Video does. `path` is the file to write; `bit_depth` (16, 24, or 32) and `sample_rate` are required. `rendered_track` chooses `main` (the default), `all_tracks`, `selected_tracks`, or a single track `{ "track": <id> }`. With an individual track, `include_return_and_main_effects` includes return tracks and Main devices (unavailable for `main`). Multi-track exports write one file per track beside `path`. The file type follows the extension (`.wav`, `.aif`/`.aiff`, `.flac`, `.mp3`; FLAC holds 16 or 24 bits only) or `file_type`. MP3 writes 320 kbps CBR at one of MP3's sample rates, and ignores `bit_depth` and `dither`. `render_as_loop` adds the tail the song leaves after the range's end onto the file's start, so the file loops without a cut tail. The range is `start` and `length` if given, otherwise the Arrangement's time selection, otherwise the whole set from 1.1.1 to the end of the last clip; it plays straight through, without the Arrangement loop. Below 32 bits, `dither` adds `triangular` noise unless told `rectangular` or `none`. `normalize` brings the highest peak to 0 dBFS. A rate below the engine's is rendered at the engine's and converted down. Files are written under temporary names and appear only when complete. Existing files are refused unless `replace` is true. Playback stops first, and plug-in devices render through the plug-ins the engine plays, lent to the export and handed back afterwards. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The file to write, absolute or relative to the app's working directory, such as `/Music/Mix.wav`. Its folder must exist. |
| `bit_depth` | one of `16`, `24`, `32` | yes | Bits per sample: 16 or 24 (integers), or 32 (floating point; WAV and AIFF only). MP3 has no bit depth, so it ignores this. |
| `sample_rate` | integer from 8000 to 384000 | yes | The file's sample rate in hertz, from 8,000 to 384,000, such as 44100 or 48000. MP3 holds 8,000, 11,025, 12,000, 16,000, 22,050, 24,000, 32,000, 44,100, or 48,000 Hz. |
| `dither` | [`Dither`](#dither) or null | no | The dither below 32 bits. Left out, `triangular`. MP3 ignores it. |
| `file_type` | [`FileType`](#filetype) or null | no | The file type. Left out, the path's extension decides: `.wav`; `.aif` or `.aiff`; `.flac`; `.mp3`. Given, it must agree with the extension. |
| `include_return_and_main_effects` | boolean | no | Include return and Main effects when rendering individual tracks. Unavailable (refused) when `rendered_track` is `main`. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `normalize` | boolean | no | Normalize: raise or lower the whole export so its highest peak is at full scale (0 dBFS). |
| `render_as_loop` | boolean | no | Render as Loop: the song goes on past the range's end as if Stop were pressed there, until the output has stayed below -120 dBFS for 100 ms or 60 s have passed, and that tail is added onto the file's start, wrapping round if it's longer than the range. The file is still exactly the range long. Off unless given. |
| `rendered_track` | [`RenderedTrack`](#renderedtrack) or null | no | Which track(s) to render: `main` (the default), `all_tracks`, `selected_tracks`, or a single track `{ "track": <id> }`. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Replace a file already at `path`. Without it, an existing file is left alone and the export refused. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |

Result: [`ExportResult`](#exportresult).
