#### `focus.previous_neighbor`

**Previous Neighbor**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `tab-focus`.

Moves the keyboard focus from a track's control to the same control on the previous track, the reverse of `focus.next_neighbor`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-014 | `Option+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `tab-focus` | Move to the same control on the previous track (previous neighbour) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `focus.toggle_tab_navigation`

**Use Tab Key to Move Focus**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether Tab and Shift-Tab move the keyboard focus between controls in the main window. While it's off, as it is by default, Tab switches between the Session and Arrangement Views. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `focus.toggle_wrap_navigation`

**Wrap Keyboard Navigation**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether Tab and Shift-Tab wrap round at the ends of the focused area or track: from its last control to its first, and from its first to its last. It's on in a new install, as Live's is; while it's off, they stop at the ends. The Settings window calls it Wrap Tab Navigation. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

### Area `midi`

#### `midi.capture`

**Capture MIDI**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Capture MIDI (Create ▸ Capture MIDI; the Control Bar's button). Brings back the notes played on the MIDI tracks that monitor their input, since the last capture or recording, as one clip on each track that was played, with their velocities and timing. A track with a clip playing while the transport runs gets the notes added to that clip: it grows to the loop pass the last note falls in and its loop moves there, keeping its length. Any other track gets a new clip in the selected scene's slot if it is empty, else the next empty slot below, else a scene added at the end; the clip's loop is the whole bars that cover its last phrase, from the first note-on to the last. With the transport stopped the first note is on 1.1.1 and the song's tempo may change to the played tempo; with it running the tempo stays. Control changes, pitch bend and pressure are not captured yet. Refused when no note was played; `transport.state` shows `capture_midi_ready`. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`Captured`](#captured).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_key`

**Computer Keyboard Key**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Presses or releases one of the computer MIDI keyboard's note keys, as typing it does: a press sends a note-on at the keyboard's velocity on MIDI channel 1, a release the note-off of the note that key started, even if the octave moved meanwhile. The notes reach the tracks whose MIDI From is Computer Keyboard or All Ins. A press fails while the keyboard is off. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The note key's letter: A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P, from the lowest note up. |
| `pressed` | boolean | yes | Whether the key goes down (the note starts) or comes up (it ends). |

Result: [`KeyboardKeyResult`](#keyboardkeyresult).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_octave`

**Computer Keyboard Octave**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the computer MIDI keyboard's octave by `steps`, as Z (down) and X (up) do: 12 semitones a step, from C-2 to C8 for the A key, stopping at the ends. Notes already held keep sounding until their keys come up. Works whether or not the keyboard is on. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer from -16 to 16 | yes | The steps to move: -1 for down (Z, C), 1 for up (X, V). Any number of steps is allowed; it stops at the ends of the range. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_velocity`

**Computer Keyboard Velocity**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Steps the computer MIDI keyboard's velocity by `steps` through 1, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, and 127, as C (lower) and V (raise) do, stopping at the ends. It starts at 100. Works whether or not the keyboard is on. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer from -16 to 16 | yes | The steps to move: -1 for down (Z, C), 1 for up (X, V). Any number of steps is allowed; it stops at the ends of the range. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

#### `midi.export_clip`

**Export MIDI Clip**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Writes a MIDI clip's notes as a type 1 Standard MIDI File at `path`, as the File menu's Export MIDI Clip does: its notes' pitches, starts, lengths and velocities, its tempo (the song's tempo where the clip starts) and its time signature. Fails for an audio clip, or for a file already at `path` unless `replace` is true. Writes a file outside the project; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The MIDI clip to write. |
| `path` | string | yes | The file to write, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Its folder must exist. `.mid` or `.midi` by convention. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Replace a file already at `path`. Without it, an existing file is left alone and the export refused. |

Result: [`MidiExportResult`](#midiexportresult).

#### `midi.import_file`

**Import MIDI File**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or type 1) into the Arrangement, as dragging it in or the Create menu's Import MIDI File does: each of the file's tracks that has notes becomes a MIDI clip. With no `track`, each becomes a new MIDI track below the last one, named as a new track is; with a `track`, the file's one track with notes goes on that MIDI track. Clips start at `at`, or the insert marker. Each clip keeps the file's leading silence, is named after its track's name (or `Track N`), carries the file's time signature, loops its whole length, and lasts from its first note to its last note-off rounded up to a whole bar. With `import_tempo`, the file's tempo and time signature come into the song as Live's "Import tempo and time signature data into Arrangement?" answer Yes does: a single-tempo file sets the song's tempo, a file whose tempo changes writes Song Tempo automation over the clip and restores the tempo at its end, and a time-signature marker is written at the clip's start and one restoring the previous signature at its end. Off (the default), the song's tempo, automation and markers are left alone. A clip placed over part of another replaces that part, so a track never plays two clips at once; when a clip on `track` ends after `at`, it's destructive as well as external. One undo step. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The Standard MIDI File to read, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Its type 0 or type 1 tracks become clips. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where the first clip starts, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). Left out, the Arrangement's insert marker. |
| `import_tempo` | boolean | no | Whether to bring the file's tempo and time signature into the song, as Live's "Import tempo and time signature data into Arrangement?" asks. Off unless given, so an agent never changes the song's tempo by accident. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track to put the file's clips on. Left out, each track of the file with notes gets a new MIDI track below the last one. |

Result: [`MidiImportResult`](#midiimportresult).

#### `midi.ports`

**MIDI Ports**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists every MIDI input and output port the computer offers, each with its Track, Sync, and Remote switches as the Settings window's Tempo & MIDI page shows them, and the computer MIDI keyboard's state. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`MidiPortsResult`](#midiportsresult).

#### `midi.set_port`

**Set MIDI Port**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Changes a MIDI port's Track, Sync, and Remote switches, as the Settings window's MIDI ports table does; switches left out stay as they are. A port is open while any of its switches is on and closed when all are off. An input's notes and controllers reach tracks only while its Track switch is on; Sync and Remote are kept and act when sync and MIDI mapping are built. The port's switches are kept for the next start, and aren't part of the set or an undo step. Opens or closes a device outside Beatlayer. Fails if the computer doesn't offer the port now.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`PortDirection`](#portdirection) | yes | Input or output. |
| `name` | string | yes | The port's name, as `midi.ports` lists it. |
| `remote` | boolean or null | no | Remote on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |
| `sync` | boolean or null | no | Sync on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |
| `track` | boolean or null | no | Track on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |

Result: [`PortInfo`](#portinfo).

#### `midi.toggle_computer_keyboard`

**Computer MIDI Keyboard**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the computer MIDI keyboard, as the Control Bar's switch and M do, to `on`, or to the other state if it's left out. While it's on, the letter keys play notes (A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P) to the tracks whose MIDI From is Computer Keyboard or All Ins; Z and X move its octave, C and V its velocity, and the letters it uses don't run their shortcuts unless Shift is held. Switching it off ends every note it holds. Whether it's on is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-MAP-003 | `M` | `M` | `global` | Turn the computer MIDI keyboard on or off | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch it on or off. Left out, it switches to the other state. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

### Area `mixer`

#### `mixer.arm_exclusive`

**Arm Track Exclusively**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Arms one track and disarms every other track, in one undo step, as a click on an Arm switch does while Exclusive Arm is on (Live's default). Only audio and MIDI tracks can be armed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_arm`

**Arm Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Arms or disarms one track for recording, leaving other tracks' arm switches as they are, so it records its input when recording starts (recording arrives in Phase 2; until then the switch is only saved). Only audio and MIDI tracks can be armed.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-013 | `C` | `C` | `track-headers` | Arm the selected tracks for recording | toggles `arm` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `arm` | boolean | yes | Whether it's armed. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_crossfade_assign`

**Assign Crossfade**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Assigns a track to a side of the crossfader, as its A and B buttons under the mixer's Crossfader section do: `a`, `b`, or `none` (neither, where every track starts). A track's sides are exclusive, so assigning one releases the other; a track assigned to neither plays through at every crossfader position. Every track but Main can be assigned, and Main carries the crossfader itself (`mixer.set_crossfader`). The assignment is saved with the set, and undo releases it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track; every track but Main. |
| `assign` | [`CrossfadeAssign`](#crossfadeassign) | yes | `a`, `b`, or `none`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_crossfader`

**Set Crossfader**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets the Main track's crossfader, as the Crossfader section's fader does. `position` runs from 0 (the A end) through 0.5 (the centre, where a new set starts) to 1 (the B end). Tracks assigned to A and B fade between the two ends on the default Constant Power curve: at the centre each side plays at -3 dB, at either end the near side plays at 0 dB, the far side is silent, and a track assigned to neither plays through at every position. The engine glides to the new position over 20 ms, so a move never clicks. The position is saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | number from 0 to 1 | yes | The position: 0 is the A end, 0.5 the centre, 1 the B end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_cue_mode`

**Cue Switches**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Cue mode, as the Main strip's Solo/Cue button and the Options menu's Solo Switches and Cue Switches do: with `enabled` true, every track's Solo switch becomes a Cue switch (`mixer.set_solo` sets it) that feeds the Cue Out at the Cue Volume (`mixer.set_cue_volume`) instead of silencing the other tracks, and Main plays what the activators leave. A cue-switched track is heard on the Cue Out after its devices and before its volume, pan and activator. It needs a Cue Out that shares no output channel with Main Out (`routing.set_cue_out`, `routing.set_main_out`): turning it on with an overlap is refused, and an overlap made later switches it off in effect. A new set is in Solo mode. The mode is saved with the set and is no undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the Solo switches are Cue switches. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_cue_volume`

**Set Cue Volume**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the Preview/Cue Volume knob on Main's strip, which scales the Cue Out in Cue mode, as a linear gain from 0 (-inf dB) to 1.995 (+6 dB); 1 (0 dB) is where a new set starts. The engine glides to the new value over 20 ms. The volume is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume` | number from 0 to 1.9952623149688795 | yes | The gain: 1 is unity (0 dB, where a new set starts) and 0 silence, up to 1.995 (+6 dB). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_mute`

**Activate/Deactivate Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Switches a track's activator: `mute` true deactivates the track, so its output and its post-fader sends are silent (its pre-fader sends still carry it), and false activates it again. Use it to silence a track without deleting it. Every track but Main has an activator.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-016 | `0` | `0` | `track-headers` | Deactivate the selected track | toggles `mute` |
| S-TRANS-010 | `F1..F8` | `F1..F8` | `global` | Turn track 1 to 8 on or off | toggles `mute` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `mute` | boolean | yes | Whether it's muted. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_pan`

**Set Track Pan**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's pan from -1 (fully left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (fully right). Use it to place a track in the stereo field. Panning keeps the power constant: at the centre both channels pass at 0 dB, and fully to one side that side is 3 dB louder and the other silent.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `pan` | number from -1 to 1 | yes | The pan position, from −1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_send`

**Set Send Level**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets how much of a track's signal its send feeds to the return track `to`, as a linear gain from 0 (-inf dB, where every send starts) to 1 (0 dB). Use it to put a track through a return's effects, such as a shared reverb. Audio, MIDI, and group tracks have a send to every return; the return's Pre/Post switch (`mixer.set_send_tap`) decides whether the send takes the track's signal before or after its pan, volume, and activator.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The sending track. |
| `to` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The return track the send feeds. |
| `level` | number from 0 to 1 | yes | The level: 1 is 0 dB, 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 sends nothing. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_send_tap`

**Set Sends Pre/Post**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a return track's Pre/Post switch, which decides where every send to that return takes its signal from each sending track: `post` (the default) after the track's pan, volume, and activator, so the send follows the fader; `pre` before them, straight after the track's devices, for a mix that ignores the faders, such as a monitor mix. Only return tracks have it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The return track. |
| `tap` | [`SendTap`](#sendtap) | yes | `pre` or `post`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_solo`

**Solo Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Solos or unsolos one track, leaving other tracks' solo switches as they are, as a Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) on a Solo switch does; to solo one track alone, use `mixer.solo_exclusive`. While any track is soloed, only soloed tracks, the groups that hold them, and the tracks inside soloed groups are heard. Return tracks stay audible if Solo in Place is on (`mixer.set_solo_in_place`); soloing a return silences every other track's output but keeps their sends to it. In Cue mode (`mixer.set_cue_mode`) the switch is the track's Cue switch and silences nothing. Every track but Main can be soloed.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-014 | `S` | `S` | `track-headers` | Solo the selected tracks | toggles `solo` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `solo` | boolean | yes | Whether it's soloed. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_solo_in_place`

**Solo in Place**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Solo in Place, the Options menu item. On (the default in a new set), soloing an audio, MIDI, or group track keeps the return tracks audible, so the soloed track is heard with its sends' effects; off, soloing such a track silences the returns too. It doesn't change what soloing a return does. The setting is saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether soloing a track keeps the return tracks audible. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_volume`

**Set Track Volume**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's volume as a linear gain: 1 is unity (0 dB), 0.5 is about -6 dB (10^(dB/20) converts decibels), 2 is about +6 dB, and 0 is silence (-inf dB). Use it to balance tracks; the Main track's volume sets the song's output level. The engine glides to the new level over 20 ms, so a change never clicks. The value must be finite and at least 0.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `volume` | number, at least 0 | yes | The gain: 1 is unity (0 dB), 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 silence. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.solo_exclusive`

**Solo Track Exclusively**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Solos one track and unsolos every other track, in one undo step, as a click on a Solo switch does while Exclusive Solo is on (Live's default). Use it to hear one track on its own. To unsolo, use `mixer.set_solo` with `solo` false. Every track but Main can be soloed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer_view.toggle`

**Mixer**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides the mixer, as View > Mixer and the Status Bar's mixer toggle do: in the Session View under the clip slots, in the Arrangement View under the track lanes, which it splits. Acts on the view in front unless `view` names one; switches unless `shown` says which. Each view keeps its own: a new set shows the Session's and hides the Arrangement's. Changes only the view, and isn't saved with the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-014 | `Cmd+Option+M` | `Ctrl+Alt+M` | `global` | Show or hide the mixer (in the Arrangement) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show it (true) or hide it (false); switches it if left out. |
| `view` | [`MixerOf`](#mixerof) or null | no | Which view's mixer; the view in front if left out. |

Result: [`MixerViewState`](#mixerviewstate).

#### `mixer_view.volume`

**Mixer Volume**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides the mixers' strips (the peak level, pan, the activator, Solo, Arm, the volume fader, and the meter), as View > Mixer Controls > Volume does. Switches unless `shown` says which. Changes only the view; the Arrangement's track headers keep their controls.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show it (true) or hide it (false); switches it if left out. |

Result: [`MixerViewState`](#mixerviewstate).

### Area `modulation`

#### `modulation.state`

**Modulation State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the parameters a track's clips and the modulators act on (all tracks' when `track` is left out): for each, the track and the parameter (a mixer control, a send, or a device's parameter), its base (what its automation, a modulator in Remote Control or its control sets), the value it played in the last block, the clip envelopes modulating it, each with its value at the play position and what it contributes, as a share of the parameter's travel, the modulator slots mapping it (`modulators`), and the modulator that holds it in Remote Control (`held_by`). A clip envelope modulates by a share: 0 to 1 for a volume or a send, which brings its level down to that share, and −1 to 1 for the rest. It reads back `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` and the other clip envelope commands, and `modulator.map`. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track, or every track when left out. |

Result: [`ModulationState`](#modulationstate).

### Area `modulator`

#### `modulator.arm_map`

**Map**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Lights or puts out a modulator slot's Map button, as clicking it does. While one is lit, every parameter in the set that can be mapped is tinted, and clicking one maps it to the slot (`modulator.map`); Esc, or the button again (`armed`: false), puts it out and changes nothing. Lighting a button puts out the one that was lit. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and `device_view.state` reports the lit button in `armed_map`. Only a modulator has slots.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |
| `armed` | boolean or null | no | Arm (true) or disarm (false); switches if left out. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The modulator; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `modulator.map`

**Map Modulator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Maps one of a modulator's slots (`slot`, 0 to 7; the Expression Control's are 0 to 4) to a parameter, as the slot's Map button and a click on the parameter's control do. `target` is a mixer control (`volume`, `pan` or `mute`) or a send of any track, or a parameter of any device on any track, but not a parameter of the modulator itself. The slot's earlier mapping is replaced; one modulator doesn't map one parameter twice. A modulator in Remote Control can't map a parameter another modulator in Remote Control holds. A modulator driven by audio, notes or MIDI (the Envelope Follower, Envelope MIDI, Shaper MIDI and Expression Control) doesn't map another modulator's parameters, nor one on a track that feeds its own track, which would make the two tracks wait on each other. The mapping is saved with the set, goes with its target when that is deleted, and shows in the `mappings` field of the query tool's `device`. One undo step (Map Modulator).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The modulator device. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |
| `target` | [`ModTarget`](#modtarget) | yes | The parameter to map: a mixer control or send of any track, or a parameter of any device but the modulator's own. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `modulator.set_shape`

**Edit Shape**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces the breakpoint shape of a Shaper or a Shaper MIDI, as every edit of its display does (adding, moving, bending or deleting a breakpoint, making one the sustain breakpoint, Clear and the six presets). `points` lists up to 64 breakpoints in order along the cycle, each with `x` (its place, 0 to 1), `y` (the output there, 0 to 1), `bend` (of the segment starting there, from -1 to 1, 0 straight) and `sustain` (true on the Shaper MIDI's sustain breakpoint, at most one in a shape). An empty list outputs 0. One undo step (Edit Shape).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The Shaper device. |
| `points` | array of [`ShapePoint`](#shapepoint) | yes | The breakpoints, in order along the cycle (at most 64), each with its place and output from 0 to 1 and the bend of the segment starting there, from −1 to 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `modulator.unmap`

**Unmap Modulator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Removes the mapping of a modulator's slot (`slot`, 0 to 7; the Expression Control's are 0 to 4), as its Unmap button does: the parameter plays its own value again from the next frame. A slot with no mapping stays as it is. One undo step (Unmap Modulator).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The modulator device. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `note`

#### `note.add`

**Add Note**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Adds a note to a MIDI clip: pitch `key` (0 to 127; 60 is middle C), starting `start` ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, lasting `length` ticks, with `velocity` (1 to 127; 100 unless given). With Draw Mode on, clicking the note area runs this for a note one grid step long. The new note is selected afterwards, and the edit is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pitch, a MIDI key from 0 to 127; 60 is middle C. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the note starts, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents. Never negative. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the note lasts, in ticks. Always positive. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `velocity` | integer or null | no | The velocity, from 1 to 127; 100 unless given. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.delete`

**Delete Notes**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Deletes notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) from a MIDI clip. With Draw Mode on, clicking a note runs this. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first. The edit is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.move`

**Move Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Moves notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) in time by `by` ticks and in pitch by `semitones`, as dragging them in the note editor does; dragging right and left runs it with `semitones` 0, and up and down snap the pitch. Nothing moves if any note would start before the clip's contents or leave the range of MIDI keys 0 to 127. The moved notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far to move them in time, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `semitones`, or both. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |
| `semitones` | integer or null | no | How far to move them in pitch, in semitones; negative is lower. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.quantize`

**Quantize**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Quantises notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) to `grid`: each note moves `amount` percent of the way from its start (or its end, with `target` `note_end`) to the nearest grid line, so 100 percent lands it on the line and 50 percent halves its distance to it. The lines are laid out from each bar's start, as the note editor's grid is, and a spacing of whole bars counts bars from 1.1.1. `grid`, `target`, and `amount` left out use the Clip View's Quantize settings (`clip_view.quantize_settings`), which follow the note editor's editing grid until a grid is set. Quantising is one undo step, and the quantised notes stay selected.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-011 | `Cmd+U` | `Ctrl+U` | `note-editor` | Quantise the selected notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer or null | no | How far each note moves toward its grid line, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The grid line spacing in ticks, over the Quantize settings. Lines are laid out from each bar's start, as the editing grid's are; a spacing of whole bars counts bars from 1.1.1. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |
| `target` | [`QuantizeTarget`](#quantizetarget) or null | no | What to move toward the grid. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.ramp_value`

**Ramp Note Values**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Sets one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) as a ramp, as dragging across several notes in the Clip View's lane does: the first note in the clip's order takes `from`, the last takes `to`, and those between take values evenly spaced between them (whole numbers for the whole-number fields). `field` takes the same fields and ranges as `note.set_value`; nothing changes if `from` or `to` is out of range. One note takes `from`. The edited notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to ramp. |
| `from` | number | yes | The value the first note takes. |
| `to` | number | yes | The value the last note takes. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.resize`

**Resize Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Moves notes' ends (`notes`, or the selected notes) by `by` ticks, as dragging a note's end in the note editor does: a positive `by` makes them longer, a negative one shorter, and every note keeps at least one tick of length. A note's start doesn't move. The resized notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How far each note's end moves, in ticks; negative is shorter. A note keeps at least one tick of length. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.set_value`

**Set Note Value**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Sets one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) to `value`, as dragging a note's stem in the Clip View's lane does: `field` is `velocity` (whole numbers 1 to 127), `release_velocity` (whole numbers 1 to 127), `chance` (0 to 1), or `velocity_deviation` (whole numbers -127 to 127). Nothing changes if `value` is outside the field's range. The edited notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to set. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value, within the field's range. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

### Area `pad`

#### `pad.delete`

**Delete Pad**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes the chains on a pad, with their devices and automation: one undo step (Delete Chain). Undo restores them, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.drop`

**Drop on Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Drops what the browser drags onto a pad. One audio file in `samples` on an empty pad makes a chain on its note holding the sampler with the file loaded (or a chain made from the pad default that Save as Default Pad saved), named after the file; on a pad with a chain it replaces the chain's sampler and sample and keeps its effects. Several files go one to a pad, rising a note each from `note` (those past note 127 are left out), or with `layer` onto that one pad as an instrument rack with a chain per file. A `device` or `preset` goes at the end of the pad's chain if it is an audio effect, at the end of its MIDI effects if it is a MIDI effect, and in place of its instrument if it is an instrument; on an empty pad each makes a chain holding it. A pad of several chains takes no drop. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note; with several samples, the first of the pads they rise from. |
| `device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) or null | no | A device to drop, as `device.add` describes one. |
| `layer` | boolean | no | With several samples, layer them on this one pad (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux) rather than spread them over pads. |
| `move_device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | A device to move onto the pad from where it is. |
| `preset` | string or null | no | A preset file to drop. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |
| `samples` | array of string | no | Audio files: one goes on the pad, several on pads rising from it. |

Result: [`PadDropped`](#paddropped).

#### `pad.hot_swap`

**Hot-Swap Pad**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Makes a pad the target of hot-swap, as its Hot-Swap button does, or ends it: loading an item from the browser then lands on the pad as dropping it would (`pad.drop`). It ends the hot-swap of a device or a chain. Only a pad of one chain, or an empty one, can be the target. It changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping the pad; switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.hot_swap_sample`

**Hot-Swap Sample**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

A pad's Hot-Swap Sample button: it makes the pad the hot-swap target and opens the folder of the sample its chain plays in the browser, so loading a sample replaces the pad's (one undo step each). Pressing it again, the hot-swap bar's close button, Esc, Q, or going from the browser to another view ends it. Only a pad whose chain plays a sample has one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping the pad; switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.preview`

**Preview Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Holds a pad's Preview button, or lets it go: while it is held each of the pad's chains plays its Receive note into itself alone at velocity 100 (C3 for a chain on All Notes), through the rest of the track's chain and its mixer, whether or not the song plays. A press with no release plays until the release, so an agent that presses must release. It changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Press (true) or release (false) the Preview button. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.rename`

**Rename Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames the chain of a pad that holds one chain: an empty name gives it the name a chain has without one. A pad of several chains can't be renamed. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name; empty gives the name a chain has without one. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.save_default`

**Save as Default Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves the pad's chain as the default pad: a sample dropped on an empty pad afterwards makes its chain from that default, with the sample in the first sampler. The one saved last is used. A pad of one chain only. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.select`

**Select Pad**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a pad, as clicking it does, and its chains in the chain list, so the devices view shows them. The selected pad is the one D switches hot-swap to. It changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.set_mute`

**Mute Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Mutes a pad, or unmutes it: it switches off the Chain Activator of each of the pad's chains (a pad of several chains mutes them all, and a mixed pad mutes the rest). One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn it on (true) or off (false); switches if left out, a mixed pad turning on. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.set_solo`

**Solo Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Solos a pad, or unsolos it: it sets the Solo of each of the pad's chains, and leaves every other chain's as it is. While any drum chain is soloed the rack's return chains stay audible carrying only the soloed chains' sends. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn it on (true) or off (false); switches if left out, a mixed pad turning on. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.swap`

**Swap Pads**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Drags one pad onto another: each pad's chains take the other pad's note as their Receive, so the set's clips play the other sound. With `layer` (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux) both pads' chains are layered on `to` as one chain holding an instrument rack of them, and `from` is left empty. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad dragged. |
| `to` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad it's dropped on. |
| `layer` | boolean | no | Layer both pads' chains on `to` instead (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux). |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `perception`

#### `perception.analyze`

**Analyze Audio**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Measures audio and reports numbers with units: loudness (integrated, momentary and short-term LUFS, loudness range in LU, true peak in dBTP, as ITU-R BS.1770-4 and EBU R 128 define them), sample peak and RMS in dBFS, the level in each octave band from 31.5 Hz to 16 kHz, the tempo in BPM, the key, and when transients start. Give `preview` to measure a preview, or a range (`start`, `length`, and `track`, as for `perception.preview`) to render one for the analysis, up to ten minutes. `measure` picks what to measure; left out, everything. Tempo and key are estimates from the audio, not the set's settings. A range renders as `perception.preview` does, refused likewise while the transport plays a set with a CLAP plug-in. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note, so a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `measure` | array or null | no | What to measure. Left out, everything. |
| `preview` | integer or null | no | A preview to analyse, by the ID `perception.preview` gave. Left out, the range below is rendered for the analysis (up to ten minutes). |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Without `preview`: where the range starts, as ticks from 1.1.1 or bar.beat.sixteenth text such as `"9.1.1"`. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | One track to hear on its own, as it sounds soloed: through its group tracks and the Main track, with the returns its sends reach while Solo in Place is on. Left out, the whole mix: the Main output. |

Result: [`AnalyzeResult`](#analyzeresult).

#### `perception.capture_view`

**Capture View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Captures one of the app's views as a PNG image, as the person sees it, for a model that reads images: the whole `window`, the `arrangement` or `session` view, the `mixer`, the `browser`, the `detail` area (Clip or Device View), or the `settings` window. The view must be on screen. The image is scaled to fit `max_size` pixels. Only the agent API's `capture_view` tool returns the image, and only while the app's window is open: headless (`bl-cli mcp`) there's no window to capture. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | [`View`](#view) | yes | The view to capture. It must be on screen: the main window shows the Arrangement or the Session View, and the browser, the mixer, and the Settings window only while they're open. |
| `max_size` | integer or null | no | The longest side of the image, in pixels, from 256 to 4,096: a larger capture is scaled down to fit. Left out, 1,568. |

Result: [`CaptureResult`](#captureresult).

#### `perception.preview`

**Preview Audio**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Renders a short audio preview of a range of the set, offline, through the engine that exports, and keeps it as a WAV file for you to listen to: the agent API's `preview` tool returns it as audio, and `uri` reads it as a resource. The range is `start` and `length` if given, otherwise the Arrangement's time selection, otherwise the whole set; it plays straight through, without the loop, and is cut to its first 30 seconds. `track` previews one track as it sounds soloed; left out, the whole mix. 16-bit stereo at 48 kHz is about 190 KB a second: a lower `sample_rate` makes it smaller. Plug-in devices render through the plug-ins the engine plays, lent to the render, so while the transport plays a set with a CLAP plug-in the preview is refused (run `transport.stop` first); otherwise rendering doesn't stop or disturb playback. The last 4 previews are kept, for `perception.analyze`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bit_depth` | one of `16`, `24`, `32` | no | Bits per sample: 16 (the default, with triangular dither), 24, or 32 (floating point). |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note, so a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | no | The preview's sample rate in hertz, from 8,000 to 192,000. Left out, the engine's rate. A lower rate makes a smaller file. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts: ticks from 1.1.1, or bar.beat.sixteenth text such as `"9.1.1"`. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | One track to hear on its own, as it sounds soloed: through its group tracks and the Main track, with the returns its sends reach while Solo in Place is on. Left out, the whole mix: the Main output. |

Result: [`PreviewResult`](#previewresult).

### Area `plugin`

#### `plugin.info`

**Plug-In Info**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports what a plug-in device's plug-in is doing: its ID and file, whether it's running, the latency it reports in frames, what went wrong if anything, whether its editor window can open, is open, and is shown (a hidden window stays open), and its parameters' values as it reports them. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

#### `plugin.list`

**List Plug-Ins in the Set**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists every plug-in the set uses, grouped by plug-in: its format, its identifier, name, the file the set says it came from, its vendor and version when the scanner knows them, the devices and tracks that use it, and whether this machine has it (missing when the scanner hasn't seen it, or says why it is blocklisted). Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetPluginList`](#setpluginlist).

#### `plugin.load`

**Load Plug-In**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Loads a plug-in from its file or bundle (`path`: a `.clap` file, or a `.vst3` bundle or module) and adds it as a device, as `device.add` adds one: to the selected track (or `track`), at `index` or where its role goes, selected, one undo step (Insert Device). `plugin` picks one of the file's plug-ins by its ID (CLAP's, or a VST3 class ID); the first if left out. Its parameters become the device's, which `device.parameters` lists and `device.set_param` and automation change. The plug-in's code runs inside Beatlayer, so load only plug-ins you trust. The scanner (`plugin.scan`) lists the plug-ins on this machine; this command still loads one by its path.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The plug-in's file or bundle (`.clap`, or `.vst3` for VST3). |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; as `device.add` places it if left out. |
| `plugin` | string or null | no | Which of the file's plug-ins, by its ID; the first if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`PluginLoaded`](#pluginloaded).

#### `plugin.load_au`

**Load Audio Unit**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Loads the Audio Unit with the given component description — its `type`, `subtype`, and `manufacturer`, four characters each, such as Apple's `aufx`, `dely`, `appl` for AUDelay — and adds it as a device, as `device.add` adds one: to the selected track (or `track`), at `index` or where its role goes, selected, one undo step (Insert Device). Its parameters become the device's, which `device.parameters` lists and `device.set_param` and automation change; its own state is saved with the set. Audio Units are macOS only: on Windows and Linux this fails with that reason. Its own editor window opens from `plugin.show_window`, as a CLAP plug-in's does, and a change made in it is one undo step. The unit's code runs inside Beatlayer, so load only units you trust.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | The component's type, four characters: `aufx` for an effect, `aumu` or `augn` for an instrument, `aumi` for a MIDI effect. |
| `subtype` | string | yes | The component's subtype, four characters, such as `dely` for Apple's AUDelay. |
| `manufacturer` | string | yes | The component's manufacturer, four characters, such as `appl` for Apple's units. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; as `device.add` places it if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`PluginLoaded`](#pluginloaded).

#### `plugin.rescan`

**Rescan Plug-Ins**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Scans the plug-ins in `paths` (or each format's system plug-in folders) again, ignoring the cache and clearing the blocklist for them, as the Rescan button does. Returns `plugin.scan`'s report; with `background`, returns at once and the browser lists what was found when the scan is done.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | boolean | no | Scan the system folders in the background and return at once, with an empty report, as the Settings window's Rescan button does; the browser lists what was found when it's done. |
| `paths` | array or null | no | The files or folders to scan; each format's system plug-in folders if left out. |

Result: [`PluginScan`](#pluginscan).

#### `plugin.scan`

**Scan Plug-Ins**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Finds the plug-ins installed on this machine and describes each one: its format, its file, its identifier, name, vendor, version, and role in a chain. Scans the files or folders in `paths` for every hosted format, or, when `paths` is left out, the system plug-in folders of CLAP and of the formats the Plug-Ins settings switch on (`plugin.settings`: `vst3_system_folders`, and on macOS `use_audio_units_v2`). The app also runs this at start, in the background, and when one of those switches turns on. Each one is loaded in a separate process with a timeout, so a plug-in that crashes or hangs is put on a blocklist with the reason instead of taking Beatlayer down; a file whose size and modification time are unchanged is answered from the cache. Reads plug-in files outside the project, so an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | boolean | no | Scan the system folders in the background and return at once, with an empty report, as the Settings window's Rescan button does; the browser lists what was found when it's done. |
| `paths` | array or null | no | The files or folders to scan; each format's system plug-in folders if left out. |

Result: [`PluginScan`](#pluginscan).

#### `plugin.set_panel_param`

**Set Plug-In Panel Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets which of a plug-in device's own parameters a panel knob shows (D19): `index` is the knob, 0 for the first and up to seven, and `param` the parameter, or null to restore the knob to the plug-in's parameter at that place. The mapping is remembered per plug-in, so another device of the same plug-in keeps it, and it changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. Returns the Device View's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The knob, 0 for the first (leftmost) and up to [`PANEL_KNOBS`] − 1. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) or null | no | The parameter it shows, from the plug-in's own; `null` restores the knob to the plug-in's parameter at that place. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `plugin.set_window`

**Set Plug-In Window Place**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Records where a plug-in device's editor window sits and how big it is, in points (`frame`): its place is saved with the set beside the document, so moving or resizing a window is never an undo step. A plug-in window reopens where it was left. Returns `plugin.info`'s report.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | [`WindowFrame`](#windowframe) | yes | Where its window sits and how big it is, in points. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

#### `plugin.settings`

**Plug-In Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads or changes how the browser shows plug-ins (IMP-07): `hidden` is the plug-ins to hide, as `format/plugin_id` keys; `show_hidden` whether hidden plug-ins still show; and `format_preference` the format to prefer when a plug-in exists in several. Also the Plug-In Sources switches of Settings ▸ Plug-Ins: `use_audio_units_v2`, `use_audio_units_v3` and `vst3_system_folders`, all off in a new install; the browser lists a format's plug-ins only while its switch is on (CLAP has none and is always listed), and turning one on scans that format in the background. Fields left out are unchanged. Returns the settings. A set that uses a hidden plug-in still loads it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format_preference` | [`PluginFormat`](#pluginformat) or null | no | The format to prefer when a plug-in exists in several. |
| `hidden` | array or null | no | The hidden plug-ins to remember, as `format/plugin_id` keys (IMP-07); empty hides none. |
| `show_hidden` | boolean or null | no | Whether the browser shows hidden plug-ins. |
| `use_audio_units_v2` | boolean or null | no | Use Audio Units v2 (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins): scan and list Audio Units on macOS. Turning it on scans them. |
| `use_audio_units_v3` | boolean or null | no | Use Audio Units v3 (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins). Kept; app-extension Audio Units aren't scanned yet. |
| `vst3_system_folders` | boolean or null | no | Use VST3 Plug-In System Folders (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins): scan and list the VST3 plug-ins in the format's system folders. Turning it on scans them. |

Result: [`PluginSettings`](#pluginsettings).

#### `plugin.show_window`

**Show Plug-In Window**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Opens or closes a plug-in device's editor, as the device's title bar button does; switches unless `shown` says which. On Windows and Linux the editor opens in a window Beatlayer owns, with the plug-in's own view embedded into it; on macOS, and for a plug-in that won't embed, in a floating window of the plug-in's own. An open window follows View ▸ Plug-In Windows and Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, which hide and show it without closing it. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. Returns `plugin.info`'s report.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Open (true) or close (false) the window; switches if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

### Area `rack`

#### `rack.move_pads`

**Move the Pads**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves the sixteen notes a drum rack's pad view shows (the rack in focus, or `rack`): to `first` (a note, rounded down to a row), or by `groups` of sixteen notes and `rows` of four from where it is, as dragging the overview's selector, or Up and Down with Cmd (Alt on Windows and Linux) for a row, do. The view stays within notes 0 to 127. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which notes show (`device_view.state`, the rack's `pads.first`).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first` | integer or null | no | Show the sixteen notes from here (rounded down to a row); the view moves by `groups` and `rows` from where it is if left out. |
| `groups` | integer or null | no | How many groups of sixteen notes to move up (positive) or down. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |
| `rows` | integer or null | no | How many rows of four notes to move up or down. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.set_auto_select`

**Auto Select**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a rack's Auto Select, the selected device's or `rack`'s: while it is on, the chain list selects every chain that is processing, which the engine publishes after each block: in an instrument or MIDI effect rack each chain a held note reached, in an audio effect rack each chain whose chain select zone holds the chain selector's value. The devices view follows. It changes only the view: neither the switch nor the selections it makes are undo steps, and the set keeps the switch.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch on (true) or off (false); switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.set_view`

**Show or Hide a Rack's View**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides one of the views of a rack, the selected device or `rack`: the Macro Controls, the chain list (View > Show Chains and Hide Chains) or the selected chain's devices. With every view hidden the rack folds into its view column. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which views each rack shows.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-012 | `Plus` | `Plus` | `device-view` | Show the selected rack's chain list | fixes `shown` = `true`; fixes `view` = `"chain_list"` |
| S-DEV-013 | `Minus` | `Minus` | `device-view` | Hide the selected rack's chain list | fixes `shown` = `false`; fixes `view` = `"chain_list"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | [`RackView`](#rackview) | yes | The view. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.set_zone_editor`

**Show a Rack's Zone Editor**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows the zone editor of a rack, the selected device or `rack`, beside its chain list: `editor` is `key` (the Key button), `velocity` (Vel) or `select` (Chain); an audio effect rack has only `select`, and a drum rack none. Leaving `editor` out, or null, hides it (Hide). It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which editor each rack shows.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) or null | no | The editor to show: `key`, `velocity` (the Vel button) or `select` (the Chain button). None, or left out, is Hide. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.switch_hot_swap_target`

**Switch Hot-Swap Target**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

While a drum rack is being hot-swapped, switches the target between the rack and the rack's last selected pad, as D does; with a pad the target an item loaded from the browser lands on the pad. It changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-007 | `D` | `D` | `global` | Switch between a Drum Rack and its last selected pad | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `routing`

#### `routing.set_cue_out`

**Set Cue Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets Main's Cue Out, the audio interface's output channels the cue mix goes to, as Main's In/Out section does: `channel` is a stereo pair of the interface's outputs, counted from 1; the default is the first pair, 1/2. It carries the cue mix once cue mode is built (a later package); the choice is kept and saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | [`Channel`](#channel) | yes | The pair: its first channel, counted from 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_input`

**Set Input**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where an audio or MIDI track takes its input from, as the In/Out section's Audio From or MIDI From chooser and its channel do. An audio track can take `external` (Ext. In, the audio interface's inputs, with a `channel`: a single channel (`{ "type": "mono", "channel": 3 }`) or a stereo pair (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }`, the pair 3/4), counted from 1), `resampling` (the Main output, for recording the mix; the track's own output and sends are then silent so it can't feed back), `none`, or `track` with another audio track, a group, a return track, or Main and a `tap`: `pre_fx` (before its devices), `post_fx` (after its devices, before its mixer), or `post_mixer` (its output, the default). A MIDI track can take `all_ins` (every MIDI input whose Track switch is on in the settings, and the computer MIDI keyboard), `computer_keyboard`, `port` with the port's `name` as the MIDI settings list it, `none`, or another MIDI track (which carries MIDI once MIDI playback is built). `channel` is 1 to 16 to take only that channel, or null (the default) for All Channels; only a port input has one. The input is heard only while the track monitors it (`routing.set_monitor`). A routing may make a loop, as in Live; the engine plays the routing that closes it as silence.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | yes | The input. |
| `channel` | integer or null | no | The MIDI channel to take, 1 to 16, or `null` (or nothing) for All Channels. Only a MIDI port input has a channel. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_main_out`

**Set Main Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets Main's Main Out, the audio interface's output channels the Main mix goes to, as Main's In/Out section does: `channel` is a stereo pair of the interface's outputs (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is the pair 3/4), counted from 1. The default is the first pair, 1/2.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | [`Channel`](#channel) | yes | The pair: its first channel, counted from 1 (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is 3/4). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_midi_output`

**Set MIDI Output**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where a MIDI track's MIDI goes, as its MIDI To chooser does: another MIDI track (give its ID; it arrives at its Track In), an output port (`{ "name": "Synth", "channel": 1 }`: the port's name as `midi.ports` lists it, with its Track switch on, and the channel to send on, 1 to 16), or `null` for No Output (a new MIDI track's). A track sends to a port the notes and controller, pitch bend and pressure messages that reach the end of its device chain (a track with an instrument sends none, the instrument playing them), at the moment their frame is heard at the audio interface's output; it keeps a missing port's name and sends again when the port returns. Choosing a port takes channel 1.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The MIDI track. |
| `to` | [`MidiTo`](#midito) or null | no | Another MIDI track (its ID), an output port with its channel (`{ "name": "Synth", "channel": 1 }`), or `null` (or nothing) for No Output. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_monitor`

**Set Monitor**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets an audio or MIDI track's Monitor switch: `in` always plays the track's input through its devices and silences its clips, `auto` plays the input while the track is armed, and `off` never plays it. A new track is `auto`. Use `in` to hear another track routed into this one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `monitor` | [`Monitor`](#monitor) | yes | `in`, `auto`, or `off`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_output`

**Set Output**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where a track's audio goes, as the In/Out section's Audio To chooser does: `default` (Main, or the group the track is in), `main` (Main, even from inside a group), `track` with another audio track (its input, heard while that track monitors it) or the track's own group, `sends_only` (only through its sends to the return tracks), or `external` (Ext. Out: the track plays on the audio interface's output channels, a single channel or a stereo pair, the first pair by default, and not into Main). Audio, group, and return tracks take any of these. A routing may make a loop, as in Live; the engine then plays the routing that closes the loop as silence.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `output` | [`Output`](#output) | yes | The output. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `scene`

#### `scene.create`

**Insert Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Inserts a new empty scene at `index` among the scenes, as Create ▸ Insert Scene (Cmd+I) does: it holds an empty slot in every audio and MIDI track. A new set opens with eight scenes. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The new scene's ID. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes among the scenes, from 0 to the number of scenes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.delete`

**Delete Scene**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `session`.

Deletes a scene, and the clips in its slots with it; the clips in the other scenes stay. Undo restores everything it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.duplicate`

**Duplicate Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Copies a scene and the clips in its slots into a new scene directly after it, as Edit ▸ Duplicate does. `clips` lists every track that holds a clip in the scene, each with the new ID its copy takes; each copy is an independent clip. A scene whose slots are all empty copies no clips. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `id` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The new scene's ID. |
| `clips` | array of pair of [`TrackId`](#trackid) and [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | Each track that holds a clip in the scene, with the new ID its copy takes, each track once. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.move`

**Move Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Moves a scene to `index` among the scenes, with the clips in its slots, as dragging a scene does. The index counts positions after the scene is taken out of its current place, so moving a scene down past its neighbour is its current index plus one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes among the scenes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.rename`

**Rename Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Renames a scene. A name may be empty: a scene without a name shows its number, which is its position.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.set_follow_actions`

**Set Scene Follow Actions**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Changes a scene's follow actions, as the Scene View does: what the scene does after it was launched, over the scenes as a clip's do over its track's slots. `enabled` is the Follow Action switch; `action_a` and `action_b` are one of `no_action`, `stop`, `play_again`, `previous`, `next`, `first`, `last`, `any`, `other` and `jump`; `chance_a` is action A's chance in whole percent, 0 to 100, and action B has the rest; `jump_a` and `jump_b` are the slot (scene) numbers Jump goes to, 1 up to the number of scenes, and 0 for none, where Jump stops the scene; `linked` is Longest (on by default): the follow time is the multiplier times the scene's longest clip; off: `time`; `multiplier` is the Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1; and `time` is the Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth (a bar is 2822400 ticks in 4/4). Fields left out stay as they are, and a number past its limit is held at the limit. One undo step. The defaults are off, A Next, B No Action, 100 %, Linked, 1x, one bar. While the song plays the action runs when the follow time has passed after the scene started, and the global switch (`session.set_follow_actions_enabled`) must be on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `action_a` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) or null | no | Action A. |

| `multiplier` | integer or null | no | The Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1. |
| `time` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.set_tempo`

Gives a scene a tempo, from 20 to 999 BPM, that launching the scene sets for the set, as the Tempo field in the Main column and the Scene View does. `tempo` left out or null switches the scene's tempo off, as double-clicking the field or Return to Default does, so launching it leaves the set's tempo as it is. One undo step.

Gives a scene a time signature that launching the scene sets for the set, as the Signature field in the Main column and the Scene View does: a numerator from 1 to 99 over a denominator of 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. `signature` left out or null switches the scene's signature off, so launching it leaves the set's signature as it is.
