### Area `session`

#### `session.back_to_arrangement`

**Back to Arrangement**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns every track to the Arrangement, as the Back to Arrangement button and F10 do. A Session clip that started has taken its track over from the Arrangement, and stays so after it stops, until this runs. It stops every track's Session clips at once, not on the launch quantisation grid, and drops launches and stops still queued; the Arrangement plays again from the playhead and the transport keeps running. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-009 | `F10` | `F10` | `global` | Return every track to the Arrangement (Back to Arrangement) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.back_to_arrangement_track`

**Back to Arrangement (Track)**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns one track to the Arrangement, as the button in the track's Arrangement header does: its Session clip stops at once, a launch or a stop still queued on it is dropped, and its Arrangement clips play again from the playhead. Other tracks are not touched, and the transport keeps running. A track nothing took over just keeps playing its Arrangement. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.capture_and_insert_scene`

**Capture and Insert Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Inserts a new scene holding copies of the clips that are playing, each in its own track's slot, as Create > Capture and Insert Scene (Cmd-Shift-I, Ctrl-Shift-I) does, and the playing clips carry on in the copies without a break. The scene goes after the scene launched last, or after the selected scene when none has been launched since the set opened, and its tempo and time signature are set to the ones in force now. With nothing playing it inserts an empty scene with the same tempo and signature, and launches nothing. One undo step. The playing clips are the engine's, so it needs an engine that runs.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

**Copy Clip to Slot**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Copies a clip into a track's Session slot at `scene`, as Option-dragging (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) a clip between slots does. The target slot must be empty and the clip's data must match the track. The copy gets its own ID. One undo step.

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.create_follow_action_chain`

**Create Follow Action Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Chains the selected slots' clips, as the clip menu's Create Follow Action Chain (Cmd+Shift+Enter) does, a chain for each track in scene order: every clip gets Follow Action on, A Next at 100 %, B No Action and Linked 1x, so each launches the one after it when it ends. Where the next clip of the selection isn't the next slot, the clip gets A Jump to its slot instead, and the last clip jumps to the first, so the chain loops within the selection. Loop switches don't change. One undo step.

#### `session.launch`

**Launch Clip**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches the clip in a track's Session slot at `scene`, as clicking the slot's launch button does. While the song plays the clip starts on the next line of the global launch quantisation grid, and until then the slot reads `queued`; while it's stopped the transport starts at once from the Arrangement position and the clip starts with it. A clip already playing on that track stops where the new one starts. The clip's launch mode (`clip.set_launch_mode`) says what the press does next: a Trigger, Gate or Repeat clip that already plays restarts on the grid, and a Toggle clip that plays is queued to stop. A Gate or Repeat clip stops when `session.release` follows. The engine publishes the slots' states with the playhead, so the UI can draw them. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.launch_scene`

**Launch Scene**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches every clip of the scene at `scene`, as clicking the scene's launch button does: all of them start on one line of the launch quantisation grid, as one launch, so a scene's clips play together. While the song is stopped the transport starts at once. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.launch_selected`

**Launch the Selected Clips and Scenes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches every selected slot that holds a clip and every selected scene, as Enter does in the Session View: each runs `session.launch` or `session.launch_scene`, so it waits for the launch quantisation grid while the song plays and starts the transport at once while it's stopped. A selected empty slot is skipped. Select a slot or a scene first. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-001 | `Enter` | `Enter` | `session` | Launch the selected clip, slot or scene | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.overdub`

**Overdub Slot**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `session`.

Records the notes an armed MIDI track plays into the MIDI clip that is playing in the slot (`track`, `scene`), a loop pass at a time: each pass adds its notes to the clip and is one undo step. A clip that does not loop overdubs until it ends. Launch the clip first; audio clips are never overdubbed. Ends like any recording: `session.stop_recording`, or `session.record` again, which pauses the overdub while the clip plays on. Recording captures input devices, so the person is asked first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.record`

**Record to Session**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `session`.

The Session Record button (Playback ▸ Record to Session, Cmd+Shift+F9; Ctrl+Shift+F9 on Windows and Linux). Records every armed track into the Session View: a MIDI track whose clip is playing overdubs it, one note pass at a time; any other armed track records a new clip into the selected scene's slot if it is empty, else into the next empty slot below it on that track, and a scene is inserted at the end when there is none. The recording starts on the next line of the launch quantisation grid while the song plays, and from the playhead, after any count-in, while it is stopped, which starts the transport. The clip exists from the start and grows as it records. While a recording is under way the command ends it instead, as pressing the button again does: the new clips play on as loops from the next grid line. Audio goes to the project's Samples/Recorded/; the set must have been saved. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first. To end a recording without asking, run `session.stop_recording`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-012 | `Cmd+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `session` | Record into the Session View | runs it |
| S-TRANS-008 | `Cmd+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `global` | Record into the Session View | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.record_slot`

**Record into Slot**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `session`.

The Clip Record button in an empty slot of an armed track: records a new clip into that slot (`track`, `scene`), starting on the next grid line, or from the playhead with the transport stopped. The track must be armed and the slot empty: a slot with a clip has a launch button instead, which `session.launch` presses. The clip exists from the start and grows as it records; `session.launch` on the recording slot, or `session.stop_recording`, ends the recording and loops the clip, and `session.stop_track` ends it without looping. Audio goes to the project's Samples/Recorded/. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.release`

**Release Clip Launch Button**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Ends the press that `session.launch` began on the slot at `track` and `scene`, as letting go of the slot's launch button does. A clip in Gate mode stops on the next line of its launch quantisation grid, or at once with quantisation off, and a Repeat clip stops the same way after the quantum it is playing; a release never cancels a launch still queued, so the clip plays one quantum before it stops. A Trigger or Toggle clip ignores the release, and so does a slot that isn't playing. The clip's mode is read at the release. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: nothing (`null`).
