#### `session.stop_track`

**Stop Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Stops the clip the track plays, as the track's stop button in the status row does: it stops on the next line of the launch quantisation grid, and until then the slot reads `queued to stop`. A launch still queued on the track is dropped, and the transport keeps playing. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.toggle_follow_actions`

**Toggle Follow Actions**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Switches the Follow Action switch of the selected slots' clips on, or off when they are all on already, as Shift+Enter does: with some on and some off, they all go on. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-013 | `Shift+Enter` | `Shift+Enter` | `session` | Turn follow actions on or off for the selected clips | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.triplet_quantization`

**Triplet Launch Quantization**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Makes the global launch quantisation the triplet of its note value, or the plain value again: 1/2 and 1/2T, 1/4 and 1/4T, 1/8 and 1/8T, 1/16 and 1/16T. `none` and the bar counts have no triplet, so it changes nothing while one of them is set. Cmd+3 with the Session View focused, and Options ▸ Triplet Launch Quantization. Saved with the set, and no undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-026 | `Cmd+3` | `Ctrl+3` | `session` | Toggle triplet launch quantisation | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

### Area `set`

#### `set.collect_all_and_save`

**Collect All and Save**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Copies every file the open set uses that lives outside its project folder into the project's `Samples/Imported` folder, re-points the set's media table at the copies, and saves the set, as File ▸ Collect All and Save does in Live, so the set no longer depends on files elsewhere. Fails if the set has never been saved; use `set.save_as` to give it a project folder first. The result's `files` is how many files were copied.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`FileReport`](#filereport).

#### `set.discard_changes`

**Don't Save**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Throws away the open set's unsaved changes, as choosing Don't Save when asked to save does: the set goes back to how it was when it was last opened or saved (a set never saved goes back to the factory default set), and its undo history is cleared. The changes can't be brought back. Nothing on disk changes. Does nothing if there are no unsaved changes.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.discard_recovery`

**Discard Recovery**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Declines to recover a set that `set.list_recoverable` lists, the one with `id` or the newest: its unsaved edits are removed from beside the set, so it isn't offered again, and a copy of its journal is kept in the recovery folder's Discarded folder for seven days. Its set file is untouched.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string or null | no | The recoverable set's `id`, as `set.list_recoverable` gives it. Leave it out for the newest. |

Result: [`DiscardedRecovery`](#discardedrecovery).

#### `set.list_recoverable`

**List Recoverable Sets**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists the sets that Beatlayer, here or in an earlier run, stopped without closing (a crash, a forced quit, a power cut) while they had unsaved edits. Each has an `id` for `set.recover` or `set.discard_recovery`, its file (null if it had never been saved), how many edits followed its last save, and when the last was made. Sets open in another running instance aren't listed. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`RecoverableSets`](#recoverablesets).

#### `set.new`

**New Beatlayer Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the open set with the factory default set: four tracks (two MIDI, two audio) and two return tracks, shown in the Arrangement View. Unsaved changes to the open set are lost, and its undo history is cleared, so save first if they matter.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-001 | `Cmd+N` | `Ctrl+N` | `global` | Create a new set | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.open`

**Open Beatlayer Set...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens the set file at `path` (or the only set in the project folder at `path`), replacing the open set and clearing its undo history. It refuses while the open set has unsaved changes: save them first with `set.save` or `set.save_as`, or throw them away with `set.discard_changes`, so losing work is always its own step. A person choosing the menu item or pressing the shortcut is asked whether to save, then picks the file in a dialog.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-002 | `Cmd+O` | `Ctrl+O` | `global` | Open a set | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The set file's path, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.recover`

**Recover Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens a set that `set.list_recoverable` lists, the one with `id` or the newest, exactly as it was after its last journalled edit. It replaces the open set, whose undo history is cleared; if the open set had unsaved edits they're kept for recovery in turn. The recovered set is unsaved: use `set.save` to keep it in its file, or `set.save_as`. Use it when the user wants back the work a crash interrupted.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string or null | no | The recoverable set's `id`, as `set.list_recoverable` gives it. Leave it out for the newest. |

Result: [`RecoveredSet`](#recoveredset).

#### `set.relink_missing`

**Relink Missing Files**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Searches for the files the open set uses that are missing or changed, and relinks each one to the first file found with the same content, as Live's automatic search does. The search covers the set's project folder, the User Library, the folders the files were last in, and any `folders` given, each with its subfolders. The result's `files` is how many files were relinked. It also runs by itself when a set is opened.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `folders` | array of string | no | Folders to search, each with its subfolders, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. May be empty. |

Result: [`FileReport`](#filereport).

#### `set.save`

**Save Beatlayer Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the set to its file, replacing the file's previous contents, which are kept in the `Backup` folder of the set's project folder (the last 10 saves). Fails if the set has never been saved; use `set.save_as` to give it a file and a project folder first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-003 | `Cmd+S` | `Ctrl+S` | `global` | Save the set | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as`

**Save Beatlayer Set As...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the set under a new name or in a new place, always inside a project folder, and that file becomes the set's. `path` gives a folder and the set's name, such as `/Music/Tango.blset` (`.blset` is added if it's missing). If the folder is a project folder, one that already holds a `.blset` set, the set joins that project as `<name>.blset` there; a set of that name there is replaced, and the replaced version kept in that project's `Backup` folder. Otherwise a new project folder, `<name> Project`, is made in the folder (or `<name> Project 2` and so on if that name is taken, so nothing is overwritten), and the set is saved inside it, as `/Music/Tango Project/Tango.blset`. The result's `path` is where the set was saved. Moving to another project folder keeps the set using the same media files. A person choosing the menu item or pressing the shortcut picks the path in a dialog that opens in the set's project folder.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-004 | `Cmd+Shift+S` | `Ctrl+Shift+S` | `global` | Save the set under a new name | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | A folder and the set's name, as a set file's path such as `/Music/Tango.blset`, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. The set goes in that folder if it's a project folder (it holds a set already), and otherwise in a new `<name> Project` folder inside it; the result says where. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as_default`

**Save Beatlayer Set As Default Set...**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the open set as the default set, which every new set starts from, as File ▸ Save Beatlayer Set As Default Set does in Live. `path` names the default set's file; left out it goes in the User Library's `Templates` folder, or beside the app's preferences when there is no User Library. The open set itself doesn't change and keeps its own file. The result's `path` is the default set's file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to save the default set as, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Left out, it goes in the User Library's `Templates` folder, or beside the app's preferences when there is no User Library. `.blset` is added if it's missing. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as_template`

**Save Beatlayer Set As Template...**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the open set as a template in the User Library's `Templates` folder, making that folder if it isn't there, as File ▸ Save Beatlayer Set As Template does in Live. `name` names the template; left out it takes the open set's name. The open set itself doesn't change and keeps its own file. The result's `path` is the template's file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string or null | no | The template's name, without the `.blset` extension; left out uses the open set's name. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

### Area `settings`

#### `settings.next_page`

**Next Settings Page**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Shows the next page of the Settings window, wrapping from the last to the first. Changes no setting.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SET-005 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `settings` | Show the next settings page | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.previous_page`

**Previous Settings Page**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Shows the previous page of the Settings window, wrapping from the first to the last. Changes no setting.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SET-006 | `Option+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `settings` | Show the previous settings page | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_auto_hide_plug_in_windows`

**Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, on the Settings window's Plug-Ins page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, a floating device's window or a plug-in's editor window hides while another track is selected and comes back when its own track is selected again, as Live's plug-in windows do. A hidden window's device still floats, and a hidden editor stays open: hiding isn't docking or closing, isn't an undo step, and the set saves the device as floating. `device.windows` and `plugin.info` say which windows show. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_auto_warp_long_samples`

**Auto-Warp Long Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Auto-Warp Long Samples on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, a new audio clip of a long sample, one of 60 seconds or more, is warped with a warp marker on the first beat of every bar its analysis finds, and its 1.1.1 on the first beat; off, it is left unwarped. Clips already in the set keep their settings. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_continuous_save`

**Save Continuously**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Turns Save Continuously on or off (it starts off). When on, every finished edit of a set that has a file is saved within a second, so reopening the set shows it without asking, and each edit is a save point in the set's history since its last normal save. Turning it on saves the open set's unsaved edits that way. When off, edits are still journalled for crash recovery, and only Save keeps them. Save still writes the set file either way.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether Save Continuously is on. |

Result: [`ContinuousSave`](#continuoussave).

#### `settings.set_create_fades_on_clip_edges`

**Create Fades on Clip Edges**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Create Fades on Clip Edges, on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, each audio clip added to the Arrangement from now on gets fades of 4 ms (0.004 s) at both edges, so a clip that starts or ends mid-waveform doesn't click; clips already in the set keep their fades, which `clip.set_fades` changes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_default_launch_mode`

**Default Launch Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Launch Mode on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the launch mode (`trigger`, `gate`, `toggle` or `repeat`) a new Session clip starts with. It's `trigger` in a new install, as Live's is. Clips made so far keep their modes, and launch modes aren't built into clips yet, so for now it only keeps the choice. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`LaunchMode`](#launchmode) | yes | The launch mode new clips start with. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_default_launch_quantization`

**Default Launch Quantization**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Launch Quantization on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the launch quantisation a new Session clip starts with, one of the global quantisation's steps (see `clip.set_launch_quantization`), or `null` to follow the global quantisation (the default, Live's "Global"). Clips already in the set keep theirs. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) or null | no | The quantisation new clips start with; `null` (or nothing) follows the global one, Live's "Global". |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_default_warp_mode`

**Default Warp Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Warp Mode on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the warp mode (`beats`, `tones`, `texture`, `re_pitch`, `complex` or `complex_pro`) a new warped clip takes. It's `beats` in a new install, as Live's is. Clips already in the set keep their modes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`DefaultWarpMode`](#defaultwarpmode) | yes | The warp mode a new warped clip takes. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_loop_warp_short_samples`

**Loop/Warp Short Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Loop/Warp Short Samples on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: what a new audio clip of a short sample, one under 60 seconds, gets when it is dropped from the browser, loaded with Enter or imported. `unwarped_one_shot` leaves Warp and the loop off; `warped_one_shot` warps it as a loop of whole bars, the loop off; `warped_loop` does the same with the loop on; `auto`, what a new install has, makes a warped loop when the file's analysis finds a steady beat that fits 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars, and an unwarped one-shot otherwise. Clips already in the set keep their settings. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`LoopWarpShortSamples`](#loopwarpshortsamples) | yes | What a new clip of a short sample gets. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_outline_view_in_focus`

**Outline View in Focus**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Outline View in Focus, on the Settings window's Display & Input page: while it's on, as it is in a new install (as Live's is), a border is drawn round the part of the main window that has the keyboard focus and an outline round the focused control; while it's off, nothing shows where the focus is. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_record_session_automation_in`

**Record Session Automation in**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Record Session automation in on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: `armed_tracks` (the default, Live's) records the control moves of a Session recording into the clips of the armed tracks, `all_tracks` into the playing clip of every track. Moves are recorded only while Automation Arm is on (`arrangement.automation_arm`). The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | [`SessionAutomationTracks`](#sessionautomationtracks) | yes | `armed_tracks` or `all_tracks`. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_select_next_scene_on_launch`

**Select Next Scene on Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Select Next Scene on Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, launching a scene (`session.launch_scene`) selects the scene after it, when there is one. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_select_on_launch`

**Select on Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Select on Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, launching a clip that sits in a slot (`session.launch`) selects that slot. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_start_recording_on_scene_launch`

**Start Recording on Scene Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Start Recording on Scene Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's off in a new install, as Live's is. Session recording isn't built yet, so for now it only keeps the choice. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_temporary_folder`

**Temporary Folder**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the Temporary Folder on the Settings window's File & Folder page: where the files Reverse, Crop, Consolidate, Freeze and Bounce write go while the set has never been saved (the first save moves them into the project's `Samples/Processed` folders). `path` is an absolute path, made when it is first needed, or `null` for the default, a `Temporary` folder in Beatlayer's application-data folder. Files already written stay where they are. Run by a person from the Browse button without a `path`, it asks for a folder. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `path` is the folder in use afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The folder's absolute path, or `null` for the default: a `Temporary` folder in Beatlayer's application-data folder. |

Result: [`TemporaryFolderResult`](#temporaryfolderresult).

#### `settings.set_theme`

**Theme**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Beatlayer's dark or light theme, which every window uses straight away. The choice is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | [`ThemeChoice`](#themechoice) | yes | The theme. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_warp_recorded_audio`

**Warp Recorded Audio**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Warp recorded audio, on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page, a Beatlayer addition (IMP-02); it's on in a new install, as Live warps its recordings. Clips have no warp settings yet, so for now recorded clips play at their file's own speed whether it's on or off; warping will read the setting for the clips a recording makes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.state`

**Settings State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports every preference the Settings window shows with a value, by page, in the form its own command takes it: the theme (`settings.set_theme`), Display & Input (zoom, Outline View in Focus, the Tab key settings), the audio device settings with Driver Error Compensation and the test tone (`audio.configure`, `audio.set_test_tone`), the MIDI ports and computer keyboard (`midi.set_port`), Create Fades on Clip Edges, Warp Recorded Audio, the Launch section, Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, the plug-ins the Browser hides and prefers (`plugin.settings`), the agent server and the assistant. The server's and the agents' tokens and the assistant's API key are never reported, only whether one is stored. Preferences aren't saved with the set. Changes nothing. Use it to check a `settings.set_*` command took effect.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SettingsState`](#settingsstate).

### Area `slot`

#### `slot.set_stop_button`

**Add Stop Button**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Adds or removes a Session slot's Clip Stop button, which the person reaches through Edit ▸ Remove Stop Button (Cmd+E on macOS, Ctrl+E on Windows) and the slot's and Session clip's context menus. The button stops the track's playing clip; the track's own stop button (its status row) and Stop All Clips do the same for one or every track. A slot has one until it's removed, so a set saved before this command loads with one in every slot of every audio and MIDI track. The switch is saved with the set, and undo adds or removes the button again.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-005 | `Cmd+E` | `Ctrl+E` | `session` | Add or remove a clip stop button | toggles `stop_button` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |
| `stop_button` | boolean | yes | Whether the slot keeps its Clip Stop button: `true` adds it, and `false` removes it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `song`

#### `song.delete_tempo_breakpoint`

**Delete Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Deletes the tempo breakpoint at `at` from the Main track's Song Tempo envelope, joining its neighbours with a straight segment. The first breakpoint, at 1.1.1, can't be deleted; `at` there is refused. A position with no breakpoint is refused too.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.delete_time_signature_change`

**Delete Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Deletes the time-signature marker at `at`, so the signature before it runs on through that position. The first marker, at 1.1.1, can't be deleted; `at` there is refused. A position with no marker is refused too.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.move_tempo_breakpoint`

**Move Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the tempo breakpoint at `at` to `to`, keeping its tempo, as dragging one along the Main track's Song Tempo envelope does. Both are tick positions, `to` is 0 (1.1.1) or later, and it mustn't land on another breakpoint. The first breakpoint, at 1.1.1, can't move; `at` there is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another breakpoint already is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.move_time_signature_change`

**Move Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the time-signature marker at `at` to `to`, as dragging it along the arrangement's time-signature lane does. Both are tick positions, `to` is 0 (1.1.1) or later, and it mustn't land on another marker. The first marker, at 1.1.1, can't move; `at` there is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another marker already is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_tempo`

**Set Tempo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the song's tempo map. To give the whole song one tempo, send a single constant segment at tick 0; add segments to change or ramp the tempo at given positions. Tempos are quarter notes per minute, from 1 to 1,000. Clips and notes keep their positions in ticks, so a new tempo changes when they sound, not where they sit in bars.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tempo` | [`TempoMap`](#tempomap) | yes | The new tempo map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_tempo_breakpoint`

**Set Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the tempo at `at` on the Main track's Song Tempo envelope, adding a breakpoint there or replacing the one that's there, as dragging a breakpoint does. Tempos are quarter notes per minute, from 1 to 1,000, and `at` is 0 (1.1.1) or later. A breakpoint between two others splits the segment there, keeping the neighbours. Clips and notes keep their positions in ticks, so a new tempo changes when they sound, not where they sit in bars. Use `song.set_tempo` to replace the whole map at once.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint sits: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `bpm` | [`Bpm`](#bpm) | yes | The tempo there, as quarter notes per minute. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_time_signature_change`

**Set Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Sets the time-signature marker at `at` to `signature`, adding one when there's none, as Create > Insert Time Signature Change and the marker's numerator and denominator fields do. The marker sits anywhere at 0 (1.1.1) or later and always starts a new bar there, so a change before the previous bar is full cuts it short. Numerators run 1 to 99 and denominators are 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. Use `song.set_time_signatures` to replace the whole map.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker sits: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) | yes | The signature from there on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_time_signatures`

**Set Time Signatures**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the song's time-signature map. To give the whole song one meter, send a single change at tick 0, such as 4/4; add changes to switch meter at given positions, each of which starts a new bar. Numerators run from 1 to 99 and denominators are 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. It changes how positions are counted in bars and beats, not where clips sit in ticks.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time_signatures` | [`TimeSignatureMap`](#timesignaturemap) | yes | The new time-signature map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `stems`

#### `stems.cancel`

**Cancel**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops the package download or the separation under way. A cancelled separation changes nothing in the set; a cancelled download keeps the packages it finished.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.close`

**Close Separate Stems**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Closes the Separate Stems dialog. A download or separation under way goes on; `stems.cancel` stops it. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.install`

**Download Required Packages Now**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Downloads and installs the open-source packages stem separation needs, ONNX Runtime and the Demucs model (about 350 MB together), into Beatlayer's application-data folder, checking each file's SHA-256. Returns at once; `stems.status` reports the progress. Installed packages aren't downloaded again. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.open`

**Separate Stems to New Audio Tracks**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Opens the Separate Stems dialog for an audio clip in the Arrangement (`clip`, or the selected clip). The first time, the dialog lists the packages stem separation needs (ONNX Runtime and the Demucs model), their sizes and where they install, with Download Required Packages Now and Cancel; once they're installed it offers Vocals, Drums, Bass and Others, High Speed or High Quality, and Separate. Changes nothing in the set: an agent calls `stems.separate` instead.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip to separate; the selected clip if left out. |

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.separate`

**Separate Stems**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Separates an audio clip in the Arrangement into stems on new audio tracks, with a Demucs network running on this computer. `stems` chooses the parts (`vocals`, `drums`, `bass`, `others`; all four if left out); `quality` is `high_speed` (one pass) or `high_quality` (two passes averaged, about twice as long); `merge` puts two or three parts together on one track. The audio between the clip's Start and End markers, or through its loop, is separated at 44.1 kHz and written to the project's Samples/Processed/Stems folder. Each part gets a track below the clip's track, inside a new group track when there's more than one, with a copy of the clip playing that part; the original clip is deactivated. Playback stops first. Returns at once; `stems.status` reports the progress and the new tracks, and the whole edit is one undo step. Needs the packages `stems.install` downloads.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip in the Arrangement to separate. |
| `merge` | boolean | no | Put the chosen parts together on one track: only with two or three parts. |
| `quality` | [`StemQuality`](#stemquality) | no | `high_speed` (the default) or `high_quality`. |
| `stems` | array of [`StemKind`](#stemkind) | no | Which parts to put on new tracks, one or more; all four if left out. |

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.status`

**Stem Separation Status**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads stem separation's state: whether its packages are installed (and each package's name, version, project page and download size), where they install, the download's progress, the separation's progress, the tracks the last separation made, and the dialog if it's open.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

### Area `track`

#### `track.add_take_lane`

**Add Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Adds a take lane under an audio track's arrangement lane, after the lanes it has. `lane.name` names it and `lane.clips` are the recorded passes it holds, each with a `name`, a `start` and `length` in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note), and audio `data` as `clip.create` takes it. The track plays only its arrangement lane: loop recording adds a lane for every pass and copies the latest pass to the arrangement lane. Audio tracks only.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio track. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLane`](#takelane) | yes | The lane and its passes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.create`

**Insert Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Creates an empty track: audio (holds audio clips), MIDI (holds MIDI clips), group (holds other tracks), or return (receives sends). It starts at unity volume and centre pan, with no devices or clips. Audio, MIDI, and group tracks go at `index` among the top-level tracks, or inside the group `parent`; return tracks go at `index` among the returns. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it. The Main track always exists and can't be created.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-001 | `Cmd+T` | `Ctrl+T` | `global` | Insert an audio track | fixes `kind` = `"audio"` |
| S-TRACK-002 | `Cmd+Shift+T` | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `global` | Insert a MIDI track | fixes `kind` = `"midi"` |
| S-TRACK-003 | `Cmd+Option+T` | `Ctrl+Alt+T` | `global` | Insert a return track | fixes `kind` = `"return"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The new track's ID. |
| `kind` | [`TrackKind`](#trackkind) | yes | Its kind. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in its list, from 0 to the list's length. |
| `parent` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The group to put it in, or `null` (or nothing) for the top level. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.delete`

**Delete Track**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Deletes a track with its clips and devices. Deleting a group track also deletes every track inside it. Use it to remove a track the song no longer needs; to silence a track and keep it, use `mixer.set_mute`. Undo restores everything it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. The Main track can't be deleted.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-018 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `track-headers` | Delete the track from its title bar | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.duplicate_without_clips`

**Duplicate Track Without Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Duplicates tracks (`tracks`, or the selected tracks) without their clips or arrangement automation: each copy goes straight after its track, with its name (the next number where the name starts with the track's number), mixer settings, sends, routing, and devices with their settings, and the copies become the selected tracks. A group's copy holds copies of its tracks, without clips. Use it to start a new part with a track's sound. One undo step, named Duplicate Track(s) Without Clips. Main can't be duplicated.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks; the selected tracks if left out. |

Result: [`TracksDuplicated`](#tracksduplicated).

#### `track.group`

**Group Tracks**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Groups tracks (`tracks`, or the selected tracks): inserts a group track named "Group" where the first track was, moves the tracks into it in order, routes each member to the group and the group to Main, leaves the group unfolded, and selects it. One undo step, named Group Tracks.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-006 | `Cmd+G` | `Ctrl+G` | `track-headers` | Group the selected tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks to group; the selected tracks if left out. |

Result: [`TracksGrouped`](#tracksgrouped).

#### `track.move`

**Move Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Moves a track to `index` in the top-level track list, or inside the group `parent`. A return track moves among the returns. The index counts positions after the track is taken out of its current place, so moving a track down past its neighbour is its current index plus one. Use it to reorder tracks or to put tracks into or out of groups. A group can't go inside itself, and the Main track can't be moved.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that list. |
| `parent` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The group to move it into, or `null` (or nothing) for the top level. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.rename`

**Rename Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Renames a track. A name may be empty, and tracks may share a name. It changes only the name in the track's title bar.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-004 | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` | `track-headers` | Rename the selected track | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.ungroup`

**Ungroup Tracks**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Ungroups a group track (`track`, or the selected track): removes the group track, moves its members back where it was in order, routes each member to Main (or parent group default), and selects the first member. One undo step, named Ungroup Tracks.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-007 | `Cmd+Shift+G` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` | `track-headers` | Ungroup the selected group track | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The group track to ungroup; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`TracksUngrouped`](#tracksungrouped).

### Area `transport`

#### `transport.continue`

**Continue Playback**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Resumes playback from where it last stopped rather than from the insert marker. It does nothing while the song plays. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-002 | `Shift+Space` | `Shift+Space` | `global` | Continue playing from where playback stopped | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.insert_marker_to_playhead`

**Move Insert Marker To Playhead**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the insert marker to the playhead: where the song is playing now, or where playback stopped. Use it to start again later from the current point. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-033 | `Cmd+Shift+Space` | `Ctrl+Shift+Space` | `arrangement` | Move the insert marker to the play position | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.locate`

**Set Arrangement Position**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the insert marker, where playback starts, to `position`, in ticks from the start of the arrangement (705,600 to the quarter note, so bar 2 of a 4/4 song is 2,822,400), as typing into the Control Bar's Arrangement Position fields does. While the song plays, playback jumps there at once; while it's stopped, `transport.continue` still resumes where playback stopped. Position 0 returns to 1.1.1, as the Home key and Return Play Position to 1.1.1 do. A position before 0 is taken as 0. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-005 | `Home`, `Fn+Left` | `Home` | `global` | Move the insert marker to the start | fixes `position` = `0` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The new insert marker, in ticks from 1.1.1. A position before 1.1.1 is taken as 1.1.1. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play`

**Play**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Starts playback from the insert marker, as the Control Bar's Play button does; while the song plays, starts it again from the insert marker. Set the insert marker first with `transport.locate`. With the Arrangement loop on, playback that reaches the loop's end goes on from its start. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play_from_insert_marker`

**Play From Insert Marker**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Starts playback from the insert marker. Until the arrangement has time selections, this does what `transport.play` does. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-032 | `Option+Space` | `Ctrl+Space` | `arrangement` | Play from the insert marker in the selected clip | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play_stop`

**Play/Stop**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops playback if the song is playing, and otherwise starts it from the insert marker: the space bar, and the Playback menu's Play item, which reads Stop while the song plays. Unlike `transport.stop`, it never returns to 1.1.1. An agent that knows what it wants should use `transport.play` or `transport.stop` instead.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-001 | `Space` | `Space` | `global` | Play from the start marker, or stop | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.return_to_start`

**Return Play Position to 1.1.1**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the insert marker, where playback starts, back to the start of the arrangement (1.1.1), as the Playback menu's Return Play Position to 1.1.1 does. While the song plays, playback jumps there at once; while it's stopped, `transport.continue` still resumes where playback stopped. The same as `transport.locate` at position 0, which the Home key runs. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.set_loop`

**Set Loop Brace**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the Arrangement loop brace to start at `start` and run for `length` ticks (705,600 to the quarter note; a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400), as the Control Bar's Loop Start and Loop Length fields do. It doesn't switch the loop on or off: use `transport.set_loop_enabled` for that. While the loop is on, playback that reaches the brace's end jumps back to its start; playback that starts at or after the end plays on. The start must be 0 (1.1.1) or later and the length more than 0. The brace is saved with the set, and undo moves it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the loop starts: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long it is: more than 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_loop_enabled`

**Arrangement Loop On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches the Arrangement loop on or off, as the Control Bar's Loop switch does, leaving the brace where it is. With it on, playback that reaches the brace's end jumps back to its start, on the exact sample, until it's switched off or playback stops. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace first. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether playback loops between the brace's start and end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_count_in`

**Metronome Count-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the metronome count-in length: `none`, `1_bar`, `2_bars`, or `4_bars`. When enabled, starting playback or recording plays the chosen bars of metronome clicks before the transport moves. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count_in` | [`CountIn`](#countin) | yes | The count-in duration in bars: none, 1 bar, 2 bars, or 4 bars. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_enabled`

**Metronome**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the metronome on or off, as the Control Bar's Metronome switch and the Playback menu's Metronome item do. When on, the metronome clicks on each beat of the song, with the downbeat accented. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-011 | `O` | `O` | `global` | Turn the metronome on or off | toggles `enabled` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the metronome clicks during playback. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_only_while_recording`

**Hear Metronome Only While Recording**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether the metronome clicks only while recording or during playback as well, as the Playback menu and Metronome Settings menu do. The setting is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `only_while_recording` | boolean | yes | When on, clicks only sound while recording. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_rhythm`

**Metronome Rhythm**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the rhythmic division the metronome clicks at: `auto` (follows the time signature's denominator), `1_bar`, `1/2`, `1/2t`, `1/4`, `1/4t`, `1/8`, `1/8t`, `1/16`, or `1/16t`. If a division exceeds the bar length under the current time signature, clicks follow the auto interval. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rhythm` | [`MetronomeRhythm`](#metronomerhythm) | yes | The rhythm division. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_sound`

**Metronome Sound**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Chooses the metronome's sound character: `classic`, `click`, or `wood`. All sounds are synthesized in code. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound` | [`MetronomeSound`](#metronomesound) | yes | The synthesised sound character. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_midi_overdub`

**MIDI Arrangement Overdub**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches MIDI Arrangement Overdub on or off, as the Control Bar's overdub switch does. With it on, notes recorded into the Arrangement merge into the MIDI clips already on the track instead of replacing them. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | When on, MIDI recorded into the Arrangement merges into the clips already there instead of replacing them. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_punch_in`

**Punch-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Punch-In on or off, as the Control Bar's Punch-In switch does. With it on, recording into the Arrangement starts at the Arrangement loop brace's start, whether or not the Loop switch is on: playback that starts before the brace records nothing until it reaches the brace, and playback that starts inside the brace records from where it starts. The metronome's "only while recording" setting sounds from the punch-in point. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether recording starts at the brace's start. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_punch_out`

**Punch-Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Punch-Out on or off, as the Control Bar's Punch-Out switch does. With it on, recording into the Arrangement ends at the Arrangement loop brace's end, whether or not the Loop switch is on: the recording stops there, playback carries on, and Arrangement Record stays on but writes nothing more. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether recording ends at the brace's end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_recording`

**Set Recording**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets whether the transport is recording: while it is, each armed audio track records its input into the project's Samples/Recorded/, each armed MIDI track records the notes it receives, and the recording becomes a clip on its track when it ends; a count-in starts it a bar or more later. With MIDI Arrangement Overdub on, recorded notes merge into the MIDI clips already there. Features like Hear Metronome Only While Recording follow it too. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first, whichever way you set it: to stop a recording without asking, run `transport.stop_recording`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | boolean | yes | Whether the transport is recording. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.state`

**Transport Status**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the Control Bar's transport section shows: whether the song plays, the play position and the insert marker (in ticks from 1.1.1, and the Arrangement Position fields' bar.beat.sixteenth), the Arrangement loop's start, length, and switch, the tempo, and the time signature, the metronome, Arrangement Record and whether a take is running or the count-in is sounding, Punch-In and Punch-Out, MIDI Arrangement Overdub, Automation Arm, the recording under way (its armed tracks and dropped frames) and what the last recording came to, and whether the audio engine runs so the transport can play. Every `transport.set_*` setting reads back here. Changes nothing. Use it to check where the song is before and after `transport.play`, `transport.stop`, `transport.locate`, or `transport.set_loop`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`TransportState`](#transportstate).

#### `transport.stop`

**Stop**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops playback, as the Control Bar's Stop button does, and keeps the position where it stopped, so `transport.continue` can resume there. Run it again while stopped to return the insert marker and the play position to the start of the arrangement (1.1.1), as pressing Stop twice does. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.stop_recording`

**Stop Recording**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops recording, the same as `transport.set_recording` with `recording` false, and without asking the person. The recording becomes a clip on its track; playback goes on. It does nothing when the transport isn't recording.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

### Area `view`

#### `view.clip_envelope`

**Clip View Envelope**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Chooses the parameter whose envelope the Clip View's Envelopes tab shows and edits, as its device and control choosers do: `target` is a control of the shown clip's track's mixer, one of its sends, or a parameter of a device in its chain, named as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` names it; `null` shows none. Changes only the view, so it's no undo step. Editing the envelope is done by the `clip.*envelope*` commands. The result says which parameter shows.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) or null | no | The parameter of the shown clip's track whose envelope the Envelopes tab shows, or `null` to show none. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.clip_tab`

**Clip View Tab**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `sample-editor`, `envelope`.

Chooses the tab the Clip View shows for its clip: `notes` (the MIDI Note Editor, Option+Shift+1) or `envelopes` (the clip's envelopes, Option+Shift+2). Left out, `tab` goes on to the next tab and round to the first after the last (Option+Tab). The Clip View shows the clip most recently selected, in the Arrangement or in a Session slot. Changes only the view, so it's no undo step and isn't saved with the set. The result says which tab shows.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-CLIPMODE-001 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `sample-editor` | Switch between the Sample and Envelopes tabs | runs it |
| S-CLIPMODE-002 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `note-editor` | Cycle the Notes, Envelopes and MPE tabs | runs it |
| S-CLIPMODE-003 | `Option+Shift+1` | `Alt+Shift+1` | `clip-view` | Show the Content Editor (the Sample or Notes tab) | fixes `tab` = `"notes"` |
| S-CLIPMODE-004 | `Option+Shift+2` | `Alt+Shift+2` | `clip-view` | Show the Envelope Editor (the Envelopes tab) | fixes `tab` = `"envelopes"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tab` | [`ClipTab`](#cliptab) or null | no | The tab to show. Left out, the Clip View goes on to the next one. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.draw_mode`

**Draw Mode**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Draw Mode (B; Options ▸ Draw Mode), which changes what a click in the MIDI Note Editor's note area does: with it on, clicking empty grid adds a note one grid step long, and clicking a note removes it; with it off, clicking selects. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result says whether it's on.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-GRID-001 | `B` | `B` | `global` | Toggle Draw Mode | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.fold_notes`

**Fold to Notes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`.

Folds or unfolds the MIDI Note Editor (F, View ▸ Fold to Notes): while it's folded, the editor shows only the key rows that hold notes, one under the next, and not the empty rows between them. `clip` names the clip; left out, the one the editor shows. `folded` says which way; left out, it switches. Folding changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step: it's saved with the set beside the song, so it's there again when the set is reopened. The result says whether the editor is folded now.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-038 | `F` | `F` | `note-editor` | Fold the editor to the key tracks that hold notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `folded` | boolean or null | no | Fold (true) or unfold (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.full_screen`

**Full Screen**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the main window into or out of full-screen mode. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-001 | `Ctrl+Cmd+F` | `F11` | `global` | Toggle full-screen mode | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.lane`

**Note Editor Lane**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`.

Chooses which of a note's values the lane under the MIDI Note Editor shows and edits: `velocity` (the lane's default), `release_velocity`, `chance`, or `velocity_deviation`. Dragging a note's stem in the lane sets that value on that note, and dragging across several notes ramps it; the same edits are the `note.set_value` and `note.ramp_value` commands. Changes only the view, so it's no undo step and isn't saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lane` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value the lane shows. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.set_zoom`

**Zoom**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `settings`.

Sets the interface zoom to `percent`, a whole percentage from 50 to 200, as the Zoom setting on the Settings window's Display & Input page does: every window's panes, controls, and text scale together and keep their places, and the main window grows if it's smaller than its minimum size at that zoom (as far as the screen allows). The result's `zoom` is the new zoom as a factor, 1.5 for 150%. The zoom is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `percent` | integer from 50 to 200 | yes | The interface zoom as a whole percentage, from 50 to 200; 100 is the size layout.md measures Live at. |

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.state`

**View State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the view commands switch: the main view (Arrangement or Session), whether the browser and the Info View show, full-screen mode and the zoom (`view.toggle_session_arrangement`, `view.toggle_browser`, `view.toggle_info_view`, `view.full_screen`, `view.set_zoom`), the Clip View with Draw Mode, the lane, Fold and the selected notes (`view.toggle_clip_view`, `view.draw_mode`, `view.lane`, `view.fold_notes`), the assistant's panel and whether plug-in windows are shown (`view.toggle_plug_in_windows`). Changes nothing. The Arrangement's own view is in `arrangement.state`, the Mixer's in `mixer_view.state`, the Session View's in `session.state` and the Device View's in `device_view.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewState`](#viewstate).

#### `view.toggle_assistant`

**Assistant**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens or closes the built-in assistant's panel: a full-height pane at the main window's right edge, beside the main view, the detail area and the Status Bar, or a window of its own while the person has floated it. The Control Bar's last control and the View menu's Assistant item do the same. A new session starts with it closed. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. It belongs to the person using the app, so the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate).

#### `view.toggle_browser`

**Browser**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides the browser at the left of the main window; the main view widens to fill its place. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-010 | `Cmd+Option+B`, `Cmd+Option+5` | `Ctrl+Alt+B`, `Ctrl+Alt+5` | `global` | Show or hide the browser | runs it |
| S-BRW-002 | `Cmd+Option+B` | `Ctrl+Alt+B` | `global` | Show or hide the browser | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.toggle_clip_view`

**Clip View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides the Clip View in the detail area, which holds the MIDI Note Editor for the Arrangement's selected MIDI clip; while it shows, it takes the detail area in place of the Device View. It shows the clip the Arrangement has selected, with its notes, and selecting another MIDI clip switches the editor to it, clearing the note selection. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result says whether it shows, what clip the editor holds, and which notes are selected.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-015 | `Cmd+Option+3` | `Ctrl+Alt+3` | `global` | Show or hide the Clip View | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.toggle_info_view`

**Info**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides the Info View at the bottom left of the main window, which reads whatever the pointer is over: the control's name, the help text of the command it runs, and its key on a separate line, and shows nothing while the pointer is over empty space. A new set opens with it shown, as in Live. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-008 | `Shift+Slash` | `Shift+Slash` | `global` | Show or hide the Info View | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.toggle_plug_in_windows`

**Plug-In Windows**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Shows or hides every floating device's window and every plug-in's editor window at once, as View ▸ Plug-In Windows does for Live's plug-in windows (Cmd-Option-P); switches unless `shown` says which. Hidden windows' devices still float, and a hidden editor stays open: it isn't docking or closing, isn't an undo step, and changes nothing in the set. Floating a device shows the windows again. Only runs while a device floats or a plug-in window is open. The result's `on` is whether they're shown afterwards.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-009 | `Cmd+Option+P` | `Ctrl+Alt+P` | `global` | Show or hide all open plug-in windows | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false) them; switches if left out. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `view.toggle_session_arrangement`

**Toggle Arrangement/Session View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the main view between the Arrangement View and the Session View. A new set opens in the Arrangement View. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-003 | `Tab` | `Tab` | `global` | Switch between Session and Arrangement (when Tab doesn't move focus) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.zoom_in`

**Zoom In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Makes the whole interface larger by one step of 10%, up to 200%: every window's panes, controls, and text scale together and keep their places. From a zoom between steps it goes to the next step up. The zoom is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ZOOM-001 | `Cmd+Plus` | `Ctrl+Plus` | `global` | Zoom the interface in | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.zoom_out`

**Zoom Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Makes the whole interface smaller by one step of 10%, down to 50%: every window's panes, controls, and text scale together and keep their places. From a zoom between steps it goes to the next step down. The zoom is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ZOOM-002 | `Cmd+Minus` | `Ctrl+Minus` | `global` | Zoom the interface out | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

#### `view.zoom_reset`

**Reset Zoom to 100%**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns the interface zoom to 100%, the size Live's layout is measured at. The zoom is kept for the next start. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ViewResult`](#viewresult).

### Area `window`

#### `window.close`

**Close Window**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `dialog`, `settings`.

Closes the frontmost secondary window, such as the Settings window. The main window stays open; quit to close it. From the keyboard or the File menu it acts only while a secondary window is in front, as in Live, where Close Window is disabled with only the main window open.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-009 | `Cmd+W` | `Ctrl+W` | `global` | Close the frontmost window | runs it |
| S-VIEW-020 | `Esc` | `Esc` | `dialog` | Close the frontmost window or dialog | runs it |
| S-SET-007 | `Esc` | `Esc` | `settings` | Close the Settings window | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

## Readback

Anything an agent can set, it can read back. Each command that isn't `read` names where its effect shows: a read command and the field in its result, or the query tool's path for an object and the field in its full result. A query field is one the set saves for the object, or one of the song's overview. `cargo xtask commands` fails when a command that changes something names none, or names a field that isn't there.

| Command | Read it with | Field |

| [`agent.forget_client`](#agentforget_client) | `settings.state` | `agents.clients` |
| [`agent.set_autonomous`](#agentset_autonomous) | `settings.state` | `agents.clients[].autonomous` |
| [`agent.set_server`](#agentset_server) | `settings.state` | `agents.server` |
| [`arrangement.cut`](#arrangementcut) | the query tool's `track` | `clips` |

### Nothing to read back

| Command | Why |
|---|---|
| [`agent.new_client_token`](#agentnew_client_token) | a new random token, which an agent is never told: the Settings window shows it to the person |
| [`agent.new_token`](#agentnew_token) | a new random token, which an agent is never told: the Settings window shows it to the person |
| [`app.quit`](#appquit) | the app ends, so there is nothing left to read from |
| [`browser.add_folder`](#browseradd_folder) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.open_folder`](#browseropen_folder) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.open_place`](#browseropen_place) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |

| [`browser.remove_folder`](#browserremove_folder) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.search`](#browsersearch) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.select`](#browserselect) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.set_preview`](#browserset_preview) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.show_file`](#browsershow_file) | the Browser's state is read with `browser.state`, which is `external` because it lists files outside the project |
| [`browser.state`](#browserstate) | a query of its own: it reads the Browser, and is `external` for the files it lists |
| [`chain.save_preset`](#chainsave_preset) | writes a file outside the set; the set doesn't change |
| [`device.save_default_preset`](#devicesave_default_preset) | writes a file outside the set; the set doesn't change |
| [`device.save_preset`](#devicesave_preset) | writes a file outside the set; the set doesn't change |

| [`midi.export_clip`](#midiexport_clip) | writes a file outside the set; the set doesn't change |
| [`pad.save_default`](#padsave_default) | the default pad is the shell's, kept in memory and in the User Library, not in the set; the next `pad.drop` on an empty pad makes its chain from it |
| [`set.discard_recovery`](#setdiscard_recovery) | deletes a recovery file outside the set |
| [`set.relink_missing`](#setrelink_missing) | finds files outside the set; the clips that use them read their media |

| [`set.save_as_template`](#setsave_as_template) | writes a file outside the set; the set doesn't change |
| [`settings.set_continuous_save`](#settingsset_continuous_save) | the app doesn't host the autosave service yet, so no read command reports Save Continuously; the command's own result does |

## Types

The types the arguments and results use, with their JSON Schemas. A `$ref` such as `#/$defs/Ticks` names a type in this list.

### `AdaptiveGrid`

A zoom-adaptive grid setting: how far apart its lines stay on screen, from `widest` to `narrowest`. Each step is twice as dense as the one before. A new set uses `narrow`.

One of:

- `"widest"`: The fewest lines.
- `"wide"`: Fewer lines.
- `"medium"`: Between.
- `"narrow"`: More lines; a new set's setting.
- `"narrowest"`: The most lines.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A zoom-adaptive grid setting: how far apart its lines stay on screen, from `widest` to `narrowest`. Each step is twice as dense as the one before. A new set uses `narrow`.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "widest",
      "description": "The fewest lines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "wide",
      "description": "Fewer lines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "medium",
      "description": "Between.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "narrow",
      "description": "More lines; a new set's setting.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "narrowest",
      "description": "The most lines.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `AddResult`

What `browser.add_to_arrangement` and `browser.load_selected` return.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | Audio tracks made for the files, top to bottom. |
| `clips` | array of [`PlacedClip`](#placedclip) | yes | The clips placed, in the order of the files. |

### `ArrangementState`

What the Arrangement View shows: every view command returns it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | [`TimeRange`](#timerange) | yes | The span of time across the track lanes, left edge to right edge. |
| `ticks_per_point` | number | yes | The zoom: ticks of song time per point of screen. |
| `scroll_y` | number | yes | How far the track lanes are scrolled down, in points. |
| `visible_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The tracks at least partly in view, top to bottom (the return tracks and Main, pinned at the bottom, are always in view and not listed). |
| `follow` | boolean | yes | Whether Follow is on. |
| `follow_paused` | boolean | yes | Whether Follow is on but paused, because the view was scrolled by hand while the song played; it resumes when playback starts or stops, or a click lands in the track lanes or the scrub area. |
| `overview` | boolean | yes | Whether the Overview shows above the rulers. |
| `optimize_height` | boolean | yes | Whether Optimize Height is on: every track fits in the lanes. |
| `optimize_width` | boolean | yes | Whether Optimize Width is on: the whole arrangement fits across. |
| `grid` | [`GridState`](#gridstate) | yes | The editing grid. |
| `insert_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the insert marker is. |
| `selected_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The selected tracks, top to bottom. |
| `selected_clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The selected clips (WP-1.8b), in the order they were selected. The editing commands act on these when there are any, and on the time selection otherwise. |

| `automation_mode` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Mode is on: each track shows its automation lane under its lane, with the device and parameter choosers. |
| `automation_arm` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Arm is on: while Arrangement Record runs, moving a control writes its values into the parameter's envelope. |
| `automation_lanes` | array of [`AutomationLane`](#automationlane) | no | The parameter each track's automation lane shows, for the tracks whose lane isn't showing the default (their volume): the choosers' choice. `target` `null` means the lane draws no envelope. |

### `AssistantProvider`

Which model API the assistant talks to.

One of:

- `"open-ai"`: An OpenAI-compatible API: OpenAI itself, OpenRouter, or a local server such as Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or vLLM, reached through [`AssistantSettings::base_url`].
- `"anthropic"`: Anthropic's Messages API.
- `"gemini"`: Google's Gemini API.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>
