```json
  "description": "Which model API the assistant talks to.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "open-ai",
      "description": "An OpenAI-compatible API: OpenAI itself, OpenRouter, or a local server such as Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or vLLM, reached through [`AssistantSettings::base_url`].",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "anthropic",
      "description": "Anthropic's Messages API.",

    }
  ]
}
```

### `AudioData`

An audio clip's data: the audio file it plays, named by content hash, and how it plays it. Times are seconds into the file. Every field but `media` is optional: a new clip plays the whole file once, at 0 dB, with no fades.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The media file the clip plays, by content hash. |
| `end` | number or null | no | The End marker: where in the file, in seconds, a clip whose loop is off stops playing, after the Start marker; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. |
| `fade_in` | number, at least 0 | no | The fade-in's length in seconds, from the clip's start in the Arrangement: 0 (no fade) unless given. |
| `fade_out` | number, at least 0 | no | The fade-out's length in seconds, up to the clip's end in the Arrangement: 0 (no fade) unless given. |
| `gain` | number, at least 0 | no | The clip's gain, as a linear gain: 1 (0 dB) unless given, 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 silence (−∞ dB). Finite and 0 or more. |
| `high_quality` | boolean | no | The HiQ switch (R12): on unless given. On, the clip is resampled by a band-limited interpolator wherever it is read at another rate than 1. |
| `loop_end` | number or null | no | Where the loop brace ends in the file, in seconds, after its start; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. While the loop is on, the Start marker must be before it. |
| `loop_start` | number, at least 0 | no | Where the loop brace starts in the file, in seconds. 0 or more; 0 unless given. |
| `looping` | boolean | no | The Loop switch: whether the clip repeats its loop brace. Off unless given. |
| `ram` | boolean | no | The RAM switch (R11): off unless given. On, the clip's whole file is held in memory instead of streamed. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) or null | no | A warped clip's own time signature, the Clip View's Signature fields; `null` (or nothing) means the song's signature at the clip's start. |
| `start` | number, at least 0 | no | The Start marker: where in the file, in seconds, the clip starts playing. 0 or more; 0 unless given. |
| `tempo` | number or null | no | The clip's tempo in BPM, from 1 to 1,000: the speed of the file after the last warp marker (R2). Given whenever there are markers. |
| `transient_edits` | [`TransientEdits`](#transientedits) | no | The clip's edits to its file's detected transients (the warping spec, R23): none unless given. They belong to the file, so replacing the file drops them (R27). |
| `warp` | boolean | no | The Warp switch (the warping spec, R1): off unless given. On, the clip follows the set's tempo through its warp map, and `start`, `end`, `loop_start` and `loop_end` are whole ticks of its contents, counted from the clip's 1.1.1, instead of seconds in the file. |
| `warp_markers` | array of [`WarpMarker`](#warpmarker) | no | The warp markers, in increasing order of both fields: a warped clip has at least one. Switching Warp off keeps them (R3). |
| `warp_mode` | [`WarpMode`](#warpmode) | no | The warp mode (the warp modes spec, R1): Beats unless given. An unwarped clip keeps it for when Warp goes back on. |
| `warp_settings` | [`WarpSettings`](#warpsettings) | no | Every mode's controls (R2): each at the table's default unless given. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "An audio clip's data: the audio file it plays, named by content hash, and how it plays it. Times are seconds into the file. Every field but `media` is optional: a new clip plays the whole file once, at 0 dB, with no fades.",
  "properties": {
    "end": {
      "description": "The End marker: where in the file, in seconds, a clip whose loop is off stops playing, after the Start marker; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },

    "transient_edits": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TransientEdits",
      "description": "The clip's edits to its file's detected transients (the warping spec, R23): none unless given. They belong to the file, so replacing the file drops them (R27)."
    },
    "warp": {
      "description": "The Warp switch (the warping spec, R1): off unless given. On, the clip follows the set's tempo through its warp map, and `start`, `end`, `loop_start` and `loop_end` are whole ticks of its contents, counted from the clip's 1.1.1, instead of seconds in the file.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "warp_markers": {
      "description": "The warp markers, in increasing order of both fields: a warped clip has at least one. Switching Warp off keeps them (R3).",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/WarpMarker"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "warp_mode": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/WarpMode",
      "description": "The warp mode (the warp modes spec, R1): Beats unless given. An unwarped clip keeps it for when Warp goes back on."
    },
    "warp_settings": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/WarpSettings",
      "description": "Every mode's controls (R2): each at the table's default unless given."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "media"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `AudioSettings`

The audio device settings, as the Settings window's Audio page sets them and the preferences file keeps them. `None` means the platform's or the device's own choice.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver` | string or null | yes | The driver type's ID (`coreaudio`, `wasapi`, `asio`, `jack`, `alsa`, or `null`), or nothing for the platform's default. |
| `output_device` | string or null | yes | The output device's ID, or nothing for the system's default output device, which the stream then follows where the driver can. |
| `input_device` | string or null | yes | The input device's ID, or nothing for no input. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | yes | The sample rate in hertz, or nothing for the device's current rate, which leaves the device's own setting alone. |
| `buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size in frames, or nothing for the device's default. |
| `output_channels` | integer or null | yes | Output channels to open, or nothing for all the device has. |
| `driver_error_compensation_ms` | number | yes | Driver Error Compensation in milliseconds, two decimals, from -1000 to 1000: added to the device's reported latency when a recording is moved earlier to line up with what was played (WP-2.13). It changes recording only, and one value serves every device. |

### `AudioStatus`

What `audio.status` returns.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `engine_on` | boolean | yes | Whether the audio engine is on. |

| `driver` | string | yes | The driver type in use (its ID). |
| `output_device` | [`DeviceRef`](#deviceref) or null | yes | The output device the stream opened, while one is open. |
| `input_device` | [`DeviceRef`](#deviceref) or null | yes | The input device the stream opened, if any. |
| `follows_default` | boolean | yes | Whether the stream follows the system's default output device. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | yes | The sample rate the device runs at, in hertz, while a stream is open. |
| `requested_buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size the settings asked for, in frames. |
| `buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size the device actually delivers, in frames, once it has called back, or what the driver says it set until then. |
| `output_channels` | integer from 0 to 65535 | yes | Output channels open. |
| `input_channels` | integer from 0 to 65535 | yes | Input channels open. |
| `buffer_ms` | number or null | yes | The output buffer's length in milliseconds. |
| `input_latency_ms` | number or null | yes | The input latency the device reports, in milliseconds, while a stream is open. Zero for a device that reports none. |
| `output_latency_ms` | number or null | yes | The output latency the device reports, in milliseconds, while a stream is open. Zero for a device that reports none. |
| `overall_latency_ms` | number or null | yes | The Audio page's Overall Latency, in milliseconds, while a stream is open: input latency plus output latency plus Driver Error Compensation, which is how far a recording is moved earlier. |
| `cpu_load` | number or null | yes | The share of each buffer's time spent processing audio, in percent, averaged over the last measurement; nothing while the engine is off. |
| `dropouts` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Dropouts since the stream opened. |
| `test_tone` | boolean | yes | Whether the test tone plays. |
| `tone` | [`ToneSettings`](#tonesettings) | yes | The test tone's level and frequency. |
| `error` | string or null | yes | The last error from the device, if the stream couldn't open or failed. |

### `AutomationTarget`

Which parameter of the track an envelope drives: `mixer` with a `param`, `send` with the return track it feeds (`to`), `device` with the device and its `param`, `chain` with a rack's chain and its mixer `param`, or `chain_send` with a drum rack's chain and the return chain it sends to (`to`). A MIDI clip's envelope can instead name a MIDI controller: `midi.cc` with its `number` (1 to 31 or 33 to 119), `midi.pitch_bend` or `midi.channel_pressure`.

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"mixer"`, `param` ([`MixerParam`](#mixerparam)): A control of the track's mixer.
- an object with `type` = `"send"`, `to` ([`TrackId`](#trackid)): The level of the track's send to a return track.
- an object with `type` = `"device"`, `device` ([`DeviceId`](#deviceid)), `param` ([`ParamId`](#paramid)): A parameter of a device in the track's chain.
- an object with `type` = `"chain"`, `chain` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)), `param` ([`MixerParam`](#mixerparam)): A control of a rack chain's mixer (WP-5.1, G2): the chain's Volume, Pan, or Chain Activator (`mute`: 1 muted, 0 not).
- an object with `type` = `"chain_send"`, `chain` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)), `to` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)): The level of a drum chain's send to a return chain of its rack (drum racks R6, G2).
- an object with `type` = `"midi.cc"`, `number` (integer from 0 to 255): A continuous controller of a MIDI clip's MIDI Ctrl envelopes (WP-2.29), 1 to 31 or 33 to 119, from 0 to 127. Only a MIDI clip's envelope names it; a track has no automation for it.
- an object with `type` = `"midi.pitch_bend"`: A MIDI clip's pitch bend envelope, from −8192 to 8191, 0 at rest.
- an object with `type` = `"midi.channel_pressure"`: A MIDI clip's channel pressure envelope, from 0 to 127.

A MIDI clip's envelope can instead name a MIDI controller: `midi.cc` with its `number` (1 to 31 or 33 to 119), `midi.pitch_bend` or `midi.channel_pressure`.",

### `Chain`

One chain of a rack: its own name, colour, info text and mixer, and its devices in signal order.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The chain's name. |
| `audio_to` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | Where a return chain's output goes: one of the set's return tracks, or the rack's own output while there is none (drum racks spec, R8). |
| `choke` | integer or null | no | The choke group a drum rack's chain is in, from 1 to 16, or none. |
| `colour` | integer or null | no | The chain's colour: an index into the palette of 5 rows of 14 swatches, from 0 to 69, or none. |
| `devices` | array of [`Device`](#device) | no | The chain's devices, in signal order. |
| `info` | string | no | The info text the user gave the chain (Edit Info Text). |
| `is_return` | boolean | no | Whether this is one of a drum rack's return chains, which sit after its drum chains (drum racks spec, R7). |

| `play` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | The note a drum rack's chain passes on to its devices, from 0 to 127: C3 (60) in a new chain. |
| `receive` | [`Receive`](#receive) | no | The note a drum rack's chain answers (drum racks spec, R1). Only a drum rack's chains have one; any other chain keeps the default. |
| `sends` | array of [`ChainSend`](#chainsend) | no | A drum rack's drum chain's sends to its return chains, post-fader; a return chain without an entry gets none (−∞ dB). |

### `ChainMixer`

A chain's mixer: `volume` (linear gain, 1 is 0 dB, 0 is -inf), `pan` (-1 left to 1 right), `enabled` (the Chain Activator) and `solo`. A MIDI effect rack's chains have no volume or pan.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | The Chain Activator: on in a new chain. A chain that's off adds nothing to its rack's output. |
| `pan` | number | no | From −1 (left) to 1 (right): centre in a new chain. |
| `solo` | boolean | no | Solo: while any chain of a rack is soloed, its unsoloed chains add nothing. |
| `volume` | number | no | Linear gain: 1 (0 dB) in a new chain. |

```json
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `ChainSelect`

How `chain.select` changes the selection.

One of:

- `"replace"`: Select only `chain`: a click.
- `"toggle"`: Add `chain` to the selection, or remove it: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click).
- `"range"`: Select every chain from the selected one to `chain`: Shift-click.
- `"previous"`: Select only the chain above the first selected one: Up.
- `"next"`: Select only the chain below the last selected one: Down.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How `chain.select` changes the selection.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "replace",
      "description": "Select only `chain`: a click.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "Add `chain` to the selection, or remove it: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "range",
      "description": "Select every chain from the selected one to `chain`: Shift-click.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "previous",
      "description": "Select only the chain above the first selected one: Up.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "next",
      "description": "Select only the chain below the last selected one: Down.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

```json
    },
    "to": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ChainId",
      "description": "The return chain."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "to",
    "level"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ChainZones`

A chain's zones, each `low`, `high` and the `fade_low` and `fade_high` values its fades span: `key` (0 to 127), `velocity` (1 to 127) and `select` (the chain select zone, 0 to 127). One left out passes everything: every note, every velocity, and chain select 0 alone.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | [`Zone`](#zone) | no | The key zone. |
| `select` | [`Zone`](#zone) | no | The chain select zone. |
| `velocity` | [`Zone`](#zone) | no | The velocity zone. |

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "A chain's zones, each `low`, `high` and the `fade_low` and `fade_high` values its fades span: `key` (0 to 127), `velocity` (1 to 127) and `select` (the chain select zone, 0 to 127). One left out passes everything: every note, every velocity, and chain select 0 alone.",
  "properties": {
    "key": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Zone",
      "description": "The key zone."
    },
    "select": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Zone",
      "description": "The chain select zone."
    },
    "velocity": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Zone",
      "description": "The velocity zone."
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `Change`

How one object differs between two versions.

One of:

- `"added"`: It's only in the newer version.
- `"removed"`: It's only in the older version.
- `"modified"`: It's in both, but different.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How one object differs between two versions.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "added",
      "description": "It's only in the newer version.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "removed",
      "description": "It's only in the older version.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "modified",
      "description": "It's in both, but different.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ChangeSet`

What a command changed: whether the song settings (the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place) changed, whether the track list changed, and which tracks, scenes, clips, and devices were added, removed, or modified, keyed by ID. Every field is empty or false if nothing changed.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | boolean | yes | The song settings changed: the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place. |
| `layout` | boolean | yes | The track tree changed: a track was added, removed, or moved, so routing may have changed. |
| `tracks` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Tracks whose own settings changed: name, mixer, sends, the tracks inside a group, or the order of the device chain. Changes to a track's clips or to its devices' settings are listed under `clips` and `devices` instead. |
| `scenes` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Scenes that were added, removed, renamed, or moved. A scene whose clips changed only is listed under `clips`, not here. |
| `clips` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Clips that changed, including clips moved to another track or between the Arrangement and a Session slot. |
| `devices` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Devices whose settings changed, including devices moved to another track. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What a command changed: whether the song settings (the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place) changed, whether the track list changed, and which tracks, scenes, clips, and devices were added, removed, or modified, keyed by ID. Every field is empty or false if nothing changed.",
  "properties": {
    "clips": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Clips that changed, including clips moved to another track or between the Arrangement and a Session slot.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "devices": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Devices whose settings changed, including devices moved to another track.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "layout": {
      "description": "The track tree changed: a track was added, removed, or moved, so routing may have changed.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "scenes": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Scenes that were added, removed, renamed, or moved. A scene whose clips changed only is listed under `clips`, not here.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "settings": {
      "description": "The song settings changed: the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "tracks": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Tracks whose own settings changed: name, mixer, sends, the tracks inside a group, or the order of the device chain. Changes to a track's clips or to its devices' settings are listed under `clips` and `devices` instead.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "settings",
    "layout",
    "tracks",
    "scenes",
    "clips",
    "devices"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `Channel`

One of the audio interface's channels: `mono` a single channel, or `pair` a stereo pair starting at it, counted from 1 (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is the pair 3/4).

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"mono"`, `channel` (integer from 0 to 65535): A single channel, counted from 1.
- an object with `type` = `"pair"`, `channel` (integer from 0 to 65535): A stereo pair: its first channel, counted from 1; the second is the next one.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "One of the audio interface's channels: `mono` a single channel, or `pair` a stereo pair starting at it, counted from 1 (`{ \"type\": \"pair\", \"channel\": 3 }` is the pair 3/4).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "A single channel, counted from 1.",
      "properties": {
        "channel": {
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "type": {
          "const": "mono",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type",
        "channel"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "A stereo pair: its first channel, counted from 1; the second is the next one.",
      "properties": {
        "channel": {
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "type": {
          "const": "pair",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type",
        "channel"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Clip`

A clip on a track's arrangement lane.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The clip's name, which may be empty. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the clip starts in the arrangement. Never negative. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the clip is. Always positive. |
| `mute` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip is switched off, so it stays in place but doesn't play. |
| `data` | [`ClipData`](#clipdata) | yes | What the clip plays. |
| `envelopes` | array of [`ClipEnvelope`](#clipenvelope) | no | The clip's envelopes (WP-3.15): one per parameter of its track it modulates, in target order. Empty for a clip with none, which is what a set saved before this package holds. |
| `launch` | [`ClipLaunch`](#cliplaunch) | no | The clip's launch settings (WP-3.4), which only a Session clip's launching reads. The defaults for a clip saved without them. |
| `offset` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | no | How far into its contents a MIDI clip starts: its notes are placed from `start - offset`, and the part before the clip's start doesn't play. 0 (or left out) plays the contents from their beginning. Never negative. Splitting a MIDI clip or trimming its left edge changes it, so each part plays what it played before. An audio clip's is always 0: its Start marker moves instead, as Live's does. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A clip on a track's arrangement lane.",
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipData",
      "description": "What the clip plays."
    },
    "envelopes": {
      "description": "The clip's envelopes (WP-3.15): one per parameter of its track it modulates, in target order. Empty for a clip with none, which is what a set saved before this package holds.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipEnvelope"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "id": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipId",
      "description": "The clip's ID."
    },
    "launch": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipLaunch",
      "description": "The clip's launch settings (WP-3.4), which only a Session clip's launching reads. The defaults for a clip saved without them."
    },
    "length": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "How long the clip is. Always positive."
    },
    "mute": {
      "description": "Whether the clip is switched off, so it stays in place but doesn't play.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The clip's name, which may be empty.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "offset": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "How far into its contents a MIDI clip starts: its notes are placed from `start - offset`, and the part before the clip's start doesn't play. 0 (or left out) plays the contents from their beginning. Never negative. Splitting a MIDI clip or trimming its left edge changes it, so each part plays what it played before. An audio clip's is always 0: its Start marker moves instead, as Live's does."
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "Where the clip starts in the arrangement. Never negative."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "name",
    "start",
    "length",
    "mute",
    "data"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ClipEnvelope`

An envelope a clip carries for a parameter of its track: the parameter it modulates, its breakpoints, and whether it follows the clip's timeline (`linked`, the default) or runs once from the clip's start (`false`).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter it modulates: a control of the clip's track's mixer, a send, or a parameter of a device in its chain. |
| `envelope` | [`Envelope`](#envelope) | yes | Its breakpoints, in position order: positions are ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, like a note's start. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Whether an automation envelope drives its parameter: a control moved by hand while the clip plays turns it off until the clip launches again or Re-Enable Automation. Always true for a modulation envelope. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Whether it modulates the parameter or sets it (WP-3.12). A clip can hold one of each kind for a parameter. |
| `linked` | boolean | no | Whether it follows the clip's region and loop (`true`, the Linked switch's default) or plays once from the clip's start (`false`). |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "An envelope a clip carries for a parameter of its track: the parameter it modulates, its breakpoints, and whether it follows the clip's timeline (`linked`, the default) or runs once from the clip's start (`false`).",
  "properties": {
    "enabled": {
      "description": "Whether an automation envelope drives its parameter: a control moved by hand while the clip plays turns it off until the clip launches again or Re-Enable Automation. Always true for a modulation envelope.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "envelope": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Envelope",
      "description": "Its breakpoints, in position order: positions are ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, like a note's start."
    },
    "kind": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EnvelopeKind",
      "description": "Whether it modulates the parameter or sets it (WP-3.12). A clip can hold one of each kind for a parameter."
    },
    "linked": {
      "description": "Whether it follows the clip's region and loop (`true`, the Linked switch's default) or plays once from the clip's start (`false`).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "target": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/AutomationTarget",
      "description": "The parameter it modulates: a control of the clip's track's mixer, a send, or a parameter of a device in its chain."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "target",
    "envelope"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ClipLaunch`

A Session clip's own launch settings (the Clip View's Launch panel, WP-3.4). They are saved with the clip, so they're part of the set and each change is one undo step; a clip without them has the defaults.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `follow` | [`FollowActions`](#followactions) | no | What the clip does by itself after it has played for a while (WP-3.10). |
| `legato` | boolean | no | Legato: the clip takes over the play position of the clip playing on its track when it launches. |
| `mode` | [`LaunchMode`](#launchmode) | no | What a press and a release of the clip's launch button do (WP-3.3). |
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) or null | no | The clip's own launch quantisation; `null` (left out) follows the global one, which Live's chooser calls "Global". |
| `velocity_amount` | number | no | How much the velocity of a note that launches the clip changes its volume, from 0 (none, the default) to 1 (100 %). |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A Session clip's own launch settings (the Clip View's Launch panel, WP-3.4). They are saved with the clip, so they're part of the set and each change is one undo step; a clip without them has the defaults.",
  "properties": {
    "follow": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/FollowActions",
      "description": "What the clip does by itself after it has played for a while (WP-3.10)."
    },
    "legato": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Legato: the clip takes over the play position of the clip playing on its track when it launches.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "mode": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/LaunchMode",
      "default": "trigger",
      "description": "What a press and a release of the clip's launch button do (WP-3.3)."
    },
    "quantization": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LaunchQuantization"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null,
      "description": "The clip's own launch quantisation; `null` (left out) follows the global one, which Live's chooser calls \"Global\"."
    },
    "velocity_amount": {
      "default": 0.0,
      "description": "How much the velocity of a note that launches the clip changes its volume, from 0 (none, the default) to 1 (100 %).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ClipViewState`

What the Clip View shows: which clip it is editing, the notes selected in it, the lane's setting, and the tab with the envelope it shows.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | boolean | yes | Whether the Clip View shows in the detail area. |
| `draw_mode` | boolean | yes | Whether Draw Mode is on (B): clicking the note area adds a note, and clicking a note removes it. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | yes | The clip the note editor shows; `null` when none does. |
| `selected` | array of integer, at least 0 | yes | The selected notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). |
| `lane` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value the lane under the note editor shows and edits. |
| `folded` | boolean | yes | Whether the note editor shows only the rows that hold notes (Fold, F). |
| `tab` | [`ClipTab`](#cliptab) | yes | The tab the Clip View shows. |
| `envelope` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) or null | yes | The parameter whose envelope the Envelopes tab shows; `null` when it shows none. |

```json
  "properties": {
    "clip": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
```

### `Device`

A device in a track's chain: a native instrument or effect, or a plug-in.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on: the device's own name until a preset or Rename gives it another. |
| `kind` | [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) | yes | What the device is. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the device is switched on. A device that's off passes its input through unchanged. |
| `params` | array of pair of [`ParamId`](#paramid) and number | yes | Parameter values the user has set, in the parameter's own units. Every value is finite. Parameters not listed keep their defaults.  They serialise as a list of `[parameter, value]` pairs, since some formats can't key a map by number. |
| `b_active` | boolean | no | Whether the device's B state is the active one, whose values [`params`](Self::params) holds (device compare R1). Left out of the saved set while A is active. |
| `chains` | array of [`Chain`](#chain) | no | A rack's chains, in order (WP-5.1). Empty for every device that isn't a rack, and left out of the saved set then, so sets saved before racks load unchanged. |
| `external` | [`External`](#external) or null | no | The device's routing to external hardware, if its type declares one (WP-5.34): an external instrument's output port and channel, the interface inputs it comes back on, and its Hardware Latency. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |
| `floating` | boolean | no | Whether the device floats in a window of its own rather than showing in the Device View (IMP-14, WP-2.5b), where its place in the chain shows as a strip. Only native devices float. Left out of the saved set while docked. Where its window sits isn't part of the document: moving or resizing a window isn't an undo step ([`WindowFrame`]). |
| `layers` | [`Layers`](#layers) | no | A multisampler's layers and the options of its layer list (WP-5.13, the multisampler spec, R2). Left out of the saved set for a device that holds none. |
| `mappings` | array of [`Mapping`](#mapping) | no | The parameters a modulator maps, one per slot (the modulation spec, R19). Left out of the saved set for a device that maps none. |
| `media` | array of [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The media the device plays, by content hash, one entry per sample slot (WP-2.16, WP-5.17): the sampler's sample is slot 0, the eight-slot drum sampler's slots are 0 to 7. The media store holds each like a clip's audio (the sampler spec, R11). A slot with no sample is `None`, and the list never ends in one. Left out of the saved set for a device that plays none; a set saved before slots existed holds one hash, which loads as slot 0. |
| `midi_sidechain` | [`MidiSidechain`](#midisidechain) or null | no | The device's MIDI sidechain input, if its type declares one (the routing spec, R32): a MIDI track whose notes and channel messages the device hears beside its audio. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |
| `other_params` | array or null | no | The values of the state that isn't active, in the same form as [`params`](Self::params) (device compare R1, R10). `None` while the two states are equal, as a new device's are, and left out of the saved set then. Use [`other_params`](Self::other_params) to read it. |
| `own_name` | string | no | The device's own name, such as `Auto Filter`, which the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is off. Empty while it's the same as [`name`](Self::name), and left out of the saved set then. |
| `plugin` | [`PluginState`](#pluginstate) or null | no | A plug-in's own state and where it was loaded from (WP-2.6), as last saved with the set. Left out of the saved set for a native device, and for a plug-in until the set is first saved with it. |
| `role` | [`DeviceRole`](#devicerole) | no | Where it goes in a chain: MIDI effects, then the instrument, then audio effects. Audio effects aren't marked in the saved set. |
| `sample_edits` | array of [`SampleEdit`](#sampleedit) | no | The edits made to the sample in slot 0 (WP-5.15, IMP-28; the multisampler spec, R55): applied in order to the media, which the file is never written for. A multisampler's layers hold their own. Loading another sample clears them. Left out of the saved set while there are none. |
| `shape` | array or null | no | The breakpoints of a Shaper's shape (R23); `None` plays the default shape. Left out of the saved set while it is the default. |
| `show_preset_name` | boolean | no | Whether the title bar shows the preset's or the given name (on, as a new device is) or the device's own name: the context menu's Show Preset Name. Left out of the saved set while on. |
| `sidechain` | [`Sidechain`](#sidechain) or null | no | The device's sidechain input, if its type declares one (WP-2.19b): where its detector can listen other than its own input. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A device in a track's chain: a native instrument or effect, or a plug-in.",
  "properties": {
    "b_active": {
      "description": "Whether the device's B state is the active one, whose values [`params`](Self::params) holds (device compare R1). Left out of the saved set while A is active.",
```

### `DeviceDescription`

What a kind of device is to the framework: its parameters' descriptors, in the order its generic UI and agents list them, and its layout.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `params` | array of [`ParamDescriptor`](#paramdescriptor) | yes | Its parameters. |
| `layout` | [`DeviceLayout`](#devicelayout) | yes | Where its controls and display cells sit (IMP-14). |
| `menu_options` | array of [`ParamId`](#paramid) | no | The switches the device lists as its own items in its Show Options menu, after Save as Default Preset (C-DEVICE-015), in this order. They are parameters like any other, but the layout places no control for them. |
| `views` | array of string | no | The views its display offers, such as `Transfer Curve`, the first being the one it starts in; empty for a display with one view. Which is shown is view state (`device.set_display_view`). |

### `DeviceFrame`

One device as the Device View shows it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `title` | string | yes | What its title bar reads: its preset's or given name while Show Preset Name is on, otherwise its own name. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its own name, such as `Auto Filter`. |
| `kind` | [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) | yes | What it is. |
| `role` | [`DeviceRole`](#devicerole) | yes | Where it goes in a chain. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it's switched on. |
| `takes_sample` | boolean | yes | Whether its type plays one sample, so a sample dropped on it loads into it (`device.load_sample`, WP-2.16). |
| `swaps_to_snapshot` | boolean | yes | Whether its type is the drum sampler, whose context menu offers the swap to Simpler and Save as Default Pad (`device.swap_to_snapshot`, one-shot drum sampler R23). |
| `show_preset_name` | boolean | yes | Whether its title shows its preset's or given name. |
| `folded` | boolean | yes | Whether it's folded to its title bar. |
| `expandable` | boolean | yes | Whether it has an expanded part, which its title bar's expand toggle shows and hides (L-DEV-004; WP-5.42). |
| `expanded` | boolean | yes | Whether its expanded part is shown. Never while it has none. |
| `floating` | boolean | yes | Whether it floats in a window of its own, its place in the chain a strip (WP-2.5b). |
| `b_active` | boolean | yes | Whether its B state is the active one, which the title bar marks "(B)" (device compare R5). |
| `selected` | boolean | yes | Whether it's the selected device. |
| `hot_swap` | boolean | yes | Whether it's the device being hot-swapped. |
| `sidechain` | [`SidechainSection`](#sidechainsection) or null | yes | Its sidechain section, if it has a sidechain input (WP-2.19b). |
| `display_view` | string or null | no | The view its display shows, if its display has views (WP-5.43): one of its description's `views`. |
| `external` | [`ExternalSection`](#externalsection) or null | no | Its routing to hardware, if it is an external device (WP-5.34). |
| `midi_sidechain` | [`MidiSidechainSection`](#midisidechainsection) or null | no | Its MIDI sidechain section, if it has a MIDI sidechain input (WP-5.27). |
| `modulator` | [`ModulatorFrame`](#modulatorframe) or null | no | For a modulator, what it maps and which Map button is armed (WP-5.10). |
| `multisampler` | [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate) or null | no | A multisampler's views and selected layers (WP-5.13, R30); left out for any other device. |
| `panel` | [`DevicePanel`](#devicepanel) or null | no | Its parameters and layout, for the generic UI; left out for a device whose type doesn't describe them. |
| `rack` | [`RackFrame`](#rackframe) or null | no | A rack's frame: its views, its chain list and the selected chain's devices (WP-5.2). None for a device that isn't a rack. |

```json
}
```

### `DeviceKind`

What a device is.

One of:

- an object with `native` (object with `device_type` (string)): A device built into Beatlayer.
- an object with `plugin` (object with `format` ([`PluginFormat`](#pluginformat)), `plugin_id` (string)): A plug-in.
- an object with `rack` (object with `kind` ([`RackKind`](#rackkind))): A rack (WP-5.1): a device that holds [`Device::chains`].

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What a device is.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A device built into Beatlayer.",
      "properties": {
        "native": {
          "properties": {
            "device_type": {
              "description": "The device type's stable identifier, such as `beatlayer.utility`.",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "device_type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "native"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A plug-in.",
      "properties": {
        "plugin": {
          "properties": {
            "format": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PluginFormat",
              "description": "The plug-in's format."
            },
            "plugin_id": {
              "description": "The plug-in's identifier in its format: a CLAP ID, a VST3 class ID, an Audio Unit's type, subtype, and manufacturer, or an LV2 URI.",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "format",
            "plugin_id"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "plugin"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A rack (WP-5.1): a device that holds [`Device::chains`].",
      "properties": {
        "rack": {
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/RackKind",
              "description": "Which of the four kinds of rack it is."
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "rack"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

| `loaded_slots` | array of boolean | no | For a device with sample slots: whether each slot holds a sample. |
| `slot_keys` | array of string | no | For a device with sample slots: the key each slot plays, as Live names notes (`C3`). |

### `DeviceRole`

Where a device goes in a chain. A chain holds its MIDI effects first, then its instrument, then its audio effects, as Live's does; only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments, and a chain holds at most one instrument (a rack holds several, one to a chain).

One of:

- `"midi_effect"`: Takes MIDI and gives MIDI, before the instrument.
- `"instrument"`: Takes MIDI and makes audio.
- `"audio_effect"`: Takes audio and gives audio, after the instrument.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Where a device goes in a chain. A chain holds its MIDI effects first, then its instrument, then its audio effects, as Live's does; only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments, and a chain holds at most one instrument (a rack holds several, one to a chain).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "midi_effect",
      "description": "Takes MIDI and gives MIDI, before the instrument.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "instrument",
      "description": "Takes MIDI and makes audio.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "audio_effect",
      "description": "Takes audio and gives audio, after the instrument.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `DisplayCell`

A display cell: a graph, a spectrum, a waveform, or an envelope editor, which grows with the room the device has. It may hold a row of controls inside its top edge and another inside its bottom edge (observed in Live 12.4.6: Compressor's display has Thresh, GR, Output, and Out along its top, and its view buttons, Knee, Look., and Env. along its bottom); they keep their size and stay pinned to those edges as the cell grows.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | What it shows, for the device that draws it and for screen readers. |
| `width` | number | yes | Its docked width, the least it has. |
| `height` | number | yes | Its docked height, the least it has. |
| `weight` | number | yes | Its share of extra room, against the other cells it shares with. |
| `bottom` | [`ControlBand`](#controlband) or null | no | Controls inside its bottom edge, from its left. |
| `slot` | integer or null | no | The sample slot the cell stands for, if it does: it shows the slot and takes a click that selects it, and a sample dropped on it (WP-5.17). |
| `top` | [`ControlBand`](#controlband) or null | no | Controls inside its top edge, from its left. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A display cell: a graph, a spectrum, a waveform, or an envelope editor, which grows with the room the device has. It may hold a row of controls inside its top edge and another inside its bottom edge (observed in Live 12.4.6: Compressor's display has Thresh, GR, Output, and Out along its top, and its view buttons, Knee, Look., and Env. along its bottom); they keep their size and stay pinned to those edges as the cell grows.",
  "properties": {
    "bottom": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ControlBand"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Controls inside its bottom edge, from its left."
    },
    "height": {
      "description": "Its docked height, the least it has.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "What it shows, for the device that draws it and for screen readers.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slot": {
      "description": "The sample slot the cell stands for, if it does: it shows the slot and takes a click that selects it, and a sample dropped on it (WP-5.17).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "top": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ControlBand"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Controls inside its top edge, from its left."
    },
    "weight": {
      "description": "Its share of extra room, against the other cells it shares with.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "Its docked width, the least it has.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "width",
    "height",
    "weight"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `Dither`

The noise added before rounding below 32 bits (the export spec, R7).

One of:

- `"none"`: No Dither.
- `"rectangular"`: Rectangular: noise spread evenly over one step.
- `"triangular"`: Triangular: the default, and the safest when the file will be processed further.
- `"noise_shaped"`: Noise Shaped: Beatlayer's own noise-shaped dither, for a final 16- or 24-bit render.

### `ExportResult`

What `export.audio` returns.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The file written (or the base path if multiple files were written). |
| `file_type` | [`FileType`](#filetype) | yes | Its type. |
| `bit_depth` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | Bits per sample. |
| `sample_rate` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Frames per second. |
| `channels` | integer from 0 to 65535 | yes | Channels in each frame (describes the first file in a multi-file export). |
| `frames` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Frames in the file (describes the first file in a multi-file export). |
| `seconds` | number | yes | The file's length in seconds (describes the first file in a multi-file export). |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the range started, in ticks from 1.1.1. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it ended, in ticks: the first position not exported. |
| `range` | [`RangeSource`](#rangesource) | yes | Where the range came from. |
| `dither` | [`Dither`](#dither) | yes | The dither used: `none` at 32 bits. |
| `peak_dbfs` | number or null | yes | The largest sample magnitude written across all rendered files, in dBFS (before rounding), or null for silence. |
| `gain_db` | number | yes | The gain Normalize applied, in dB: 0 without it (describes the first file in a multi-file export). |
| `render_rate` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The rate the engine rendered at (describes the first file in a multi-file export), which is higher than the file's when the file's is below the engine's. |
| `took_seconds` | number | yes | How long the export took, in seconds. |
| `speed` | number | yes | How many times faster than real time it ran. |
| `missing_media` | array of string | yes | Media that clips name and that couldn't be found, by content hash: those clips are silent in the export. |
| `files` | array of string | no | Every file written by the export: one for Main or a single track, or one per track for all-tracks or selected-tracks exports. |
| `silenced_external_devices` | array of string | no | The devices that work with hardware (an external instrument), by the name their title bar shows and their ID: they send nothing to hardware in an offline render and bring back silence. |

| `min_width` | number | yes | The smallest size its contents take at 100%, in points: the device at its docked size under its title bar. |
| `min_height` | number | yes | See `min_width`. |
| `grows_across` | boolean | yes | Whether the window can grow across: only a device with a display cell that grows can. |
| `grows_down` | boolean | yes | Whether the window can grow down. |
| `view` | [`DeviceFrame`](#deviceframe) | yes | The device, as its window draws it. |
| `shown` | boolean | yes | Whether the window shows: always, unless Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows is on (as it is in a new install) and another track is selected, when it hides until its track is selected again. A hidden window's device still floats. |

### `FollowAction`

What a follow action does when its time comes (the Clip View's action list, in its order).

One of:

- `"no_action"`: Nothing: the clip plays on as it was.
- `"stop"`: Stops the clip.
- `"play_again"`: Launches the clip again from its start.
- `"previous"`: Launches the clip before this one in its group.
- `"next"`: Launches the clip after this one in its group.
- `"first"`: Launches the first clip of the group.
- `"last"`: Launches the last clip of the group.
- `"any"`: Launches any clip of the group, this one included.
- `"other"`: Launches any clip of the group but this one.
- `"jump"`: Launches the clip at a slot number the action names.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What a follow action does when its time comes (the Clip View's action list, in its order).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "no_action",
      "description": "Nothing: the clip plays on as it was.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "stop",
      "description": "Stops the clip.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "play_again",
      "description": "Launches the clip again from its start.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "previous",
      "description": "Launches the clip before this one in its group.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "next",
      "description": "Launches the clip after this one in its group.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "first",
      "description": "Launches the first clip of the group.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "last",
      "description": "Launches the last clip of the group.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "any",
      "description": "Launches any clip of the group, this one included.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "other",
      "description": "Launches any clip of the group but this one.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "jump",
      "description": "Launches the clip at a slot number the action names.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `FollowActions`

A clip's or a scene's follow actions: the Follow Action switch, actions A and B with the chance that splits them, and the follow time.

On a scene, `linked` is the Longest button: the time is the multiplier times the longest clip of the scene.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_a` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) | no | Action A, which runs with the chance `chance_a`. Next by default. |
| `action_b` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) | no | Action B, which runs the rest of the time. No Action by default. |
| `chance_a` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | The chance of action A in whole percent, 0 to 100. Action B has the rest, so the two always add up to 100. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | The Follow Action switch. Off, nothing runs; off is the default. |
| `jump_a` | integer, at least 0 | no | The slot (scene) number action A's Jump goes to, counted from 1; 0 leaves it empty, and a jump to an empty target stops the clip. |
| `jump_b` | integer, at least 0 | no | The slot (scene) number action B's Jump goes to, as `jump_a`. |
| `linked` | boolean | no | Linked: the follow time is a multiple of the clip's length (the multiplier counts loops, and a clip whose Loop switch is off follows at its end). Unlinked: `time`. On by default. |
| `multiplier` | integer, at least 0 | no | The Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1. |
| `time` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | no | The Unlinked follow time in ticks (bars.beats.sixteenths), from a sixteenth; one 4/4 bar by default. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A clip's or a scene's follow actions: the Follow Action switch, actions A and B with the chance that splits them, and the follow time.\n\nOn a scene, `linked` is the Longest button: the time is the multiplier times the longest clip of the scene.",
  "properties": {
    "action_a": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/FollowAction",
      "default": "next",
      "description": "Action A, which runs with the chance `chance_a`. Next by default."
    },
    "action_b": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/FollowAction",
      "default": "next",
      "description": "Action B, which runs the rest of the time. No Action by default."
    },
    "chance_a": {
      "default": 100,
      "description": "The chance of action A in whole percent, 0 to 100. Action B has the rest, so the two always add up to 100.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "enabled": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "The Follow Action switch. Off, nothing runs; off is the default.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "jump_a": {
      "default": 1,
      "description": "The slot (scene) number action A's Jump goes to, counted from 1; 0 leaves it empty, and a jump to an empty target stops the clip.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "jump_b": {
      "default": 1,
      "description": "The slot (scene) number action B's Jump goes to, as `jump_a`.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "linked": {
      "description": "Linked: the follow time is a multiple of the clip's length (the multiplier counts loops, and a clip whose Loop switch is off follows at its end). Unlinked: `time`. On by default.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "multiplier": {
      "default": 1,
      "description": "The Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "time": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "default": 2822400,
      "description": "The Unlinked follow time in ticks (bars.beats.sixteenths), from a sixteenth; one 4/4 bar by default."
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `HardwareLatency`

Hardware Latency: `{ "unit": "milliseconds", "value": 12.5 }` (0 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ "unit": "samples", "value": 600 }` (0 to 192000; kept in samples).

One of:

- an object with `unit` = `"milliseconds"`, `value` (number): Milliseconds, 0 to 1000: for analogue connections.
- an object with `unit` = `"samples"`, `value` (integer, at least 0): Samples, 0 to 192,000: for digital connections.

```json
  "description": "Hardware Latency: `{ \"unit\": \"milliseconds\", \"value\": 12.5 }` (0 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ \"unit\": \"samples\", \"value\": 600 }` (0 to 192000; kept in samples).",

      "description": "Milliseconds, 0 to 1000: for analogue connections.",

          "const": "milliseconds",
          "type": "string"

          "type": "number"
        }
      },

        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "Samples, 0 to 192,000: for digital connections.",

        "unit": {
          "const": "samples",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The delay.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "unit",
        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
```
```json
}
```

</details>

### `Input`

Where a track takes its input from. Audio tracks: `external` (Ext. In, the audio interface's inputs, with its `channel`; a new audio track's), `resampling` (the Main output), `track` (another audio track, a MIDI track with an instrument, a return, or Main, tapped at `tap`; with a `chain` of an instrument or audio effect rack on that track, that chain's signal at `tap`), or `none` (No Input). MIDI tracks: `all_ins` (every MIDI input; a new MIDI track's), `computer_keyboard`, `port` (one MIDI input, by its name as the MIDI settings list it), `track` (another MIDI track), or `none`.

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"none"`: No Input.
- an object with `type` = `"external"`, `channel` ([`Channel`](#channel)): Ext. In: the audio interface's inputs, one channel or a stereo pair. Audio tracks only.
- an object with `type` = `"all_ins"`: All Ins: every MIDI input port whose Track switch is on, and the computer MIDI keyboard. MIDI tracks only.
- an object with `type` = `"computer_keyboard"`: The computer MIDI keyboard. MIDI tracks only.
- an object with `type` = `"port"`, `name` (string): One MIDI input port, by the name the MIDI system gives it. MIDI tracks only. The track keeps the name while the port is away and receives again when a port of that name returns.
- an object with `type` = `"resampling"`: Resampling: the Main output. Audio tracks only.
- an object with `type` = `"track"`, `track` ([`TrackId`](#trackid)), `chain` ([`ChainId`](#chainid) or null), `tap` ([`Tap`](#tap)): Another track's signal.

MIDI tracks: `all_ins` (every MIDI input; a new MIDI track's), `computer_keyboard`, `port` (one MIDI input, by its name as the MIDI settings list it), `track` (another MIDI track), or `none`.",

```json
          "type": "string"
        }
```

### `ItemKind`

One of:

### `JobState`

Where a download or a separation is.

One of:

- `"idle"`: Nothing is under way.

- `"failed"`: It failed: see `error`.
- `"cancelled"`: It was cancelled.

### `LaunchMode`

How a Session clip's launch button behaves (the clip's Launch Mode, and the Default Launch Mode setting).

One of:

- `"trigger"`: Pressing starts the clip; releasing does nothing. The observed default.
- `"gate"`: The clip plays while the button is held.
- `"toggle"`: Pressing starts the clip and the next press stops it.
- `"repeat"`: The clip retriggers while the button is held.

### `LaunchQuantization`

One step of the launch quantisation grid: how long a slot waits after a launch or a stop is asked for.

One of:

- `"none"`: No quantisation: a launch or a stop takes effect at once (the menu's "None", S-GQ-005).
- `"8_bars"`: Eight bars.
- `"4_bars"`: Four bars.
- `"2_bars"`: Two bars.
- `"1_bar"`: One bar, the observed default.
- `"half"`: A half note.
- `"half_triplet"`: A half-note triplet.
- `"quarter"`: A quarter note.
- `"quarter_triplet"`: A quarter-note triplet.
- `"eighth"`: An eighth note.
- `"eighth_triplet"`: An eighth-note triplet.
- `"sixteenth"`: A sixteenth note.
- `"sixteenth_triplet"`: A sixteenth-note triplet.
- `"thirty_second"`: A thirty-second note.

### `Layer`

One sample of a multisample (R2).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer's ID, unique within its device. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name: the file's name until renamed. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | Its sample, which the media store holds. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The sample's length in frames at its own rate, after its edits. |
| `sample_rate` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The sample's own rate, in hertz: the unit its markers count in. |
| `channels` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | How many channels the sample has. |
| `key` | [`Zone`](#zone) | yes | The notes it plays over. |
| `velocity` | [`Zone`](#zone) | yes | The velocities it plays at. |
| `select` | [`Zone`](#zone) | yes | The Sample Selector values it plays at. |
| `root_key` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The key that plays the sample at its own pitch, 0 to 127 (R15). |
| `volume` | number | yes | Its level as a linear gain from 0 (−∞ dB) to +24 dB (rule G1). |
| `start` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Sample Start, in frames of the sample (R16). |
| `end` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Sample End, in frames of the sample. |
| `loop_start` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Loop Start, in frames. |
| `loop_end` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Loop End, in frames. |
| `release_loop` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where the release loop begins, between Loop End and Sample End. |
| `crossfade_ms` | number | no | The loop's crossfade in milliseconds (R19). |
| `detune` | number | no | Its tuning, in cents from −50 to 50. |
| `edits` | array of [`SampleEdit`](#sampleedit) | no | The sample's edits, applied in order to the media (WP-5.15, R55). The markers, [`length`](Self::length) and the sample the engine plays are the edited sample's; the source file is never written. |
| `link` | boolean | no | Link: the voice starts at Loop Start instead of Sample Start. The Sample Start it keeps comes back when Link goes off. |
| `loop_detune` | number | no | How the voice is retuned inside a loop, in cents (R19). |
| `one_shot` | boolean | no | Whether the layer's voices play on to Sample End whatever the note does (R50's `one_shot`). No control in the Sample tab sets it: an SFZ import does, and `device.update_layers`. |
| `pan` | number | no | Its place in the stereo field, −50 to 50. |
| `release` | [`ReleaseMode`](#releasemode) | no | What the note's end does inside a sustain loop (R18). |
| `sustain` | [`SustainMode`](#sustainmode) | no | The sustain loop's kind (R17). |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "One sample of a multisample (R2).",
  "properties": {
    "channels": {
      "description": "How many channels the sample has.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "crossfade_ms": {
      "description": "The loop's crossfade in milliseconds (R19).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "detune": {
```

### `LayerSelectMode`

How `device.select_layers` changes the selection.

One of:

- `"replace"`: The listed layers become the selection (a click).
- `"add"`: They join it (Shift-click).
- `"toggle"`: Each leaves the selection if it's in it and joins it if not (Cmd-click).
- `"same_range"`: The selection becomes every layer whose range in the editor in view equals the first listed layer's (Select All With Same Range).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How `device.select_layers` changes the selection.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "replace",
      "description": "The listed layers become the selection (a click).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "add",
      "description": "They join it (Shift-click).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "Each leaves the selection if it's in it and joins it if not (Cmd-click).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "same_range",
      "description": "The selection becomes every layer whose range in the editor in view equals the first listed layer's (Select All With Same Range).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `LayerSort`

How the layer list is sorted (R11).

One of:

- `"name"`: Alphabetically by name, ignoring case.
- `"key"`: By the key zone's lowest key.
- `"velocity"`: By the velocity zone's lowest velocity.
- `"selector"`: By the sample select zone's lowest value.

### `LoopWarpShortSamples`

Loop/Warp Short Samples (Record, Warp & Launch, Warp/Fades, L-SET-018): what a new clip of a short sample gets (the warping spec, R29 and R32).

One of:

- `"unwarped_one_shot"`: Warp and the loop off.
- `"warped_one_shot"`: Warped, the loop off.
- `"warped_loop"`: Warped, the loop on over the whole file.
- `"auto"`: A loop when its analysis finds a steady beat that fits whole bars, a one-shot otherwise. What a new install has.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "Loop/Warp Short Samples (Record, Warp & Launch, Warp/Fades, L-SET-018): what a new clip of a short sample gets (the warping spec, R29 and R32).",

      "const": "unwarped_one_shot",
      "description": "Warp and the loop off.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "warped_one_shot",
      "description": "Warped, the loop off.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "warped_loop",
      "description": "Warped, the loop on over the whole file.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "auto",
      "description": "A loop when its analysis finds a steady beat that fits whole bars, a one-shot otherwise. What a new install has.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `MidiData`

A MIDI clip's data: its notes, Start and End markers, and loop brace.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notes` | array of [`Note`](#note) | yes | The notes, in no particular order. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The End marker: where a clip whose loop is off stops playing, after the Start marker; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip. |
| `loop_end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where the loop brace ends, in ticks, after its start; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip. While the loop is on, the Start marker must be before it. |
| `loop_start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | no | Where the loop brace starts, in ticks: 0 or more; 0 unless given. |
| `looping` | boolean | no | The Loop switch: whether the clip repeats its loop brace. Off unless given. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) or null | no | The clip's time signature, the Clip View's Signature fields. `null` (or nothing) means the song's signature at the clip's position. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | no | The Start marker: where in its contents the clip starts playing. 0 unless given. |

```json
  "description": "A MIDI clip's data: its notes, Start and End markers, and loop brace.",

    "end": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The End marker: where a clip whose loop is off stops playing, after the Start marker; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip."
    },
    "loop_end": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Where the loop brace ends, in ticks, after its start; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip. While the loop is on, the Start marker must be before it."
    },
    "loop_start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "Where the loop brace starts, in ticks: 0 or more; 0 unless given."
    },
    "looping": {
      "description": "The Loop switch: whether the clip repeats its loop brace. Off unless given.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "notes": {
      "description": "The notes, in no particular order.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/Note"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "signature": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/TimeSignature"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The clip's time signature, the Clip View's Signature fields. `null` (or nothing) means the song's signature at the clip's position."
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "The Start marker: where in its contents the clip starts playing. 0 unless given."
    }
  },
  "required": [

  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `Note`

A note in a MIDI clip.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | integer from 0 to 127 | yes | The MIDI key, from 0 to 127. Middle C (C3 in Live) is 60. |
| `velocity` | integer from 1 to 127 | yes | The velocity, from 1 to 127. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the note starts, counted from the beginning of the clip's contents: the clip's start less its offset. Never negative. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the note lasts. Always positive. |
| `mute` | boolean | no | Whether the note is switched off, so it stays in place but doesn't play. |
| `pressure` | array of [`PressurePoint`](#pressurepoint) | no | The note's own pressure, played as polyphonic pressure over its length: points in order of `at`, none at the same place. A note with none plays no pressure. |
| `probability` | number from 0 to 1 | no | The chance the note will play, from 0 to 1: 1 (100 %) unless given. |
| `release_velocity` | integer from 1 to 127 | no | The release velocity, from 1 to 127; 64 unless given. |
| `velocity_deviation` | integer from -127 to 127 | no | How far velocity may deviate randomly, from -127 to +127: 0 unless given. |

```json
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",

        "$ref": "#/$defs/PressurePoint"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "probability": {
      "description": "The chance the note will play, from 0 to 1: 1 (100 %) unless given.",
      "format": "double",
      "maximum": 1.0,
      "minimum": 0.0,
      "type": "number"
    },
    "release_velocity": {
      "description": "The release velocity, from 1 to 127; 64 unless given.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 127,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",

    },

      "description": "The velocity, from 1 to 127.",

      "maximum": 127,
      "minimum": 1,
```

### `Output`

Where a track's audio goes: `default` (Main, or the group the track is in), `main` (Main, even from inside a group), `track` (another audio track's input, or the group the track is in), `sends_only` (only through its sends), or `external` (Ext. Out, the audio interface's outputs, with its `channel`: a single channel or a stereo pair, the first pair by default).

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"default"`: Main, or the group the track is in: where a new track's audio goes.
- an object with `type` = `"main"`: Main, even from a track inside a group.
- an object with `type` = `"external"`, `channel` ([`Channel`](#channel)): Ext. Out: the audio interface's outputs. The track plays on those device channels and not into Main (WP-2.13).
- an object with `type` = `"sends_only"`: Nowhere but the track's sends.
- an object with `type` = `"track"`, `track` ([`TrackId`](#trackid)): Another track: an audio track's input (Track In), or the group the track is in.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Where a track's audio goes: `default` (Main, or the group the track is in), `main` (Main, even from inside a group), `track` (another audio track's input, or the group the track is in), `sends_only` (only through its sends), or `external` (Ext. Out, the audio interface's outputs, with its `channel`: a single channel or a stereo pair, the first pair by default).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "Main, or the group the track is in: where a new track's audio goes.",
      "properties": {
        "type": {
          "const": "default",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "Main, even from a track inside a group.",
      "properties": {
        "type": {
          "const": "main",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "Ext. Out: the audio interface's outputs. The track plays on those device channels and not into Main (WP-2.13).",
      "properties": {
        "channel": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Channel",
          "description": "Which of the interface's outputs, counted from 1: a single channel or a stereo pair. The first pair (1/2) by default."
        },
        "type": {
          "const": "external",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {

        }
      },
```
